Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. link_exists \"$VETH_PEER\" && incus_device_owns_peer; then\n    info \"2/4 $VETH_HOST is up and $VETH_PEER is owned by $CONTAINER; skipping veth recreation\"\n    ip link set \"$VETH_HOST\" up\nelse\n    info \"2/4 op-ovsbr0-uplink (ATTACH_XDP=0 since steering moved to OpenFlow table 1)\"\n    BRIDGE=\"$BR\" UPLINK=\"$UPLINK\" \\\n        VETH_HOST=\"$VETH_HOST\" VETH_PEER=\"$VETH_PEER\" \\\n        ATTACH_XDP=0 \\\n        \"$OP_OVSBR0_UPLINK\"\nfi\n\ninfo \"3/4 sudo incus device attach\"\nif command -v sudo incus >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    # Remove default Incus eth0 to avoid 2 interfaces and wrong default route for internet\n    sudo incus config device remove \"$CONTAINER\" eth0 2>/dev/null || true\n    if ! sudo incus config device show \"$CONTAINER\" 2>/dev/null | grep -q \"^${INCUS_DEV}:\"; then\n        sudo incus config device add \"$CONTAINER\" \"$INCUS_DEV\" nic \\\n            nictype=physical parent=\"$VETH_PEER\" name=\"$INCUS_DEV\"\n        info \"added $INCUS_DEV to $CONTAINER (only interface)\"\n    fi\n    # Bind-mount host /etc/xray for live edits (Xray + OpenFlow steering config)\n    if ! sudo incus config device show \"$CONTAINER\" 2>/dev/null | grep -q \"^xray-config:\"; then\n        sudo incus config device add \"$CONTAINER\" xray-config disk source=/etc/xray path=/etc/xray\n        info \"bind-mounted host /etc/xray into $CONTAINER for live edits\"\n    fi\n    # Bind-mount OVS run dir for unix socket access from container (gRPC bridge + OpenFlow controller)\n    if ! sudo incus config device show \"$CONTAINER\" 2>/dev/null | grep -q \"^ovs-run:\"; then\n        sudo incus config device add \"$CONTAINER\" ovs-run disk source=/var/run/openvswitch path=/var/run/openvswitch\n        info \"bind-mounted host /var/run/openvswitch into $CONTAINER for OVSDB/unix socket\"\n    fi\n    state=$(incus info \"$CONTAINER\" 2>/dev/null | awk -F': *' '/^Status/ {print $2; exit}')\n    if [ \"${state:-}\" != \"RUNNING\" ]; then\n        sudo incus start \"$CONTAINER\"\n        sleep 2\n    fi\n    # Route the rDNS-owned public identity directly to The Sled's container\n    # veth path. Do not attach another XDP program over OVS AF_XDP on eth0.\n    resolved_public_ip=\"$(getent ahostsv4 \"$CONTAINER_PUBLIC_HOSTNAME\" | awk '{print $1; exit}')\"\n    if [ -n \"${resolved_public_ip:-}\" ]; then\n        CONTAINER_PUBLIC_IP=\"$resolved_public_ip\"\n    fi\n    ip route replace \"$CONTAINER_PUBLIC_IP/32\" dev \"$VETH_HOST\"\n    sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 >/dev/null\n    sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.proxy_arp=1 >/dev/null\n    sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.\"$BR\".proxy_arp=1 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n    ip neigh replace proxy \"$CONTAINER_PUBLIC_IP\" dev \"$BR\"\nelse\n    info \"incus not installed — skipping device attach\"\nfi\n\ninfo \"4/4 op-xdp-ct-setup\"\nif command -v sudo incus >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -x \"$OP_XDP_CT_SETUP\" ]; then\n    CT_PID=$(incus info \"$CONTAINER\" | awk -F': *' '/PID/ {print $2; exit}')\n    if [ -n \"${CT_PID:-}\" ] && [ \"$CT_PID\" != \"0\" ]; then\n        CT_IF=\"$INCUS_DEV\" \"$OP_XDP_CT_SETUP\" \"$CT_PID\"\n    else\n        info \"could not resolve PID for $CONTAINER\"\n    fi\nfi\n\ninfo \"done.\"\n"}}

The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. ovsdb: &OvsdbClient,\n    bridge: &str,\n    port: &str,\n    port_type: Option<&str>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let existing_ports = ovsdb\n        .list_bridge_ports(bridge)\n        .await\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"list_bridge_ports {}\", bridge))?;\n    if existing_ports.iter().any(|p| p == port) {\n        tracing::info!(%port, %bridge, \"port already present on bridge\");\n {}\", port, port_type))?;\n        }\n    } else {\n        ovsdb\n            .add_port_with_type(bridge, port, port_type)\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"add_port {} -> rtn::create_veth_pair(host, peer)\n        .await\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"create_veth_pair {}<->{}\", host, peer))?;\n    rtn::link_up(host)\n        .await\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"link up {}\", host))?;\n    tracing::info!(%host, %peer, \"veth pair ready\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[tokio::main(flavor = \"current_thread\")]\nasync fn main() -> Result<()> {\n    tracing_subscriber::fmt()\n        .with_env_filter(\n            tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter::try_from_default_env()\n                .unwrap_or_else(|_| tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter::new(\"info\")),\n        )\n        .init();\n\n    let bridge = env_or(\"BRIDGE\", \"ovsbr0\");\n    let uplink = env_or(\"UPLINK\", \"ens3\");\n    let uplink_ovs_type env_or(\"OF_VETH_HOST\", \"of-uplink0\");\n    let of_veth_peer = env_or(\"OF_VETH_PEER\", \"of-phys\");\n    let enable_of_veth = env_or(\"ENABLE_OF_VETH\", \"1\") != \"0\";\n    let xdp_obj = PathBuf::from(env_or(\"XDP_OBJ\", \"/usr/local/lib/op-xdp/xdp_steering.o\"));\n    let xdp_sec = env_or(\"XDP_SEC\", \"xdp\");\n    let xdp_mode = XdpMode::parse(&env_or(\"XDP_MODE\", \"generic\"))?;\n    let attach_xdp = env_or(\"ATTACH_XDP\", \"1\") != \"0\";\n\n    tracing::info!(\n        %bridge, %uplink, %data_veth_host, %data_veth_peer, %of_veth_host, %of_veth_peer,\n        xdp_obj = %xdp_obj.display(),\n        %xdp_sec, ?xdp_mode, attach_xdp, enable_of_veth, %uplink_ovs_type,\n        \"op-ovsbr0-uplink starting\"\n    );\n\n    let ovsdb = OvsdbClient::new();\n    ovsdb\n        .ensure_initialized()\n        .await\n        .context(\"OVSDB not reachable\")?;\n\n    // 1) Bridge must already exist (op-ovsbr0-setup runs first).\n    if !ovsdb\n        .bridge_exists(&bridge)\n        .await\n        .context(\"bridge_exists query\")?\n    {\n        anyhow::bail!(\n            \"bridge {} not present in OVSDB — run op-ovsbr0-setup first\",\n            bridge\n        );\n    }\n    tracing::info!(%bridge, \"bridge present\");\n\n    // 2) Prepare uplink: flush v4 + link up. Errors on flush are tolerated\n    //    (interface may already have nothing to flush).\n    let _ = rtn::flush_addresses(&uplink).await;\n    let _ = rtn::flush_default_routes_v4(&uplink).await;\n    rtn::link_up(&uplink)\n        .await\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"link up {}\", uplink))?;\n    tracing::info!(%uplink, \"uplink flushed and up\");\n\n    // 3) Attach uplink to bridge. AF_XDP mode is an OVSDB Interface type/options\n    //    choice; it is separate from the libbpf XDP program attached below.\n    let uplink_type = if uplink_ovs_type == \"afxdp\" {\n        Some(\"afxdp\")\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n    ensure_bridge_port_with_type(&ovsdb, &bridge, &uplink, uplink_type).await?;\n    if uplink_ovs_type == \"afxdp\" {\n        ovsdb\n            .set_interface_options(\n                &uplink,\n                &[\n                    (\"xdp-mode\", af_xdp_mode.as_str()),\n                    (\"n_rxq\", af_xdp_rxq.as_str()),\n                ],\n            )\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"set AF_XDP options on {}\", uplink))?;\n        tracing::info!(%uplink, xdp_mode = %af_xdp_mode, n_rxq = %af_xdp_rxq, \"AF_XDP uplink options applied\");\n    } else if uplink_ovs_type != \"system\" {\n        tracing::warn!(%uplink_ovs_type, \"unknown UPLINK_OVS_TYPE, using normal system port\");\n    }\n\n    // 4) Data veth pair: The Sled/Shuttle gRPC data path.\n    ensure_host_veth(&data_veth_host, &data_veth_peer).await?;\n\n    // 5) OpenFlow veth pair: control plane stays distinct from data traffic.\n    if enable_of_veth {\n        ensure_host_veth(&of_veth_host, &of_veth_peer).await?;\n    }\n\n    // 6) Attach host-side veths to bridge.\n    ensure_bridge_port(&ovsdb, &bridge, &data_veth_host).await?;\n    if enable_of_veth {\n        ensure_bridge_port(&ovsdb, &bridge, &of_veth_host).await?;\n    }\n\n    // 7) XDP attach on UPLINK and DATA_VETH_HOST. .context(\"pid must be a number\")?;\n\n    let ct_if = std::env::var(\"CT_IF\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \"eth0\".into());\n    let mac = std::env::var(\"HOST_MAC\").unwrap_or_else(|_| .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"32\".into())\n        .parse()\n        .unwrap_or(32);\n    let ipv4_gw = std::env::var(\"IPV4_GW\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \"148.113.204.1\".into());\n    let grpc_addr = std::env::var(\"GRPC_ADDR\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \"10.200.0.1\".into());\n    let grpc_prefix: u8 = std::env::var(\"GRPC_PREFIX\")\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"30\".into())\n        .parse()\n        .unwrap_or(30);\n    let of_if = std::env::var(\"OF_IF\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \"of-phys\".into());\n    let of_addr = std::env::var(\"OF_ADDR\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \"10.210.0.1\".into());\n    let of_prefix: u8 = std::env::var(\"OF_PREFIX\")\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"30\".into())\n        .parse()\n        .unwrap_or(30);\n\n    println!(\"op-xdp-ct-setup: entering netns pid={}\", pid);\n\n    with_netns_pid(pid, move || {\n        let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()\n            .enable_all()\n            .build()?;\n\n        rt.block_on(async {\n            // MAC — interface must be down to change MAC\n            rtnetlink::link_down(&ct_if).await.ok();\n            rtnetlink::set_mac_address(&ct_if, &mac)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"set MAC {} on {}\", mac, ct_if))?;\n            rtnetlink::link_up(&ct_if)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"link up {}\", ct_if))?;\n            println!(\"  MAC {} set on {}\", mac, ct_if);\n\n            // IPv4 public address\n            rtnetlink::add_ipv4_address(&ct_if, &ct_ipv4, ipv4_prefix)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"add {}/{} to {}\", ct_ipv4, ipv4_prefix, ct_if))?;\n            println!(\"  {}/{} added to {}\", ct_ipv4, ipv4_prefix, ct_if);\n\n            // IPv4 link route (gateway reachable on-link)\n            let gw_v4: Ipv4Addr = ipv4_gw.parse()?;\n            rtnetlink::add_link_route_v4(&ct_if, gw_v4, 32)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"add link route {} on {}\", ipv4_gw, ct_if))?;\n            println!(\"  {} scope link on {}\", ipv4_gw, ct_if);\n\n            // IPv4 default route\n            rtnetlink::add_default_route_v4(&ct_if, &ipv4_gw, 100)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"add default v4 via {}\", ipv4_gw))?;\n            println!(\"  default v4 via {}\", ipv4_gw);\n\n            // gRPC IPv4 alias\n            rtnetlink::add_ipv4_address(&ct_if, &grpc_addr, grpc_prefix)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"add {}/{} to {}\", grpc_addr, grpc_prefix, ct_if))?;\n            println!(\"  {}/{} added to {}\", grpc_addr, grpc_prefix, ct_if);\n\n            if !of_if.is_empty() && rtnetlink::link_exists(&of_if).await? {\n                rtnetlink::link_up(&of_if)\n                    .await\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"link up {}\", of_if))?;\n                rtnetlink::add_ipv4_address(&of_if, &of_addr, of_prefix)\n                    .await\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"add {}/{} to {}\", of_addr, of_prefix, of_if))?;\n                println!(\"  {}/{} added to {}\", of_addr, of_prefix, of_if);\n            } else if !of_if.is_empty() {\n                println!(\"  OpenFlow interface {} not present, skipping\", of_if);\n            }\n\n            println!(\"op-xdp-ct-setup: done\");\n            Ok(())\n        })\n    })\n    .await\n}\n"}}

conn.send_flow(&delete_all)\n        .await\n        .context(\"delete all flows\")?;\n    info!(\"cleared existing flows\");\n\n    // Install each intent flow.\n    let mut installed = 0u32;\n    for intent in &intent_flows {\n        match build_flow_from_intent(intent, &port_map) {\n            Ok(flow) => match conn.send_flow_sync(&flow).await {\n                Ok(()) => {\n                      e\n                    );\n                }\n            },\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\"skipping flow: {:#}\", e);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    info!(installed, \"flows installed; entering keepalive loop\");\n\n    // Keepalive loop.\n    loop {\n        let _ = conn.recv_message().await?;\n    }\n}\n\n/// Build a `rovs_openflow::Flow` from an `IntentFlow`, resolving port names.\nfn build_flow_from_intent(\n    intent: &IntentFlow,\n    port_map: &std::collections::HashMap<String, u32>,\n) -> Result<rovs_openflow::Flow> {\n    let mut m = Match::new();\n\n    if let Some(ref name) = intent.in_port {\n        let port = port_map\n            .get(name)\n            .ok_or_else(|| .get(name)\n                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"out_port '{}' not found\", name))?;\n            actions = actions.output(OutputPort::Port(*port));\n        }\n    }\n    if actions.controller(max_len);\n        }\n    }\n    // action_drop = empty actions = implicit drop.\n\n    let mut f = rovs_openflow::Flow::add()\n        .match_fields(m)\n        .actions(actions)\n        .priority(intent.priority)\n        .cookie(intent.cookie)\n        .table(intent.table_id);\n\n    if intent.idle_timeout > 0 {\n        f = f.idle_timeout(intent.idle_timeout);\n    }\n    if intent.hard_timeout > 0 {\n        f = f.hard_timeout(intent.hard_timeout);\n    }\n\n    Ok(f)\n}\n"}}

pub name: String,\n    pub index: u32,\n    pub mac_address: Option<String>,\n    pub mtu: Option<u32>,\n    pub flags: Vec<String>,\n    pub state: String,\n    pub kind: Option<String>,\n    pub u8,\n    pub family: String,\n}\n\n/// List all network interfaces with their details\npub async fn list_interfaces() -> Result<Vec<NetworkInterface>> {\n    let (connection, handle, _) = new_connection()?;\n    tokio::spawn(connection);\n\n    let mut interfaces = Vec::new();\n    let mut links = handle.link().get().execute();\n\n    while let Some(link) = links.try_next().await? {\n        let index = link.header.index;\n        let mut name = String::new();\n        let mut mac_address = None;\n        let mut mtu = None;\n        let mut kind = None;\n\n        // Extract attributes\n        for attr in &link.attributes {\n            match attr {\n                LinkAttribute::IfName(n) => name = n.clone(),\n                LinkAttribute::Address(addr) => {\n                    mac_address = Some(\n                        addr.iter()\n                            .map(|b| format!(\"{:02x}\", b))\n                            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                            .join(\":\"),\n                    );\n                }\n                LinkAttribute::Mtu(m) => mtu = Some(*m),\n                LinkAttribute::LinkInfo(infos) => {\n                    for info in infos {\n                        if let netlink_packet_route::link::LinkInfo::Kind(k) = info {\n                            kind = Some(format!(\"{:?}\", k));\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                _ => {}\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Determine state from flags\n        let flags_val = &link.header.flags;\n        let flags: Vec<String> = flags_val.iter().map(|f| format!(\"{:?}\", f)).collect();\n        let is_up = flags_val\n            .iter()\n            .any(|f| matches!(f, netlink_packet_route::link::LinkFlag::Up));\n        let state = if is_up {\n            \"up\".to_string()\n        } else {\n            \"down\".to_string()\n        };\n\n        // Get addresses for this interface\n        let addresses = match get_interface_addresses(&handle, index).await {\n            Ok(addrs) => addrs,\n            Err(e) => {\n                log::warn!(\"Failed to get addresses for interface {}: {}\", name, e);\n                Vec::new()\n            }\n        };\n\n        interfaces.push(NetworkInterface {\n            name,\n            index,\n            mac_address,\n            mtu,\n            flags,\n            state,\n            kind,\n            addresses,\n        });\n    }\n\n    Ok(interfaces)\n}\n\n/// Get addresses for a specific interface\nasync fn get_interface_addresses(\n    handle: &rtnetlink::Handle,\n    ifindex: u32,\n) -> Result<Vec<InterfaceAddress>> {\n    let mut addresses = Vec::new();\n    let mut addr_stream = handle\n        .address()\n        .get()\n        .set_link_index_filter(ifindex)\n        .execute();\n\n    while let Some(addr_msg) = addr_stream.try_next().await? {\n        let family = match addr_msg.header.family {\n            netlink_packet_route::AddressFamily::Inet => \"inet\".to_string(),\n            netlink_packet_route::AddressFamily::Inet6 => \"inet6\".to_string(),\n            f => format!(\"{:?}\", f),\n        };\n\n        for attr in &addr_msg.attributes {\n            if let AddressAttribute::Address(addr) = attr {\n                let addr_str = addr.to_string();\n\n                addresses.push(InterfaceAddress {\n                    address: addr_str,\n                    prefix_len: addr_msg.header.prefix_len,\n                    family: family.clone(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(addresses)\n}\n\n/// Get default route information\npub async fn get_default_route() -> Result<Option<simd_json::OwnedValue>> {\n    use netlink_packet_route::route::RouteAttribute;\n\n    let (connection, handle, _) = new_connection()?;\n    tokio::spawn(connection);\n\n    let mut routes = handle.route().get(IpVersion::V4).execute();\n\n    while let Some(route) = routes.try_next().await? {\n        // Check if this is a default route (destination 0.0.0.0/0)\n        if route.header.destination_prefix_length == 0 {\n            let mut gateway = None;\n            let mut oif_index = None;\n\n            for attr in &route.attributes {\n                match attr {\n                    RouteAttribute::Gateway(gw) => {\n                        gateway = Some(format!(\"{:?}\", gw));\n                    }\n                    RouteAttribute::Oif(idx) => {\n                        oif_index = Some(idx);\n                    }\n                    _ => {}\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Try to get interface name for the output interface\n            let mut oif_name = None;\n            if let Some(idx) = oif_index {\n                let mut links = handle.link().get().match_index(*idx).execute();\n                if let Some(link) = links.try_next().await? {\n                    for attr in &link.attributes {\n                        if let LinkAttribute::IfName(name) = attr {\n                            oif_name = Some(name.clone());\n                            break;\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            return Ok(Some(simd_json::json!({\n                \"gateway\": gateway,\n                \"interface_index\": oif_index,\n                \"interface_name\": oif_name,\n                \"destination\": \"0.0.0.0/0\",\n            })));\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(None)\n}\n\n/// Add IPv4 address to interface\npub async fn add_ipv4_address(ifname: &str, ip: &str, prefix: u8) -> Result<()> {\n    let (connection, handle, _) = new_connection()?;\n    tokio::spawn(connection);\n\n    // Find interface by name\n    let mut links = handle.link().get().match_name(ifname.to_string()).execute();\n    let link = links\n        .try_next()\n        .await?\n        .context(format!(\"Interface '{}' not found\", ifname))?;\n\n    let ifindex = link.header.index;\n\n    // Parse IP address\n    let addr: Ipv4Addr = ip.parse().context(\"Invalid IPv4 address\")?;\n\n    // Add address to interface\n    handle\n        .address()\n        .add(ifindex, addr.into(), prefix)\n        .execute()\n        .await\n        .context(\"Failed to add IP address\")?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Delete IPv4 address from interface\n#[allow(dead_code)]\npub async fn del_ipv4_address(ifname: &str, ip: &str, prefix: u8) -> Result<()> {\n    let (connection, handle, _) = new_connection()?;\n    tokio::spawn(connection);\n\n    // Find interface by name\n    let mut links = handle.link().get().match_name(ifname.to_string()).execute();\n    let link = links\n        .try_next()\n        .await?\n        .context(format!(\"Interface '{}' not found\", ifname))?;\n\n    let ifindex = link.header.index;\n\n    // Parse IP address\n    let addr: Ipv4Addr = ip.parse().context(\"Invalid IPv4 address\")?;\n\n    // Get addresses filtered by interface, prefix, and address\n    let mut addresses = handle\n        .address()\n        .get()\n        .set_link_index_filter(ifindex)\n        .set_prefix_length_filter(prefix)\n        .set_address_filter(std::net::IpAddr::V4(addr))\n        .execute();\n\n    if let Some(addr_msg) = addresses.try_next().await? {\n        handle.address().del(addr_msg).execute().await?;\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Flush all addresses from interface\n#[allow(dead_code)]\n"}}

**audit/event-chain backbone** that has to make tag-driven xray routing auditable. In the target chain (Brief §3) — `PluginSchema (XrayRoute/PrivacyRoute) → tag set → op-of-controller materialises → steer_v4 + OVS rules + xray routing.rules → EventChainService.ChainEvent → StateSync.StateChange` — every materialisation step must land as a `ChainEvent` recorded by *this* crate, with `tags_touched: Vec<Tag>` typed against the closed tag enum, `actor_id` = the op-of-controller identity, `capability_id` = the routing capability, `event_hash` Merkle-batched into the Snowball, and the resulting effective state hashed into `result_effective_hash`. Today the crate cannot do this: tags are free strings, the chain is RAM-only with MD5, the Shuttle does not actually subscribe to xray-route mutations and does not inject gRPC headers, and the SQLite shadow-cache means the UI's \"schema-backed flow state\" can drift from what the controller actually programmed into `steer_v4`. The crate must (1) close the `Tag` enum, (2) persist the chain through `/dev/shm` and the Btrfs blockchain, (3) expose `EventChainService.SubscribeChain` so `op-of-controller` and the UI consume the same hash-linked truth, and (4) inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` / `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` / `X-WireGuard-Pubkey` via a Tonic interceptor so every routing mutation has provable, auditable provenance.\ncrates/op-plugins/compare-op-plugins.md:26:- Internal crate integrations: op-core, op-dbus-model, op-state, op-state-store, op-blockchain, op-network, op-dynamic-loader, op-execution-tracker.\ncrates/op-plugins/compare-op-plugins.md:77:- `op-network` - documented in SPEC\ncrates/op-chat/src/nl_admin.rs:239:            \"ovs-vsctl\",\ncrates/op-chat/src/nl_admin.rs:240:            \"ovs-ofctl\",\ncrates/op-chat/src/nl_admin.rs:242:            \"ovsdb-client\",\ncrates/op-chat/src/nl_admin.rs:246:            \"ip addr\",\ncrates/op-chat/src/nl_admin.rs:247:            \"ip link\",\ncrates/op-chat/src/nl_admin.rs:248:            \"ip route\",\ncrates/op-chat/src/nl_admin.rs:751:        let content = \"You can use ovs-vsctl add-br ovsbr0 to create the bridge\";\ncrates/op-chat/src/nl_admin.rs:753:        assert!(forbidden.contains(&\"ovs-vsctl\".to_string()));\ndeploy/CHIMERA-ICUS-README.md:199:   ip link show\ncrates/op-plugins/SPEC.md:49:op-network = { path = \"../op-network\" }\ncrates/op-plugins/SPEC.md:108:- op-network\ncrates/op-plugins/REVIEW.md:189:  - `op-core`, `op-state`, `op-state-store`, `op-blockchain`, `op-network`,\ncrates/op-plugins/REVIEW.md:971:- `op-of-controller` listening port (6653) is hardcoded constant rather\ncrates/op-plugins/REVIEW.md:1187:    - `op-xdp-steering` BPF map writer (gRPC into `op-grpc-bridge`).\ncrates/op-plugins/REVIEW.md:1302:2. {"timestamp":"2026-05-22T04:05:52.270Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"I stayed read-only against source and s6, except one caveat: I accidentally invoked `/usr/local/bin/op-ovsbr0-uplink --version`; it does not implement `--version`, so it began startup and then exited. It did not show completion and I did not see evidence it changed live state, but that binary should get a real `--version`/`--help` guard before we depend on it operationally.\n\nWhat I found:\n\n`op-ovsdb` is the intended `ovs-vsctl` / `ovsdb-client` replacement. It wraps `rovs-ovsdb`, auto-detects `/usr/local/var/run/openvswitch/db.sock`, keeps a persistent client, exposes an IDL-backed read path, and has typed methods for `create_bridge`, `add_port`, `add_port_with_type`, `set_interface_type`, `set_bridge_property`, `delete_port`, `list_bridges`, `list_bridge_ports`, and monitor/update paths.\n\n`op-network::ovsdb` is a compatibility facade over `op-ovsdb`. Existing callers can keep using `op_network::ovsdb::OvsdbClient`, but the backend is now the new `op-ovsdb` crate.\n\n`op-network::rtnetlink` is the native `ip` replacement. It covers link up/down, address add/delete/flush, default routes, link routes, veth creation, rename, ifindex lookup, proxy NDP, IPv6 table routes, and netns-compatible operations.\n\n`op-network::xdp` is the native `ip link ... xdp` / `bpftool attach-ish` replacement for loading and attaching XDP programs via `libbpf-rs`. It supports generic, driver, and hardware modes. It does not appear to cover BPF map updates yet, so anything that used `bpftool map update` still needs a native map writer before full replacement.\n\n`op-network::openflow` is the `ovs-ofctl` replacement substrate. It re-exports `rovs-openflow` with `VConn`, `Flow`, `Match`, `ActionList`, OXM/NXM, PacketIn/Out, etc. The current `op-of-controller` binary can read JSON intents and install flows over a Unix/TCP `VConn`, but older review notes say the long-term controller should be Xray over a Unix socket, not this binary as an independent controller. So I would treat the crate API as the replacement, but confirm whether the `op-of-controller` binary itself is still allowed.\n\nCurrent active s6 forbidden-command surface is mainly:\n\n- `/etc/s6/sv/ovs-vswitchd/run`: uses `ovs-vsctl --no-wait init`\n- `/etc/s6/sv/ovs-vethpair/*`: uses `ip` for veth/link/address\n- `/etc/s6/sv/ovsbr0-afxdp/*`: uses `ovs-vsctl` and `ip`\n- `/etc/s6/sv/setup-static-eth0/*` and `/etc/s6/rc.local`: stale direct `ip` address/route setup\n\nLikely replacements, pending your confirmation:\n\n- `ovs-vethpair` -> `op-ovsbr0-uplink` with `DATA_VETH_HOST=grpc-uplink DATA_VETH_PEER=grpc-phys ENABLE_OF_VETH=0/1 ATTACH_XDP=0/1`\n- `ovsbr0-afxdp` -> probably split between `op-ovsbr0-setup` and `op-ovsbr0-uplink`, but the live script also handles `148.113.204.83/32` routing on `ovsbr0`; current binaries may need a small native route/address bootstrap mode.\n- `ovs-ofctl` usage -> `rovs-openflow` path, probably through Xray or a corrected controller.\n- `bpftool map update` usage -> not fully covered yet unless there is another crate/binary I have not inspected.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

{"timestamp":"2026-05-22T04:06:59.463Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes, confirmed: `rovs-ovsdb` is the real replacement for `ovsdb-client`, and `op-ovsdb` is the repo facade around it.\n\nWhat it replaces cleanly:\n\n- `ovsdb-client transact ...`\n  - `rovs_ovsdb::Client::transact(operations)`\n  - Wrapped by `op_ovsdb::OvsdbClient::transact(...)`\n\n- `ovsdb-client list-dbs`\n  - `rovs_ovsdb::Client::list_dbs()`\n  - Wrapped by `op_ovsdb::OvsdbClient::list_dbs()`\n\n- raw OVSDB socket JSON-RPC via `socat`\n  - `rovs-transport` handles `unix:/path/to/db.sock`\n  - `rovs-jsonrpc` handles JSON-RPC framing\n  - `rovs-ovsdb` handles OVSDB schema/monitor/transactions\n\n- hand-built bridge/port transactions\n  - `rovs_ovsdb::Transaction`\n  - Methods used in `op-ovsdb`: `create_bridge`, `add_system_port`, `add_internal_port`, `delete_bridge`, `delete_bridge_uuid`, `mutate_by_name`\n\n- OVSDB polling/readbacks\n  - `rovs_ovsdb::Client::idl()`\n  - `client.wait()`\n  - `monitor`, `monitor_cond`, `monitor_cond_since`\n  - `op-ovsdb` exposes `monitor_db`, `idl`, `wait_for_update`\n\nImportant distinction: it replaces `ovsdb-client`, not `ovs-vswitchd` or `ovsdb-server`. We still need the daemons. The current forbidden line in `ovs-vswitchd/run`:\n\n```sh\novs-vsctl --no-wait init\n```\n\nis not an `ovsdb-client` operation exactly; it initializes the root `Open_vSwitch` row if needed. `op-ovsdb::ensure_initialized()` only warns if `Open_vSwitch` is empty. It does not currently create that initial row. So that is a gap before we remove `ovs-vsctl --no-wait init`.\n\nSo my replacement map is:\n\n- `ovsdb-client` -> definitely `op-ovsdb` / `rovs-ovsdb`\n- `ovs-vsctl add-br/add-port/set/list` -> mostly `op-ovsdb`, already covered\n- `ovs-vsctl --no-wait init` -> not fully covered yet; needs a small native initializer\n- `ovs-ofctl` -> `rovs-openflow`\n- `ip ...` -> `op-network::rtnetlink`\n- `ip link ... xdp` -> `op-network::xdp`\n- `bpftool map update` -> not covered yet from what I saw\n\nI would confirm `op-ovsdb` as the OVSDB client replacement, with one TODO: add `ensure_open_vswitch_root_row()` or equivalent before cutting the last `ovs-vsctl --no-wait init` out of s6.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

{"timestamp":"2026-05-22T04:07:37.009Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes. `rovs-openflow` is the real `ovs-ofctl` replacement substrate.\n\nWhat it covers:\n\n- `ovs-ofctl add-flow`\n  - `rovs_openflow::Flow::add()`\n  - `Match` builder for OXM/NXM fields\n  - `ActionList` builder for output, normal, controller, CT/NAT, learn, resubmit, set tunnel, group, etc.\n  - `VConn::send_flow()` / `send_flow_sync()`\n\n- `ovs-ofctl del-flows`\n  - `rovs_openflow::Flow::delete()`\n  - Same `VConn::send_flow*` path\n\n- `ovs-ofctl dump-flows`\n  - `FlowStatsRequest`\n  - `VConn` has flow stats parsing support via multipart replies\n\n- Packet handling\n  - `PacketIn`\n  - `PacketOut`\n  - `VConn::send_packet_out`\n\n- Controller/session mechanics\n  - `VConn::connect(Address)`\n  - supports `unix:` through shared `rovs-transport`\n  - OpenFlow handshake\n  - echo handling\n  - barrier-backed sync flow install\n\nSo the clean mapping is:\n\n- `ovsdb-client` / OVSDB JSON-RPC shell -> `op-ovsdb` over `rovs-ovsdb`\n- `ovs-ofctl` -> `op-network::openflow` over `rovs-openflow`\n- raw Unix/TCP transport -> `rovs-transport`\n\nBut live state shows an important issue: inside `wg-xray`, `op-of-controller.service` is loaded and auto-restarting, while `xray.service` is failed. I also do not see a listening OpenFlow Unix socket like `xray-of.sock` or TCP `6653` from the host probe.\n\nSo I’d phrase it this way: `rovs-openflow` is the correct library replacement for `ovs-ofctl`, but we still need to decide which process owns it. Based on your architecture, that should probably be Xray or an Xray-adjacent controller path, not a stale standalone `op-of-controller` service unless you intentionally want that binary to be the OpenFlow programmer inside `wg-xray`.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

{"timestamp":"2026-05-22T04:07:44.959Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"For OpenFlow: no, not in the OVSDB sense.\n\nThere are two different “transact” concepts here:\n\n- OVSDB `transact`\n  - Replaced by `rovs-ovsdb` / `op-ovsdb`\n  - This is for database operations: Bridge, Port, Interface, Controller rows, mirrors, options, etc.\n\n- OpenFlow flow programming\n  - Replaced by `rovs-openflow`\n  - This is not called `transact`; it sends OpenFlow messages: `FlowMod`, `MultipartRequest`, `PacketOut`, `BarrierRequest`, etc.\n\nSo:\n\n```text\novsdb-client transact ...     -> op-ovsdb / rovs-ovsdb\novs-ofctl add-flow/del-flows  -> rovs-openflow\novs-ofctl dump-flows          -> rovs-openflow multipart flow stats\n```\n\nIf a shell script used OVSDB `transact` to set bridge controllers, add ports, set interface options, or create mirrors, that belongs to `op-ovsdb`.\n\nIf it used `ovs-ofctl` to install packet steering rules, that belongs to `rovs-openflow`.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-05-22T04:07:44.965Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"For OpenFlow: no, not in the OVSDB sense.\n\nThere are two different “transact” concepts here:\n\n- OVSDB `transact`\n  - Replaced by `rovs-ovsdb` / `op-ovsdb`\n  - This is for database operations: Bridge, Port, Interface, Controller rows, mirrors, options, etc.\n\n- OpenFlow flow programming\n  - Replaced by `rovs-openflow`\n  - This is not called `transact`; it sends OpenFlow messages: `FlowMod`, `MultipartRequest`, `PacketOut`, `BarrierRequest`, etc.\n\nSo:\n\n```text\novsdb-client transact ...     -> op-ovsdb / rovs-ovsdb\novs-ofctl add-flow/del-flows  -> rovs-openflow\novs-ofctl dump-flows          -> rovs-openflow multipart flow stats\n```\n\nIf a shell script used OVSDB `transact` to set bridge controllers, add ports, set interface options, or create mirrors, that belongs to `op-ovsdb`.\n\nIf it used `ovs-ofctl` to install packet steering rules, that belongs to `rovs-openflow`."}],"phase":"final_answer"}}

Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n"}},"realtime_active":false,"summary":"none","user_instructions":"### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. {"timestamp":"2026-05-22T04:08:22.056Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes, exactly. `rovs-ovsdb` is a big deal because it replaces raw OVSDB `transact`.\n\nIt gives us:\n\n- Direct Unix socket OVSDB access without `ovsdb-client`, `socat`, or hand-framed JSON-RPC.\n- Native `transact()` for arbitrary OVSDB operations.\n- Typed `Transaction` builders for common operations like bridge and port creation.\n- Persistent connection instead of reconnecting for every shell command.\n- IDL monitoring, so reads can come from an in-memory OVSDB replica instead of repeated selects.\n- Cleaner error handling around transaction results.\n\nSo all of these old patterns should become `rovs-ovsdb` / `op-ovsdb`:\n\n```sh\novsdb-client transact ...\nprintf '{\"method\":\"transact\"...}' | socat UNIX-CONNECT:/run/openvswitch/db.sock\novs-vsctl add-br ...\novs-vsctl add-port ...\novs-vsctl set Interface ...\novs-vsctl list-ports ...\n```\n\nThe only OVSDB gap I saw is `ovs-vsctl --no-wait init`, which initializes the root `Open_vSwitch` row. That can be added to `op-ovsdb`; after that, the OVSDB shell surface can be removed cleanly.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-05-22T04:08:22.061Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"Yes, exactly. `rovs-ovsdb` is a big deal because it replaces raw OVSDB `transact`.\n\nIt gives us:\n\n- Direct Unix socket OVSDB access without `ovsdb-client`, `socat`, or hand-framed JSON-RPC.\n- Native `transact()` for arbitrary OVSDB operations.\n- Typed `Transaction` builders for common operations like bridge and port creation.\n- Persistent connection instead of reconnecting for every shell command.\n- IDL monitoring, so reads can come from an in-memory OVSDB replica instead of repeated selects.\n- Cleaner error handling around transaction results.\n\nSo all of these old patterns should become `rovs-ovsdb` / `op-ovsdb`:\n\n```sh\novsdb-client transact ...\nprintf '{\"method\":\"transact\"...}' | socat UNIX-CONNECT:/run/openvswitch/db.sock\novs-vsctl add-br ...\novs-vsctl add-port ...\novs-vsctl set Interface ...\novs-vsctl list-ports ...\n```\n\nThe only OVSDB gap I saw is `ovs-vsctl --no-wait init`, which initializes the root `Open_vSwitch` row. That can be added to `op-ovsdb`; after that, the OVSDB shell surface can be removed cleanly."}],"phase":"final_answer"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-05-22T04:10:21.746Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call","status":"completed","call_id":"call_QHRhV6bTxIOS2rKAihxNmll4","name":"apply_patch","input":"*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: docs/network/README.md\n+# Network Source Of Truth\n+\n+This folder documents the rebuilt network stack as it exists after the Btrfs\n+volume loss and ground-up network rebuild. Treat live s6 service definitions,\n+live Incus configuration, and live OVS/Xray state as the operational source of\n+truth. Older repo scripts and snapshots are historical unless they match the\n+live topology described here.\n+\n+## Current Topology\n+\n+The active data path is:\n+\n+1. Host `eth0` provides the public uplink.\n+2. Host OVS runs `ovsdb-server` and `ovs-vswitchd` under s6.\n+3. `ovsbr0` is the OVS bridge boundary.\n+4. The gRPC veth pair is `grpc-uplink` on the host and `grpc-phys` as the peer\n+   consumed by Incus.\n+5. Incus attaches `grpc-phys` to the `wg-xray` container as `eth0`.\n+6. Inside `wg-xray`, the visible NIC is `eth0`, not `grpc-phys`.\n+7. Xray owns gRPC routing for containers. OVS/OpenFlow and XDP own steering and\n+   obfuscation policy.\n+\n+Confirmed live naming:\n+\n+| Role | Live name |\n+| --- | --- |\n+| Host uplink | `eth0` |\n+| OVS bridge | `ovsbr0` |\n+| Host gRPC veth end | `grpc-uplink` |\n+| Incus-consumed veth peer | `grpc-phys` |\n+| Container | `wg-xray` |\n+| Container-visible gRPC NIC | `eth0` |\n+\n+Names such as `grpc-pipe`, `grpc-bridge`, `grpc-uplink0`, and `vop-br0` belong\n+to older experiments unless live s6 or live Incus state reintroduces them.\n+\n+## Native Replacement Crates\n+\n+The rebuilt stack should not rely on shell helpers such as `ovs-vsctl`,\n+`ovs-ofctl`, `ovsdb-client`, raw `socat` JSON-RPC, or ad hoc `ip` commands for\n+service logic. The replacement crates are:\n+\n+| Old surface | Replacement |\n+| --- | --- |\n+| `ovsdb-client transact ...` | `op-ovsdb` backed by `rovs-ovsdb` |\n+| raw OVSDB JSON-RPC over `socat` | `rovs-ovsdb` through `rovs-jsonrpc` and `rovs-transport` |\n+| `ovs-vsctl add-br`, `add-port`, `set Interface`, `list-ports` | `op-ovsdb::OvsdbClient` typed methods |\n+| `ovs-ofctl add-flow`, `del-flows`, `dump-flows` | `op-network::openflow` backed by `rovs-openflow` |\n+| `ip link`, `ip addr`, `ip route` | `op-network::rtnetlink` |\n+| `ip link ... xdp` | `op-network::xdp` backed by `libbpf-rs` |\n+\n+`op-ovsdb` is the main OVSDB replacement. It uses `rovs-ovsdb` for persistent\n+Unix socket connections, native `transact`, typed `Transaction` builders, and an\n+IDL-backed in-memory OVSDB replica. This replaces both `ovsdb-client` and most\n+`ovs-vsctl` usage.\n+\n+`op-network::openflow` is the OpenFlow replacement. It re-exports\n+`rovs-openflow`, including `VConn`, `Flow`, `Match`, `ActionList`,\n+`FlowStatsRequest`, `PacketIn`, and `PacketOut`. This replaces `ovs-ofctl`\n+mechanics. The owner process still matters: the target architecture keeps Xray\n+as the routing controller, with OpenFlow messages emitted over the Xray-owned\n+controller path rather than an ad hoc TCP controller.\n+\n+## Known Gaps Before Full Cutover\n+\n+`ovs-vsctl --no-wait init` is still present in the live `ovs-vswitchd` s6\n+service. `op-ovsdb::ensure_initialized()` currently verifies connectivity and\n+warns when the `Open_vSwitch` root table is empty, but it does not yet create\n+the initial root row. Add a native root-row initializer before removing that\n+last `ovs-vsctl` call.\n+\n+`bpftool map update` replacement is not confirmed yet. `op-network::xdp` covers\n+native XDP program load, attach, and detach. If any live service updates BPF\n+maps, add or identify a native map writer before deleting the shell path.\n+\n+`op-of-controller` exists as a Rust binary using `rovs-openflow`, but live\n+architecture needs confirmation before it is treated as the controller of\n+record. Current intent is that Xray owns gRPC routing and OpenFlow policy\n+materialization.\n+\n+## s6 Cleanup Rules\n+\n+Active s6 services should be small launchers for native binaries. They should\n+not contain OVSDB JSON payloads, OpenFlow command strings, or imperative network\n+setup logic that belongs in Rust.\n+\n+Keep only services needed for the live topology. Disabled mistrials should be\n+archived or removed after confirming they are not referenced by the active\n+s6-rc database.\n+\n+Descriptive service names should identify the thing being managed:\n+\n+| Current or proposed name | Meaning |\n+| --- | --- |\n+| `ovsdb-server` | OVSDB daemon |\n+| `ovs-vswitchd` | OVS switch daemon |\n+| `ovsbr0-afxdp` | `ovsbr0` plus AF_XDP uplink bootstrap |\n+| `ovs-vethpair` | host/container gRPC veth pair bootstrap |\n+| `xray-routing` | Xray routing controller service, if moved into s6 |\n+| `grpc-identity-bridge` | Rust gRPC bridge service, if moved into s6 |\n+\n+## Next Documentation Files\n+\n+Planned files for this folder:\n+\n+| File | Purpose |\n+| --- | --- |\n+| `live-topology.md` | Exact live addresses, interfaces, routes, and container mapping |\n+| `s6-services.md` | Active s6 service graph and cleanup decisions |\n+| `native-replacements.md` | Command-by-command migration from shell helpers to Rust crates |\n+| `xray-openflow.md` | Xray, OpenFlow table A/B, and obfuscation steering contract |\n*** End Patch\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-05-22T04:10:28.590Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_ygPnE3DiqCEX7Ult63dL6Z9O","output":"Chunk ID: ad5c16\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1218\nOutput:\n# Network Source Of Truth\n\nThis folder documents the rebuilt network stack as it exists after the Btrfs\nvolume loss and ground-up network rebuild. Treat live s6 service definitions,\nlive Incus configuration, and live OVS/Xray state as the operational source of\ntruth. Older repo scripts and snapshots are historical unless they match the\nlive topology described here.\n\n## Current Topology\n\nThe active data path is:\n\n1. Host `eth0` provides the public uplink.\n2. Host OVS runs `ovsdb-server` and `ovs-vswitchd` under s6.\n3. `ovsbr0` is the OVS bridge boundary.\n4. The gRPC veth pair is `grpc-uplink` on the host and `grpc-phys` as the peer\n   consumed by Incus.\n5. Incus attaches `grpc-phys` to the `wg-xray` container as `eth0`.\n6. Inside `wg-xray`, the visible NIC is `eth0`, not `grpc-phys`.\n7. Xray owns gRPC routing for containers. OVS/OpenFlow and XDP own steering and\n   obfuscation policy.\n\nConfirmed live naming:\n\n| Role | Live name |\n| --- | --- |\n| Host uplink | `eth0` |\n| OVS bridge | `ovsbr0` |\n| Host gRPC veth end | `grpc-uplink` |\n| Incus-consumed veth peer | `grpc-phys` |\n| Container | `wg-xray` |\n| Container-visible gRPC NIC | `eth0` |\n\nNames such as `grpc-pipe`, `grpc-bridge`, `grpc-uplink0`, and `vop-br0` belong\nto older experiments unless live s6 or live Incus state reintroduces them.\n\n## Native Replacement Crates\n\nThe rebuilt stack should not rely on shell helpers such as `ovs-vsctl`,\n`ovs-ofctl`, `ovsdb-client`, raw `socat` JSON-RPC, or ad hoc `ip` commands for\nservice logic. The replacement crates are:\n\n| Old surface | Replacement |\n| --- | --- |\n| `ovsdb-client transact ...` | `op-ovsdb` backed by `rovs-ovsdb` |\n| raw OVSDB JSON-RPC over `socat` | `rovs-ovsdb` through `rovs-jsonrpc` and `rovs-transport` |\n| `ovs-vsctl add-br`, `add-port`, `set Interface`, `list-ports` | `op-ovsdb::OvsdbClient` typed methods |\n| `ovs-ofctl add-flow`, `del-flows`, `dump-flows` | `op-network::openflow` backed by `rovs-openflow` |\n| `ip link`, `ip addr`, `ip route` | `op-network::rtnetlink` |\n| `ip link ... xdp` | `op-network::xdp` backed by `libbpf-rs` |\n\n`op-ovsdb` is the main OVSDB replacement. It uses `rovs-ovsdb` for persistent\nUnix socket connections, native `transact`, typed `Transaction` builders, and an\nIDL-backed in-memory OVSDB replica. This replaces both `ovsdb-client` and most\n`ovs-vsctl` usage.\n\n`op-network::openflow` is the OpenFlow replacement. It re-exports\n`rovs-openflow`, including `VConn`, `Flow`, `Match`, `ActionList`,\n`FlowStatsRequest`, `PacketIn`, and `PacketOut`. This replaces `ovs-ofctl`\nmechanics. The owner process still matters: the target architecture keeps Xray\nas the routing controller, with OpenFlow messages emitted over the Xray-owned\ncontroller path rather than an ad hoc TCP controller.\n\n## Known Gaps Before Full Cutover\n\n`ovs-vsctl --no-wait init` is still present in the live `ovs-vswitchd` s6\nservice. `op-ovsdb::ensure_initialized()` currently verifies connectivity and\nwarns when the `Open_vSwitch` root table is empty, but it does not yet create\nthe initial root row. Add a native root-row initializer before removing that\nlast `ovs-vsctl` call.\n\n`bpftool map update` replacement is not confirmed yet. `op-network::xdp` covers\nnative XDP program load, attach, and detach. If any live service updates BPF\nmaps, add or identify a native map writer before deleting the shell path.\n\n`op-of-controller` exists as a Rust binary using `rovs-openflow`, but live\narchitecture needs confirmation before it is treated as the controller of\nrecord. Current intent is that Xray owns gRPC routing and OpenFlow policy\nmaterialization.\n\n## s6 Cleanup Rules\n\nActive s6 services should be small launchers for native binaries. They should\nnot contain OVSDB JSON payloads, OpenFlow command strings, or imperative network\nsetup logic that belongs in Rust.\n\nKeep only services needed for the live topology. Disabled mistrials should be\narchived or removed after confirming they are not referenced by the active\ns6-rc database.\n\nDescriptive service names should identify the thing being managed:\n\n| Current or proposed name | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `ovsdb-server` | OVSDB daemon |\n| `ovs-vswitchd` | OVS switch daemon |\n| `ovsbr0-afxdp` | `ovsbr0` plus AF_XDP uplink bootstrap |\n| `ovs-vethpair` | host/container gRPC veth pair bootstrap |\n| `xray-routing` | Xray routing controller service, if moved into s6 |\n| `grpc-identity-bridge` | Rust gRPC bridge service, if moved into s6 |\n\n## Next Documentation Files\n\nPlanned files for this folder:\n\n| File | Purpose |\n| --- | --- |\n| `live-topology.md` | Exact live addresses, interfaces, routes, and container mapping |\n| `s6-services.md` | Active s6 service graph and cleanup decisions |\n| `native-replacements.md` | Command-by-command migration from shell helpers to Rust crates |\n| `xray-openflow.md` | Xray, OpenFlow table A/B, and obfuscation steering contract |\n"}}

Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. {"timestamp":"2026-05-22T04:13:40.364Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"For the live s6 cleanup: no, I would not wait for the D-Bus tree.\n\nReason: s6 bootstraps the substrate that the D-Bus tree will depend on. OVSDB, `ovs-vswitchd`, `ovsbr0`, the Incus veth boundary, Xray, and the gRPC bridge need to come up before higher-level D-Bus object orchestration can be trusted. If s6 still shells out through forbidden commands, the base layer is already out of policy before D-Bus gets a chance to act.\n\nBut I would split the replacement work:\n\n- Do now: replace boot/runtime substrate commands with native Rust binaries or add missing native binaries.\n  - `ovsdb-client`/raw `transact` -> `op-ovsdb`\n  - `ovs-vsctl` bridge/port/interface ops -> `op-ovsdb`\n  - `ip` link/address/route logic -> `op-network::rtnetlink`\n  - `ovs-ofctl` flows -> `rovs-openflow`, probably via Xray path\n- Wait for D-Bus tree: user-facing or dynamic control operations.\n  - mutating routes from UI/chatbot\n  - adding/removing schema-owned services\n  - changing obfuscation/routing policy\n  - exposing Accountability Page objects\n  - long-lived state projection and audit controls\n\nOne exception: `ovs-vsctl --no-wait init`. We should add a tiny native OVSDB root initializer first, then replace it. That is still substrate work and does not need D-Bus.\n\nSo the practical sequence is: native s6 substrate first, D-Bus object tree second, policy/control-plane mutations through D-Bus after that.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

{"timestamp":"2026-05-22T04:15:26.763Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_RZ5gUJoafQzOIPkmYLBK98Lp","output":"Chunk ID: 9296eb\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1362\nOutput:\n[package]\nname = \"op-ovsdb\"\nversion.workspace = true\nedition.workspace = true\nlicense.workspace = true\ndescription = \"OVSDB client facade backed by rovs-ovsdb (IDL, transactions, monitor)\"\n\n[dependencies]\nrovs-ovsdb.workspace = true\nanyhow.workspace = true\nserde_json.workspace = true\ntokio.workspace = true\ntracing.workspace = true\nuuid.workspace = true\n//! OVSDB client facade backed by `rovs-ovsdb`.\n//!\n//! Provides an `OvsdbClient` with the same method names as the legacy\n//! hand-rolled JSON-RPC client in `op-network::ovsdb`, but internally uses\n//! `rovs_ovsdb::Client` for a persistent connection, in-memory IDL replica,\n//! and typed `Transaction` builder.\n//!\n//! # Architecture\n//!\n//! - **Persistent connection** — one `rovs_ovsdb::Client` is reused across\n//!   calls (vs. the old per-call `UnixStream` reconnect).\n//! - **IDL replica** — `client.idl().rows(\"Bridge\")` gives zero-copy reads\n//!   of OVSDB state, matching AGENTS.md \"1:1 Direct Read\" rule.\n//! - **Transaction builder** — `rovs_ovsdb::Transaction::create_bridge`,\n//!   `add_system_port`, `add_internal_port`, etc. replace hand-built JSON.\n//! - **Monitor** — a dedicated background `rovs_ovsdb::Client` calls\n//!   `wait()` in a loop and pushes `serde_json::Value` updates into an\n//!   `mpsc::Receiver`, preserving the existing `monitor_db()` consumer API.\n//!\n//! This crate replaces the OVSDB **transport layer only**. It does NOT\n//! touch schema validation, plugin registry, DBus mirror, reconciler,\n//! orchestrator, audit trail, gRPC, rtnetlink, or container lifecycle.\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse serde_json::{json, Value};\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tokio::sync::Mutex;\nuse uuid::Uuid;\n\n// Re-export rovs-ovsdb types for advanced callers.\npub use rovs_ovsdb::{ClientConfig, Idl, MonitorVersion, RowRef, Transaction};\n\n/// Default OVSDB Unix socket paths (checked in order).\nconst SOCKET_PATHS: &[&str] = &[\n    \"/usr/local/var/run/openvswitch/db.sock\",\n    \"/var/run/openvswitch/db.sock\",\n    \"/run/openvswitch/db.sock\",\n];\n\n/// Resolve the OVSDB socket path.\n///\n/// Checks `OVSDB_SOCKET` env var first, then falls back to auto-detecting\n/// from `SOCKET_PATHS` by looking for an existing file.\nfn resolve_socket_path() -> String {\n    if let Ok(path) = std::env::var(\"OVSDB_SOCKET\") {\n        return path;\n    }\n    SOCKET_PATHS\n        .iter()\n        .find(|p| Path::new(p).exists())\n        .unwrap_or(&SOCKET_PATHS[0])\n        .to_string()\n}\n\n/// Format a socket path as a `rovs-transport` address string.\nfn socket_addr(path: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\"unix:{}\", path)\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Inner client state (behind Arc<Mutex<>> for lazy async init)\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nstruct Inner {\n    client: Option<rovs_ovsdb::Client>,\n    socket_path: String,\n}\n\nimpl Inner {\n    /// Ensure the `rovs_ovsdb::Client` is connected. Idempotent.\n    async fn ensure_connected(&mut self) -> Result<&mut rovs_ovsdb::Client> {\n        if self.client.is_none() {\n            let addr = socket_addr(&self.socket_path);\n            tracing::debug!(\"Connecting to OVSDB at {}\", addr);\n            let client = rovs_ovsdb::Client::connect(&addr)\n                .await\n                .context(\"Failed to connect to OVSDB\")?;\n            tracing::info!(\"Connected to OVSDB, IDL state: {:?}\", client.idl().state());\n            self.client = Some(client);\n        }\n        Ok(self.client.as_mut().expect(\"just ensured client is Some\"))\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Public facade\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// OVSDB client backed by `rovs-ovsdb`.\n///\n/// Construct with [`OvsdbClient::new`] (sync) or [`OvsdbClient::connect`]\n/// (async, eager connection). The lazy variant connects on first use.\npub struct OvsdbClient {\n    inner: Arc<Mutex<Inner>>,\n}\n\nimpl OvsdbClient {\n    /// Create a client that connects lazily on first operation.\n    ///\n    /// The socket path is auto-detected from `SOCKET_PATHS`.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            inner: Arc::new(Mutex::new(Inner {\n                client: None,\n                socket_path: resolve_socket_path(),\n            })),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a client with an explicit socket path (lazy connect).\n    pub fn with_socket(path: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            inner: Arc::new(Mutex::new(Inner {\n                client: None,\n                socket_path: path.into(),\n            })),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Connect eagerly and return a ready client.\n    pub async fn connect() -> Result<Self> {\n        let this = Self::new();\n        this.inner.lock().await.ensure_connected().await?;\n        Ok(this)\n    }\n\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n    // Lifecycle\n    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    /// Ensure the OVSDB database is reachable and the IDL is monitoring.\n    ///\n    /// Idempotent — safe to call repeatedly.\n    pub async fn ensure_initialized(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut guard = self.inner.lock().await;\n        let client = guard.ensure_connected().await?;\n\n        if !client.is_connected() {\n            // Reconnect — the old connection may have dropped.\n"}}

Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n"}},"realtime_active":false,"summary":"none","user_instructions":"### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-05-22T04:17:18.714Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call","status":"completed","call_id":"call_fPSwhPXZVujFwSgACmXRO5L5","name":"apply_patch","input":"*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: crates/op-ovsdb/src/lib.rs\n@@\n     pub async fn ensure_initialized(&self) -> Result<()> {\n         let mut guard = self.inner.lock().await;\n         let client = guard.ensure_connected().await?;\n@@\n \n         Ok(())\n     }\n+\n+    /// Ensure the singleton `Open_vSwitch` root row exists.\n+    ///\n+    /// This is the native replacement for `ovs-vsctl --no-wait init`. It does\n+    /// not create bridges or ports; it only inserts the root row required by\n+    /// OVSDB before `ovs-vswitchd` and higher-level OVSDB transactions can use\n+    /// the database normally.\n+    ///\n+    /// Returns `true` when a row was inserted and `false` when the database was\n+    /// already initialized.\n+    pub async fn ensure_open_vswitch_root_row(&self) -> Result<bool> {\n+        let mut guard = self.inner.lock().await;\n+        let client = guard.ensure_connected().await?;\n+\n+        let select = json!([{\n+            \"op\": \"select\",\n+            \"table\": \"Open_vSwitch\",\n+            \"where\": [],\n+            \"columns\": [\"_uuid\"]\n+        }]);\n+        let result = client.transact(select).await?;\n+        check_transaction_errors(&result)?;\n+\n+        let has_root = result\n+            .get(0)\n+            .and_then(|op| op.get(\"rows\"))\n+            .and_then(|rows| rows.as_array())\n+            .is_some_and(|rows| !rows.is_empty());\n+        if has_root {\n+            tracing::info!(\"Open_vSwitch root row already exists\");\n+            return Ok(false);\n+        }\n+\n+        let insert = json!([{\n+            \"op\": \"insert\",\n+            \"table\": \"Open_vSwitch\",\n+            \"row\": {}\n+        }]);\n+        let result = client.transact(insert).await?;\n+        check_transaction_errors(&result)?;\n+\n+        let _ = client.run().await;\n+        tracing::info!(\"Open_vSwitch root row inserted\");\n+        Ok(true)\n+    }\n \n     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n     // Raw RPC\n     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n*** End Patch\n"}}
