It does\n+    /// not create bridges or ports; it only inserts the root row required by\n+    /// OVSDB before `ovs-vswitchd` and higher-level OVSDB transactions can use\n+    /// the database normally.\n+    ///\n+    /// Returns `true` when a row was inserted and `false` when the database was\n+    /// already initialized.\n+    pub async fn ensure_open_vswitch_root_row(&self) -> Result<bool> {\n+        let mut guard = self.inner.lock().await;\n+        let client = guard.ensure_connected().await?;\n+\n+        let select = json!([{\n+            \"op\": \"select\",\n+            \"table\": \"Open_vSwitch\",\n+            \"where\": [],\n+            \"columns\": [\"_uuid\"]\n+        }]);\n+        let result = client.transact(select).await?;\n+        check_transaction_errors(&result)?;\n+\n+        let has_root = result\n+            .get(0)\n+            .and_then(|op| op.get(\"rows\"))\n+            .and_then(|rows| rows.as_array())\n+            .is_some_and(|rows| !rows.is_empty());\n+        if has_root {\n+            tracing::info!(\"Open_vSwitch root row already exists\");\n+            return Ok(false);\n+        }\n+\n+        let insert = json!([{\n+            \"op\": \"insert\",\n+            \"table\": \"Open_vSwitch\",\n+            \"row\": {}\n+        }]);\n+        let result = client.transact(insert).await?;\n+        check_transaction_errors(&result)?;\n+\n+        let _ = client.run().await;\n+        tracing::info!(\"Open_vSwitch root row inserted\");\n+        Ok(true)\n+    }\n+\n     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n     // Raw RPC\n     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n"}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. UPLINK          = ens3\n//!   UPLINK_OVS_TYPE = system          (system | afxdp)\n//!   AF_XDP_MODE     = skb             (skb | native, when UPLINK_OVS_TYPE=afxdp)\n//!   AF_XDP_RXQ      = 2               (when UPLINK_OVS_TYPE=afxdp)\n//!   DATA_VETH_HOST  = grpc-uplink0\n//!   DATA_VETH_PEER  = grpc-phys\n//!   OF_VETH_HOST    = of-uplink0\n//!   OF_VETH_PEER    = of-phys\n//!   ENABLE_OF_VETH  = 1\n//!   XDP_OBJ         = /usr/local/lib/op-xdp/xdp_steering.o\n//!   XDP_SEC         = xdp\n//!   XDP_MODE        = generic         (generic | driver | hardware)\n//!   ATTACH_XDP      = 1               (set to 0 to skip XDP attach)\n//!\n//! Legacy VETH_HOST/VETH_PEER are still accepted as fallbacks for the data pair.\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse op_network::ovsdb::OvsdbClient;\nuse op_network::rtnetlink as rtn;\nuse op_network::xdp::{self, XdpMode};\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\n\nfn env_or(k: &str, d: &str) -> String {\n    std::env::var(k).unwrap_or_else(|_| d.to_string())\n}\n\nfn env_or_compat(primary: &str, legacy: &str, default: &str) -> String {\n    std::env::var(primary)\n        .or_else(|_| std::env::var(legacy))\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| default.to_string())\n}\n\nasync fn ensure_bridge_port(ovsdb: &OvsdbClient, bridge: &str, port: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    ensure_bridge_port_with_type(ovsdb, bridge, port, None).await\n}\n\nasync fn ensure_bridge_port_with_type(\n    ovsdb: &OvsdbClient,\n    bridge: &str,\n    port: &str,\n    port_type: Option<&str>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let existing_ports = ovsdb\n        .list_bridge_ports(bridge)\n        .await\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"list_bridge_ports {}\", bridge))?;\n    if existing_ports.iter().any(|p| p == port) {\n        tracing::info!(%port, %bridge, \"port already present on bridge\");\n        if let Some(port_type) = port_type {\n            ovsdb\n                .set_interface_type(port, port_type)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"set interface {} type {}\", port, port_type))?;\n        }\n    } else {\n        ovsdb\n            .add_port_with_type(bridge, port, port_type)\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"add_port {} -> {}\", port, bridge))?;\n        tracing::info!(%port, %bridge, \"port added to bridge\");\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nasync fn ensure_host_veth(host: &str, peer: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    rtn::create_veth_pair(host, peer)\n        .await\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"create_veth_pair {}<->{}\", host, peer))?;\n    rtn::link_up(host)\n        .await\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"link up {}\", host))?;\n    tracing::info!(%host, %peer, \"veth pair ready\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[tokio::main(flavor = \"current_thread\")]\nasync fn main() -> Result<()> {\n    tracing_subscriber::fmt()\n        .with_env_filter(\n            tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter::try_from_default_env()\n                .unwrap_or_else(|_| tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter::new(\"info\")),\n        )\n        .init();\n\n    let bridge = env_or(\"BRIDGE\", \"ovsbr0\");\n    let uplink = env_or(\"UPLINK\", \"ens3\");\n    let uplink_ovs_type = env_or_compat(\"UPLINK_OVS_TYPE\", \"OVS_UPLINK_TYPE\", \"system\");\n    let af_xdp_mode = env_or(\"AF_XDP_MODE\", \"skb\");\n    let af_xdp_rxq = env_or(\"AF_XDP_RXQ\", \"2\");\n    let data_veth_host = env_or_compat(\"DATA_VETH_HOST\", \"VETH_HOST\", \"grpc-uplink\");\n    let data_veth_peer = env_or_compat(\"DATA_VETH_PEER\", \"VETH_PEER\", \"eth0\");\n    let of_veth_host = env_or(\"OF_VETH_HOST\", \"of-uplink0\");\n    let of_veth_peer = env_or(\"OF_VETH_PEER\", \"of-phys\");\n    let enable_of_veth = env_or(\"ENABLE_OF_VETH\", \"1\") != \"0\";\n    let xdp_obj = PathBuf::from(env_or(\"XDP_OBJ\", \"/usr/local/lib/op-xdp/xdp_steering.o\"));\n    let xdp_sec = env_or(\"XDP_SEC\", \"xdp\");\n    let xdp_mode = XdpMode::parse(&env_or(\"XDP_MODE\", \"generic\"))?;\n    let attach_xdp = env_or(\"ATTACH_XDP\", \"1\") != \"0\";\n\n    tracing::info!(\n        %bridge, %uplink, %data_veth_host, %data_veth_peer, %of_veth_host, %of_veth_peer,\n        xdp_obj = %xdp_obj.display(),\n        %xdp_sec, ?xdp_mode, attach_xdp, enable_of_veth, %uplink_ovs_type,\n        \"op-ovsbr0-uplink starting\"\n    );\n\n    let ovsdb = OvsdbClient::new();\n    ovsdb\n        .ensure_initialized()\n        .await\n        .context(\"OVSDB not reachable\")?;\n\n    // 1) Bridge must already exist (op-ovsbr0-setup runs first).\n    if !ovsdb\n        .bridge_exists(&bridge)\n        .await\n        .context(\"bridge_exists query\")?\n    {\n        anyhow::bail!(\n            \"bridge {} not present in OVSDB — run op-ovsbr0-setup first\",\n            bridge\n        );\n    }\n    tracing::info!(%bridge, \"bridge present\");\n\n    // 2) Prepare uplink: flush v4 + link up. Errors on flush are tolerated\n    //    (interface may already have nothing to flush).\n    let _ = rtn::flush_addresses(&uplink).await;\n    let _ = rtn::flush_default_routes_v4(&uplink).await;\n    rtn::link_up(&uplink)\n        .await\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"link up {}\", uplink))?;\n    tracing::info!(%uplink, \"uplink flushed and up\");\n\n    // 3) Attach uplink to bridge. AF_XDP mode is an OVSDB Interface type/options\n    //    choice; it is separate from the libbpf XDP program attached below.\n    let uplink_type = if uplink_ovs_type == \"afxdp\" {\n        Some(\"afxdp\")\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n    ensure_bridge_port_with_type(&ovsdb, &bridge, &uplink, uplink_type).await?;\n    if uplink_ovs_type == \"afxdp\" {\n        ovsdb\n            .set_interface_options(\n                &uplink,\n                &[\n                    (\"xdp-mode\", af_xdp_mode.as_str()),\n                    (\"n_rxq\", af_xdp_rxq.as_str()),\n                ],\n            )\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"set AF_XDP options on {}\", uplink))?;\n        tracing::info!(%uplink, xdp_mode = %af_xdp_mode, n_rxq = %af_xdp_rxq, \"AF_XDP uplink options applied\");\n    } else if uplink_ovs_type != \"system\" {\n        tracing::warn!(%uplink_ovs_type, \"unknown UPLINK_OVS_TYPE, using normal system port\");\n    }\n\n    // 4) Data veth pair: The Sled/Shuttle gRPC data path.\n    ensure_host_veth(&data_veth_host, &data_veth_peer).await?;\n\n    // 5) OpenFlow veth pair: control plane stays distinct from data traffic.\n    if enable_of_veth {\n        ensure_host_veth(&of_veth_host, &of_veth_peer).await?;\n    }\n\n    // 6) Attach host-side veths to bridge.\n    ensure_bridge_port(&ovsdb, &bridge, &data_veth_host).await?;\n    if enable_of_veth {\n        ensure_bridge_port(&ovsdb, &bridge, &of_veth_host).await?;\n    }\n\n    // 7) XDP attach on UPLINK and DATA_VETH_HOST. OpenFlow stays plain rtnetlink/OVS.\n    if attach_xdp {\n        if !xdp_obj.exists() {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                path = %xdp_obj.display(),\n                \"XDP_OBJ not present — skipping XDP attach (set ATTACH_XDP=0 to silence)\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            let loaded = xdp::load(&xdp_obj, &xdp_sec)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"load XDP ELF {}\", xdp_obj.display()))?;\n            loaded\n                .attach(&uplink, xdp_mode)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"attach XDP to {}\", uplink))?;\n            tracing::info!(%uplink, ?xdp_mode, \"XDP attached to uplink\");\n            loaded\n                .attach(&data_veth_host, xdp_mode)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"attach XDP to {}\", data_veth_host))?;\n            tracing::info!(%data_veth_host, ?xdp_mode, \"XDP attached to data veth host\");\n        }\n    } else {\n        tracing::info!(\"ATTACH_XDP=0, skipping XDP load/attach\");\n    }\n\n    // 7) Bring the bridge itself up last.\n    rtn::link_up(&bridge)\n        .await\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"link up {}\", bridge))?;\n    tracing::info!(%bridge, \"bridge link up\");\n\n    tracing::info!(\"op-ovsbr0-uplink: done\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n"}}

This replaces the s6 `ip link` and `ip addr replace` shell commands for the\n//! physical Incus handoff link. The peer end is expected to be claimed by Incus\n//! as `nictype=physical parent=grpc-phys name=eth0`.\n\nuse anyhow::{bail, Context, Result};\nuse op_network::rtnetlink;\nuse std::net::Ipv4Addr;\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct Config {\n    host_end: String,\n    container_end: String,\n    host_addr: Ipv4Cidr,\n    peer_addr: Ipv4Addr,\n    linklocal_addr: Ipv4Cidr,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct Ipv4Cidr {\n    addr: Ipv4Addr,\n    prefix: u8,\n}\n\nimpl Ipv4Cidr {\n    fn parse(input: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        let Some((addr, prefix)) = input.split_once('/') else {\n            bail!(\"expected IPv4 CIDR, got {}\", input);\n        };\n        let addr = addr\n            .parse()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid IPv4 address in {}\", input))?;\n        let prefix = prefix\n            .parse::<u8>()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid IPv4 prefix in {}\", input))?;\n        if prefix > 32 {\n            bail!(\"IPv4 prefix must be <= 32 in {}\", input);\n        }\n        Ok(Self { addr, prefix })\n    }\n}\n\nfn env_or(key: &str, default: &str) -> String {\n    std::env::var(key).unwrap_or_else(|_| default.to_string())\n}\n\nfn config() -> Result<Config> {\n    Ok(Config {\n        host_end: env_or(\"HOST_END\", \"grpc-uplink\"),\n        container_end: env_or(\"CONTAINER_END\", \"grpc-phys\"),\n        host_addr: Ipv4Cidr::parse(&env_or(\"HOST_ADDR\", \"10.200.0.2/32\"))?,\n        peer_addr: env_or(\"PEER_ADDR\", \"10.200.0.1\")\n            .parse()\n            .context(\"invalid PEER_ADDR\")?,\n        linklocal_addr: Ipv4Cidr::parse(&env_or(\"LINKLOCAL_ADDR\", \"169.254.249.57/16\"))?,\n    })\n}\n\n#[tokio::main(flavor = \"current_thread\")]\nasync fn main() -> Result<()> {\n    let cfg = config()?;\n    let command = std::env::args().nth(1).unwrap_or_else(|| \"up\".to_string());\n\n    match command.as_str() {\n        \"up\" => up(&cfg).await,\n        \"down\" => down(&cfg).await,\n        other => bail!(\"unknown command '{}'; expected up or down\", other),\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn up(cfg: &Config) -> Result<()> {\n    let host_present = rtnetlink::link_exists(&cfg.host_end).await?;\n    let container_present = rtnetlink::link_exists(&cfg.container_end).await?;\n\n    if !host_present && container_present {\n        eprintln!(\n            \"[op-grpc-vethpair] orphan peer present without host end; recreating {} <-> {}\",\n            cfg.host_end, cfg.container_end\n        );\n        rtnetlink::delete_link(&cfg.container_end).await?;\n    }\n\n    let host_present = rtnetlink::link_exists(&cfg.host_end).await?;\n    let container_present = rtnetlink::link_exists(&cfg.container_end).await?;\n    if !host_present && !container_present {\n        rtnetlink::create_veth_pair(&cfg.host_end, &cfg.container_end)\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"create {} <-> {}\", cfg.host_end, cfg.container_end))?;\n    }\n\n    rtnetlink::link_up(&cfg.host_end)\n        .await\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"link up {}\", cfg.host_end))?;\n\n    if rtnetlink::link_exists(&cfg.container_end).await? {\n        rtnetlink::link_up(&cfg.container_end)\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"link up {}\", cfg.container_end))?;\n    }\n\n    rtnetlink::replace_ipv4_address(\n        &cfg.host_end,\n        &cfg.host_addr.addr.to_string(),\n        cfg.host_addr.prefix,\n    )\n    .await\n    .with_context(|| format!(\"set host address on {}\", cfg.host_end))?;\n    rtnetlink::replace_ipv4_address(\n        &cfg.host_end,\n        &cfg.linklocal_addr.addr.to_string(),\n        cfg.linklocal_addr.prefix,\n    )\n    .await\n    .with_context(|| format!(\"set link-local address on {}\", cfg.host_end))?;\n\n    rtnetlink::add_link_route_v4(&cfg.host_end, cfg.peer_addr, 32)\n        .await\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"route peer {} via {}\", cfg.peer_addr, cfg.host_end))?;\n\n    println!(\n        \"[op-grpc-vethpair] ready: {} <-> {}\",\n        cfg.host_end, cfg.container_end\n    );\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nasync fn down(cfg: &Config) -> Result<()> {\n    if rtnetlink::link_exists(&cfg.host_end).await? {\n        rtnetlink::delete_link(&cfg.host_end).await?;\n    } else {\n        rtnetlink::delete_link(&cfg.container_end).await?;\n    }\n    println!(\n        \"[op-grpc-vethpair] deleted: {} <-> {}\",\n        cfg.host_end, cfg.container_end\n    );\n    Ok(())\n}\n"}},"status":"completed"}}

IPv6 default route\")?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Delete all IPv4 default routes via a specific interface.\n/// Called before enslaving an interface as an OVS uplink so leftover routes\n/// don't shadow the default route we later add via ovsbr0-mgmt.\npub async fn flush_default_routes_v4(ifname: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    let (connection, handle, _) = new_connection()?;\n    tokio::spawn(connection);\n\n    let mut links = handle.link().get().match_name(ifname.to_string()).execute();\n    let link = links\n        .try_next()\n        .await?\n        .context(format!(\"Interface '{}' not found\", ifname))?;\n    let ifindex = link.header.index;\n\n    let (conn2, handle2, _) = new_connection()?;\n    tokio::spawn(conn2);\n\n    let mut to_del = Vec::new();\n    let mut routes = handle2.route().get(IpVersion::V4).execute();\n    while let Ok(Some(route)) = routes.try_next().await {\n        use netlink_packet_route::route::RouteAttribute;\n        if route.header.destination_prefix_length == 0 {\n            let on_iface = route\n                .attributes\n                .iter()\n                .any(|a| matches!(a, RouteAttribute::Oif(i) if *i == ifindex));\n            if on_iface {\n                to_del.push(route);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    let (conn3, handle3, _) = new_connection()?;\n    tokio::spawn(conn3);\n    for route in to_del {\n        let _ = handle3.route().del(route).execute().await;\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Replace IPv4 default route (idempotent: delete ALL existing v4 defaults, then add).\npub async fn add_default_route_v4(ifname: &str, gateway: &str, metric: u32) -> Result<()> {\n    let (connection, handle, _) = new_connection()?;\n    tokio::spawn(connection);\n\n    let mut links = handle.link().get().match_name(ifname.to_string()).execute();\n    let link = links\n        .try_next()\n        .await?\n        .context(format!(\"Interface '{}' not found\", ifname))?;\n    let ifindex = link.header.index;\n\n    let gw: Ipv4Addr = gateway.parse().context(\"Invalid IPv4 gateway\")?;\n\n"}}

}\n    }\n\n    /// Check whether a bridge exists.\n    pub async fn bridge_exists(&self, bridge_name: &str) -> Result<bool> {\n        // Prefer IDL lookup (zero-copy).\n        {\n            let return Ok(false);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Fallback: select via transaction.\n        match self.find_bridge_uuid(bridge_name).await {\n            Ok(_) => Ok(true),\n            Err(_) => Ok(false),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Find a bridge UUID by name.\n    async fn find_bridge_uuid(&self, bridge_name: &str) -> Result<String> {\n        // IDL path.\n        {\n            let guard = self.inner.lock().await;\n            if let Some(client) = guard.client.as_ref() {\n                if client.is_connected() {\n                    for row in client.idl().rows(\"Bridge\") {\n                        if row.get_string(\"name\") == Some(bridge_name) {\n                            return Ok(row.uuid.to_string());\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Fallback: select via transaction.\n        let ops = json!([{\n            \"op\": \"select\",\n            \"table\": \"Bridge\",\n            \"where\": [[\"name\", \"==\", bridge_name]],\n            \"columns\": [\"_uuid\"]\n        }]);\n        let result = self.transact(ops).await?;\n\n        if let Some(rows) = result[0][\"rows\"].as_array() {\n            if let Some(first) = rows.first() {\n                if let Some(uuid_arr) = first[\"_uuid\"].as_array() {\n                    if uuid_arr.len() == 2 && uuid_arr[0] == \"uuid\" {\n                        return Ok(uuid_arr[1].as_str().unwrap_or_default().to_string());\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        anyhow::bail!(\"Bridge '{}' not found\", bridge_name)\n    }\n\n    /// List all bridge names.\n    pub async fn list_bridges(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n        // IDL path.\n        {\n            let guard = self.inner.lock().await;\n            if let Some(client) = guard.client.as_ref() {\n                if client.is_connected() {\n                    let names: Vec<String> = client\n                        .idl()\n                        .rows(\"Bridge\")\n                        .filter_map(|r| r.get_string(\"name\").map(String::from))\n                        .collect();\n                    return Ok(names);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Fallback: select.\n        let ops = json!([{\n            \"op\": \"select\",\n            \"table\": \"Bridge\",\n            \"where\": [],\n            \"columns\": [\"name\"]\n        }]);\n        let result = self.transact(ops).await?;\n        let mut bridges = Vec::new();\n ports_val);\n                            }\n                            break;\n                        }\n                    }\n                    return Ok(names);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Fallback: select via transaction.\n        let bridge_uuid = self.find_bridge_uuid(bridge_name).await?;\n        let ops = json!([{\n            \"op\": \"select\",\n         for port in set {\n                                if let Some(arr) = port.as_array() {\n                                    if arr.len() == 2 && arr[0] == \"uuid\" {\n }\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let mut port_names = Vec::new();\n        for pu in     \"columns\": [\"name\"]\n            }]);\n            let res = self.transact(ops).await?;\n            if let Some(rows) = res[0][\"rows\"].as_array() {\n                if let Some(first) = }\n        }\n        Ok(port_names)\n    }\n\n    /// Get bridge info as a JSON string.\n    pub async fn get_bridge_info(&self, bridge_name: &str) -> Result<String> {\n        let bridge_uuid = &bridge_uuid]]],\n            \"columns\": []\n        }]);\n        let result = self.transact(ops).await?;\n        Ok(serde_json::to_string_pretty(&result[0][\"rows\"][0])?)\n    }\n\n    //   \"op\": \"mutate\",\n                \"table\": \"Bridge\",\n                \"where\": [[\"_uuid\", \"==\", [\"uuid\", bridge_uuid]]],\n                \"mutations\": [[\"ports\", \"delete\", port_uuid]]]\n            },\n            {\n                \"op\": \"delete\",\n                \"table\": \"Interface\",\n                \"where\": [[\"name\", \"==\", port_name]]\n            }\n        ]);\n        let result = self.transact(ops).await?;\n        check_transaction_errors(&result)?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    //      Err(err) => return Err(err).with_context(|| format!(\"read {}\", path.display())),\n    };\n\n    let root: Value =\n        serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).with_context(|| format!(\"parse {}\", path.display()))?;\n    let mut flows = Vec::new();\n\n    for flow in root\n        .get(\"flows\")\n        .and_then(|v| v.as_array())\n        .into_iter()\n        .flatten()\n    {\n        let mut intent = IntentFlow {\n            priority: flow\n                .get(\"priority\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())\n                .and_then(|v| u16::try_from(v).ok())\n                .unwrap_or(default_priority),\n            cookie: flow.get(\"cookie\").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()).unwrap_or(0),\n            idle_timeout: flow\n                .get(\"idle_timeout\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())\n                .and_then(|v| u16::try_from(v).ok())\n                .unwrap_or(0),\n            hard_timeout: flow\n                .get(\"hard_timeout\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())\n                .and_then(|v| u16::try_from(v).ok())\n                .unwrap_or(0),\n            table_id: flow\n                .get(\"table\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())\n                .and_then(|v| u8::try_from(v).ok())\n                .unwrap_or(0),\n            ..Default::default()\n        };\n\n        // Parse match fields.\n        if let Some(mf) = flow.get(\"match_fields\").and_then(|v| v.as_object()) {\n            intent.in_port = mf\n                .get(\"in_port\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                .map(|s| s.to_string());\n\n            intent.eth_type = mf\n                .get(\"dl_type\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                .and_then(parse_hex_u16);\n\n            intent.ip_proto = mf\n                .get(\"ip\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                .map(|_| 0x04) // \"ip\" keyword → eth_type 0x0800 handled below\n                .or_else(|| mf.get(\"tcp\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).map(|_| 0x06))\n                .or_else(|| mf.get(\"udp\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).map(|_| 0x11))\n                .or_else(|| mf.get(\"icmp\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).map(|_| 0x01))\n                .or_else(|| mf.get(\"icmp6\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).map(|_| 0x3a));\n\n            // Set eth_type from protocol keywords.\n            if mf.contains_key(\"ip\") || mf.contains_key(\"nw_dst\") || mf.contains_key(\"nw_src\") {\n                intent.eth_type = Some(0x0800);\n            } else if mf.contains_key(\"arp\") {\n                intent.eth_type = Some(0x0806);\n            } else if mf.contains_key(\"tcp\") {\n                intent.eth_type = Some(0x0800);\n                intent.ip_proto = Some(0x06);\n            } else if mf.contains_key(\"udp\") {\n                intent.eth_type = Some(0x0800);\n                intent.ip_proto = Some(0x11);\n            } else if mf.contains_key(\"icmp\") {\n                intent.eth_type = Some(0x0800);\n                intent.ip_proto = Some(0x01);\n            } else if mf.contains_key(\"icmp6\") {\n                intent.eth_type = Some(0x86DD);\n                intent.ip_proto = Some(0x3a);\n            }\n\n            intent.nw_dst = mf\n                .get(\"nw_dst\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                .and_then(parse_ipv4_with_mask);\n\n            intent.nw_src = mf\n                .get(\"nw_src\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                .and_then(parse_ipv4_with_mask);\n\n            intent.tp_dst = mf\n                .get(\"tp_dst\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())\n                .or_else(|| {\n                    mf.get(\"tp_dst\")\n                        .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())\n                        .and_then(|v| u16::try_from(v).ok())\n                });\n\n            intent.tp_src = mf\n                .get(\"tp_src\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())\n                .or_else(|| {\n                    mf.get(\"tp_src\")\n                        .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())\n                        .and_then(|v| u16::try_from(v).ok())\n                });\n\n            intent.ct_state = mf\n                .get(\"ct_state\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                .and_then(parse_ct_state);\n\n            intent.tcp_flags = mf\n                .get(\"tcp_flags\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                .and_then(parse_tcp_flags);\n\n            intent.dl_src = mf\n                .get(\"dl_src\")\n                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                .map(|s| s.to_string());\n        }\n\n        // Parse actions.\n        if let Some(actions) = flow.get(\"actions\").and_then(|v| v.as_array()) {\n            for action in actions {\n                let kind = action.get(\"type\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or(\"\");\n                match kind {\n                    \"output\" => {\n                        intent.out_port = action\n                            .get(\"port\")\n                            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                            .map(|s| s.to_string());\n                    }\n                    \"normal\" => {\n                        intent.action_normal = true;\n                    }\n                    \"drop\" => {\n                        intent.action_drop = true;\n                    }\n                    \"controller\" => {\n                        intent.action_controller = action\n                            .get(\"max_len\")\n                            .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())\n                            .and_then(|v| u16::try_from(v).ok())\n                            .or(Some(128));\n                    }\n                    // ct, set_field, load_register, arp_responder etc. are\n                    // handled by the rovs-openflow Action enum when needed.\n                    // For now, log a warning for unsupported action types.\n                    other => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\"unsupported action type '{}' in intent, skipping\", other);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        flows.push(intent);\n    }\n\n    Ok(flows)\n}\n\nfn parse_hex_u16(s: &str) -> Option<u16> {\n    let s = s.strip_prefix(\"0x\").unwrap_or(s);\n    u16::from_str_radix(s, 16).ok()\n}\n\nfn parse_ipv4_with_mask(s: &str) -> Option<Ipv4Addr> {\n    let addr_str = s.split('/').next()?;\n    addr_str.parse().ok()\n}\n\n/// Parse ct_state string like \"+est+trk\" into a bitmask.\nfn parse_ct_state(s: &str) -> Option<u32> {\n    let mut mask = 0u32;\n    for token in s.split('+').skip(1) {\n        // Skip the leading '+' which produces an empty first token.\n        match token {\n            \"est\" => mask |= 0x10,\n            \"trk\" => mask |= 0x20,\n            \"new\" => mask |= 0x08,\n            \"rel\" => mask |= 0x04,\n            \"inv\" => mask |= 0x01,\n            \"rpl\" => mask |= 0x02,\n            \"nat\" => mask |= 0x40,\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n    Some(mask)\n}\n\n/// Parse tcp_flags string like \"+syn-ack\" or \"0x000\" into a value.\nfn parse_tcp_flags(s: &str) -> Option<u16> {\n    if let Some(hex) = s.strip_prefix(\"0x\") {\n        return u16::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok();\n    }\n    let mut flags = 0u16;\n    for token in s.split('-') {\n        let token = token.trim_start_matches('+');\n        match token {\n            \"syn\" => flags |= 0x002,\n            \"ack\" => flags |= 0x010,\n            \"fin\" => flags |= 0x001,\n            \"rst\" => flags |= 0x004,\n            \"psh\" => flags |= 0x008,\n            \"urg\" => flags |= 0x020,\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n"}}

Schema: `subid: \"sch.service.mcp.backend@v1\"`, `endpoint`, `tls_cert_ref`, `capabilities[]`, `tags[]`, `flow_table_cookie` (so OF rule programmed by Xray binds back to the schema record).\ncrates/op-gateway/REVIEW.md:421:- **Hardcoded controller-style endpoints** (`grpc://localhost:50051`, `:50052`) directly contradict the 2026-05-10 topology, where the actual decision should compile down to a schema-driven Xray routing.rules + ovsbr0 flow-table A entry.\ncrates/op-gateway/REVIEW.md:457:- **Inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`, `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID`, `X-WireGuard-Pubkey` on every outbound gRPC call to the chosen MCP backend via a tonic interceptor in this crate.**\ncrates/op-gateway/REVIEW.md:465:- Build a tonic `Interceptor` that takes a `WireGuardSession` and stamps `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint = blake2s(session_hash || event_hash)`, `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID = uuid::Uuid::now_v7()`, `X-WireGuard-Pubkey = peer_pubkey`. Place in `op-grpc-bridge`, consume here.\ncrates/op-gateway/REVIEW.md:492:- **Feature: tonic server-side gateway** that *is* the boundary (today the crate is library-only). Decisions ought to be enforceable at the wire, not advisory.\ncrates/op-gateway/REVIEW.md:510:- [ ] `op-gateway:headers` — Implement tonic interceptor that injects `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`, `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID`, `X-WireGuard-Pubkey` from the chosen `WireGuardSession`. — **Accept:** outbound gRPC carries all three headers under integration test — **blocker** — §5#5.\ncrates/op-gateway/REVIEW.md:540:This crate is meant to be a **walled-garden boundary translator**: a `PluginSchema`-validated `XrayRoute` (with its `tags[]`) arrives, and `op-gateway` must produce both (a) a per-request `RoutingDecision` event in the audit chain, and (b) the right MCP backend wire-up *via Xray*, so that the same tag that decided the decision also materialised as the OF flow-table A entry on `ovsbr0` and the `steer_v4` map entry on `ens3`. Today it does the opposite: it picks one of two hardcoded `grpc://localhost:5005{1,2}` strings, never speaks to Xray's UNIX socket, never injects the three `X-Ghostbridge-*` headers, and never emits a `ChainEvent`. To be correct under the 2026-05-10 topology, the crate must: drop SQLite + Btrfs from the hot path, derive identity exclusively from `/dev/shm` sled records, render every decision as a schema row whose materialisation step *programs Xray* (not the gateway), and stamp every outbound gRPC with the three accountability headers so that flow-table cookies, audit hashes, and WG identity all point at the same thing.\ndeploy/scripts/v2/00-final-setup.sh:7:#   vop-eth0 -> captured into wg-xray as grpc-pipe\ndeploy/scripts/v2/00-final-setup.sh:8:#   grpc-pipe-> 148.113.204.83/32 (public) + 10.200.0.1/24\ndeploy/scripts/v2/00-final-setup.sh:9:#   XDP      -> loaded on eth0 + grpc-pipe, steer_v4 populated\ndeploy/scripts/v2/00-final-setup.sh:38:ip link del grpc-bridge 2>/dev/null || true\ndeploy/scripts/v2/00-final-setup.sh:42:incus config device remove \"$CT\" grpc-pipe 2>/dev/null || true\ndeploy/scripts/v2/00-final-setup.sh:72:info \"Creating veth pair (grpc-bridge <-> grpc-pipe)\"\ndeploy/scripts/v2/00-final-setup.sh:73:ip link add grpc-bridge type veth peer name grpc-pipe\ndeploy/scripts/v2/00-final-setup.sh:74:ip link set grpc-bridge up\ndeploy/scripts/v2/00-final-setup.sh:75:ip addr add \"10.200.0.2/24\" dev grpc-bridge\ndeploy/scripts/v2/00-final-setup.sh:76:ip link set grpc-pipe down  # Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n"}},"realtime_active":false,"summary":"none","user_instructions":"### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}

Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. tonic::transport::Channel;\nuse tonic::{Request, Status};\nuse tracing::{debug, info, warn};\nuse uuid::Uuid;\n\n/// The Sled layout — must match op-grpc-bridge/src/interceptor.rs exactly.\n#[repr(C)]\nstruct IdentitySled {\n    wireguard_pubkey: [u8; 32],\n    mutation_index: u64,\n    is_valid: bool,\n    hashed_footprint: [u8; 32],\n}\n\n/// gRPC bridge client that talks to op-grpc-bridge at :50051\n/// and injects Ghostbridge headers for every request.\npub struct GrpcBridgeClient {\n    channel: Channel,\n    trace_id: String,\n}\n\nimpl GrpcBridgeClient {\n    /// Connect to the op-grpc-bridge gRPC server.\n    pub async fn connect(addr: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        let channel = Channel::from_shared(addr.to_string())?\n            .connect()\n            .await\n            .context(\"Failed to connect to op-grpc-bridge\")?;\n\n        let trace_id = format!(\"mcp-proxy-{}\", Uuid::new_v4());\n        info!(\"Connected to op-grpc-bridge at {}, trace_id={}\", addr, trace_id);\n\n        Ok(Self { channel, trace_id })\n    }\n\n    /// Read the current footprint from The Sled (shared memory).\n    /// Falls back to a zero-footprint if /dev/shm is unavailable (dev mode).\n    fn read_current_footprint() -> String {\n        match File::open(\"/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat\") {\n            Ok(file) => {\n                let mmap = unsafe { MmapOptions::new().map(&file) };\n                match mmap {\n                    Ok(mmap) => {\n                        let sled_ptr = mmap.as_ptr() as *const IdentitySled;\n                        let footprint = unsafe { (*sled_ptr).hashed_footprint };\n                        hex::encode(footprint)\n                    }\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        warn!(\"Mmap failed for plugin_schema.dat: {}\", e);\n                        \"0\".repeat(64)\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                debug!(\"SchemaEngine sled not available at /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat — using dev footprint\");\n                \"0\".repeat(64)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Inject Ghostbridge identity headers into a tonic Request.\n    fn inject_headers<T>(&self, mut req: Request<T>) -> Request<T> {\n        let footprint = Self::read_current_footprint();\n        if let Ok(val) = footprint.parse::<MetadataValue<_>>() {\n            req.metadata_mut().insert(\"x-ghostbridge-footprint\", val);\n        }\n        if let Ok(val) = self.trace_id.parse::<MetadataValue<_>>() {\n            req.metadata_mut().insert(\"x-ghostbridge-trace-id\", val);\n        }\n        req\n    }\n\n    /// Handle an MCP JSON-RPC request by routing it to the appropriate\n    /// op-grpc-bridge service and returning a JSON-RPC response.\n    pub async fn handle_mcp_request(&self, req: &OwnedValue) -> OwnedValue {\n        let method = req[\"method\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"\");\n        let id = req.get(\"id\").cloned().unwrap_or_else(OwnedValue::null);\n\n        match method {\n            // ── MCP Protocol Surface ──────────────────────────────────\n            \"initialize\" => self.handle_initialize(&id).await,\n            \"tools/list\" => self.handle_tools_list(&id).await,\n            \"tools/call\" => self.handle_tools_call(&id, req).await,\n\n            // ── State Operations ──────────────────────────────────────\n            \"state/get\" | \"getState\" => self.handle_get_state(&id, req).await,\n            \"state/mutate\" | \"mutate\" => self.handle_mutate(&id, req).await,\n\n            // ── Plugin Operations ─────────────────────────────────────\n            \"plugins/list\" | \"listPlugins\" => self.handle_list_plugins(&id).await,\n            \"plugins/schema\" | \"getSchema\" => self.handle_get_schema(&id, req).await,\n            \"plugins/call\" | \"callMethod\" => self.handle_call_method(&id, req).await,\n\n            // ── Event Chain ───────────────────────────────────────────\n            \"events/get\" | \"getEvents\" => self.handle_get_events(&id, req).await,\n            \"events/verify\" | \"verifyChain\" => self.handle_verify_chain(&id).await,\n\n            _ => {\n                warn!(\"Unknown MCP method forwarded to gRPC: {}\", method);\n                error_response(&id, -32601, format!(\"Method not found: {}\", method))\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n    // MCP Protocol Handlers\n    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n    async fn handle_initialize(&self, id: &OwnedValue) -> OwnedValue {\n        simd_json::json!({\n            \"jsonrpc\": \"2.0\",\n            \"id\": id.clone(),\n"}}

Today the crate cannot do any of (a)–(d): it has no `tags_touched[]` field, no schema-tag-aware validator, no sled-backed store, and no `X-Ghostbridge-*` headers on its SSE handler. Closing those gaps — together with consuming `op-state-store::SchemaEngine` instead of the local duplicate — is what turns `op-projection` into a real participant in the xray schema-tag routing pipeline rather than a generic, drift-prone JSON streamer.\ncrates/op-plugins/REVIEW.md:24:  no OSCAL plumbing yet).\ncrates/op-plugins/REVIEW.md:33:- **Blocks August 2, 2026 (EU AI Act) readiness?** Yes (no `control_refs`,\ncrates/op-plugins/REVIEW.md:123:- **OSCAL mapping:** none.\ncrates/op-plugins/REVIEW.md:138:- **OSCAL mapping:** none. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. PropertyDelete,\n    MethodCall,\n    Signal,\n    ObjectAdded,\n    ObjectRemoved,\n    SchemaMigration,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ChangeSource {\n    DBus,\n    Grpc,\n    Internal,\n}\n\npub struct SchemaEngine {\n    /// Authoritative Event Chain\n    pub event_chain: Arc<RwLock<EventChain>>,\n    /// Real-time change projection channel\n    change_tx: broadcast::Sender<StateChange>,\n    /// State cache for instant gRPC retrieval\n    state_cache: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, simd_json::OwnedValue>>>,\n    /// System D-Bus connection authority\n    pub dbus_connection: Arc<OnceCell<Connection>>,\n    /// Resource limiter for D-Bus operations\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    dbus_call_limiter: Arc<Semaphore>,\n\n    /// Authoritative RCP stores\n    pub ovsdb: Arc<OvsdbClient>,\n    pub nonnet: Arc<NonNetDb>,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Debug for SchemaEngine {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        f.debug_struct(\"SchemaEngine\").finish()\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl op_core::state_publisher::StatePublisher for SchemaEngine {\n    async fn publish_change(\n        &self,\n        plugin_id: String,\n        path: String,\n        change_type: op_core::state_publisher::ChangeType,\n        property: Option<String>,\n        old_value: Option<simd_json::OwnedValue>,\n        new_value: simd_json::OwnedValue,\n        tags: Vec<String>,\n        source: String,\n    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n        let internal_type = match change_type {\n            op_core::state_publisher::ChangeType::PropertySet => ChangeType::PropertySet,\n            op_core::state_publisher::ChangeType::Signal => ChangeType::Signal,\n            op_core::state_publisher::ChangeType::Deleted => ChangeType::ObjectRemoved,\n        };\n\n        self.process_authoritative_change(\n            plugin_id,\n            path,\n            internal_type,\n            property,\n            old_value,\n            new_value,\n            tags,\n            source,\n            ChangeSource::Internal,\n        )\n        .await\n        .map(|_| ())\n        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(e))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl SchemaEngine {\n    /// Create a new authoritative Schema Engine\n    pub fn new(\n        event_chain: Arc<RwLock<EventChain>>,\n        ovsdb: Arc<OvsdbClient>,\n        nonnet: Arc<NonNetDb>,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let (change_tx, _) = broadcast::channel(1024);\n        Self {\n            event_chain,\n            change_tx,\n            state_cache: Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new())),\n            dbus_connection: Arc::new(OnceCell::new()),\n            dbus_call_limiter: Arc::new(Semaphore::new(32)),\n            ovsdb,\n            nonnet,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Authoritative D-Bus connection getter\n    pub async fn dbus_connection(&self) -> anyhow::Result<Connection> {\n        self.dbus_connection\n            .get_or_try_init(|| async { Connection::system().await })\n            .await\n            .cloned()\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(e))\n    }\n\n    fn compute_tags(&self, plugin_id: &str, object_path: &str) -> Vec<String> {\n        let mut tags = Vec::new();\n        if plugin_id == \"net\" || object_path.contains(\"/ovsdb/\") {\n            tags.push(\"network\".to_string());\n            tags.push(\"ovsdb\".to_string());\n        } else if object_path.contains(\"/nonnet/\") {\n            tags.push(\"nonnet\".to_string());\n            tags.push(\"plugin\".to_string());\n        } else {\n            tags.push(\"state\".to_string());\n            tags.push(plugin_id.to_string());\n        }\n        tags\n    }\n\n    /// Process a change that has already happened in an authoritative store.\n    /// This records the change in the event chain and broadcasts it to gRPC.\n    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\n    pub async fn process_authoritative_change(\n        &self,\n        plugin_id: String,\n        object_path: String,\n        change_type: ChangeType,\n        member_name: Option<String>,\n        old_value: Option<simd_json::OwnedValue>,\n        new_value: simd_json::OwnedValue,\n        mut tags: Vec<String>,\n        actor_id: String,\n        source: ChangeSource,\n    ) -> Result<StateChange, String> {\n        if tags.is_empty() {\n            tags = self.compute_tags(&plugin_id, &object_path);\n        }\n\n        let event = {\n            let mut chain = self.event_chain.write().await;\n            let op = match change_type {\n                ChangeType::PropertySet => OperationType::PropertySet,\n                ChangeType::ObjectRemoved => OperationType::Custom(\"delete\".to_string()),\n                _ => OperationType::EmitSignal,\n            };\n            let event = chain.record(\n                actor_id.clone(),\n                plugin_id.clone(),\n                \"1.0.0\".to_string(),\n                op,\n                object_path.clone(),\n                tags.clone(),\n                Decision::Allow,\n                &new_value,\n            );\n            event.clone()\n        };\n\n        self.update_cached_plugin_state(\n            &plugin_id,\n            &object_path,\n            change_type,\n            member_name.as_deref(),\n            &new_value,\n        )\n        .await;\n\n        let change = StateChange {\n            change_id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),\n            event_id: event.event_id,\n            plugin_id,\n            object_path,\n            change_type,\n            member_name,\n            old_value,\n            new_value,\n            tags_touched: tags,\n            event_hash: event.event_hash.clone(),\n            timestamp: event.timestamp,\n            actor_id,\n            source,\n        };\n\n        let _ = self.change_tx.send(change.clone());\n        Ok(change)\n    }\n\n    /// Start the Schema Engine background tasks.\n    /// Subscribes to authoritative RCP stores and Today it does only half of that — `tags_touched` is an opaque `Vec<String>` populated by a hardcoded `compute_tags` ladder, and the `ChainEvent` broadcast (`OperationGrpcServer::chain_events`) is wired up but never sent to, so even the `SubscribeEvents` half of the streaming contract is dead. To make the chain real, this crate must (a) introduce a typed `XrayRouteService` whose `Materialize`/`Withdraw` RPCs read schema-validated `tags[]` and emit `ChainEvent`s carrying `tags_touched[]` and `subid` (`mut.network.xray-route.materialize@v1`); (b) extend `SubscribeRequest`/`SubscribeSignalsRequest`/`SubscribeEventsRequest` filters with a typed `tags[]` parameter bound to the `XrayRoute`/`PrivacyRoute` plugin-schema tag namespace (not free strings); (c) bridge `SchemaEngine::change_tx` → `OperationGrpcServer::chain_events` so every steer_v4 / ovsbr0 / Xray-rules materialization fires both a `StateChange` and a `ChainEvent`; and (d) add `actor_id`+`capability_id` enforcement so that only credentials carrying `cap.xray.route.materialize` can append `XrayRoute` rows. In the target chain (Brief §3) — `PluginSchema (XrayRoute/PrivacyRoute) → tag set → op-of-controller materialises → steer_v4 + OVS rules + xray routing.rules → EventChainService.ChainEvent → StateSync.StateChange` — every materialisation step must land as a `ChainEvent` recorded by *this* crate, with `tags_touched: Vec<Tag>` typed against the closed tag enum, `actor_id` = the op-of-controller identity, `capability_id` = the routing capability, `event_hash` Merkle-batched into the Snowball, and the resulting effective state hashed into `result_effective_hash`. Today the crate cannot do this: tags are free strings, the chain is RAM-only with MD5, the Shuttle does not actually subscribe to xray-route mutations and does not inject gRPC headers, and the SQLite shadow-cache means the UI's \"schema-backed flow state\" can drift from what the controller actually programmed into `steer_v4`. The crate must (1) close the `Tag` enum, (2) persist the chain through `/dev/shm` and the Btrfs blockchain, (3) expose `EventChainService.SubscribeChain` so `op-of-controller` and the UI consume the same hash-linked truth, and (4) inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` / `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` / `X-WireGuard-Pubkey` via a Tonic interceptor so every routing mutation has provable, auditable provenance.\n"}}

Scribe (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator)\n// The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes WireGuard identity\n// against the 1:1 PluginSchema in shared memory and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n\nuse chrono::Utc;\nuse memmap2::MmapOptions;\nuse sha2::{Digest, Sha256};\nuse std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};\nuse std::io::Write;\n\nuse crate::IdentitySled;\n\n/// THE SLED: 1:1 Zero-copy shared memory layout mapping directly to the SchemaEngine.\n/// This struct represents the absolute base schema as it exists in `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`.\n/// The SchemaEngine coordinates this memory space; if `is_valid` is false, the entity\n/// does not exist on the system.\n#[repr(C)]\npub struct PluginSchema {\n    pub wireguard_pubkey: [u8; 32],\n    pub mutation_index: u64,\n    pub is_valid: bool,\n    pub hashed_footprint: [u8; 32], // The vectorized \"Thought\"\n}\n\n/// The genesis \"Snowball\" session record, created by A.N.N.A. Scribe when a WireGuard\n/// connection arrives. This is the first entry in the accountability loop, tying the\n/// WireGuard pubkey to the current schema mutation state.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct SessionLedger {\n    pub wireguard_pubkey: String,\n    pub hashed_footprint: String, // The genesis \"Snowball\"\n    pub trace_id: String,\n}\n\n/// A.N.N.A. Scribe (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator)\n///\n/// The top-level gatekeeper who merges the ephemeral WireGuard identity with the\n/// absolute present state into a \"Snowball\" session. She relies strictly on the\n/// 1:1 `PluginSchema`. If the schema in memory is invalid, she refuses to generate\n/// the session identity — enforcing that without a valid schema, the entity does\n/// not exist on the system.\npub struct AnnaScribe;\n\nimpl AnnaScribe {\n    /// THE GREETING (Genesis Call)\n    ///\n    /// A.N.N.A. Scribe notarizes the WireGuard identity against the 1:1 memory schema.\n    /// She casts a raw pointer to the `PluginSchema` in shared memory, extracts the\n    /// `mutation_index`, and performs the **Strike/Etch** to generate the first hashed\n    /// footprint. This creates the **Identity Sled** (the Snowball) entirely in memory,\n    /// completely avoiding unintended Btrfs mutation loops while preserving NVMe I/O\n    /// strictly for the blockchain transport.\n    ///\n    /// Uses `md5::compute` to tie the WireGuard key to the current `mutation_index`,\n    /// directly matching the hashing methodology used by the Btrfs `EventChain`.\n    pub fn notarize_arrival(wg_pubkey: &str) -> Result<SessionLedger, String> {\n        // 1:1 Direct Read from the SchemaEngine's shared memory (No SQL, No Polling)\n        let file = File::open(\"/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat\")\n            .map_err(|_| \"A.N.N.A. Scribe: Missing Schema. Connection Rejected.\".to_string())?;\n\n        // Zero-copy cast into the absolute base schema\n        let mmap = unsafe {\n            MmapOptions::new()\n                .map(&file)\n                .map_err(|_| \"Memory map failed\".to_string())?\n        };\n        let schema_ptr = mmap.as_ptr() as *const PluginSchema;\n\n        let is_valid = unsafe { (*schema_ptr).is_valid };\n        let current_mutation = unsafe { (*schema_ptr).mutation_index };\n\n        // The Absolute Base: No valid schema, does not exist.\n        if !is_valid {\n            return Err(\"A.N.N.A. Scribe: Invalid Schema State. Cease and Desist.\".to_string());\n        }\n\n        // The Strike/Etch: Bind the WireGuard Key to the current mutation index\n        // to start the Snowball. Uses MD5 to maintain cryptographic continuity\n        // with the EventChain system.\n        let payload = format!(\"{}:{}\", wg_pubkey, current_mutation);\n        let genesis_hash = format!(\"{:x}\", md5::compute(payload.as_bytes()));\n\n        Ok(SessionLedger {\n            wireguard_pubkey: wg_pubkey.to_string(),\n            hashed_footprint: genesis_hash.clone(),\n            trace_id: format!(\"trace-{}\", genesis_hash),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// THE STRIKE/ETCH: Generates the cryptographic hash (footprint) for the identity.\n    /// This is used to notarize the session and lock in the 1:1 schema.\n    /// Uses SHA-256 for the high-fidelity footprint used in the Schema Shuttle loop.\n    pub fn etch_footprint(sled: &IdentitySled) -> [u8; 32] {\n        let mut hasher = Sha256::new();\n        hasher.update(sled.wireguard_pubkey);\n        hasher.update(sled.mutation_index.to_le_bytes());\n\n        let result = hasher.finalize();\n        let mut footprint = [0u8; 32];\n        footprint.copy_from_slice(&result);\n        footprint\n    }\n\n    /// THE SNOWBALL: Appends the session ledger.\n    /// Strictly preserved in RAM (tmpfs) to avoid Btrfs mutation loops.\n    /// NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport.\n    pub fn append_snowball(footprint: &[u8; 32], action: &str) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n        let timestamp = Utc::now().to_rfc3339();\n        let footprint_hex = hex::encode(footprint);\n        let entry = format!(\"[{}] {} | {}\\n\", timestamp, footprint_hex, action);\n\n        // Path is in tmpfs to preserve NVMe I/O for Btrfs blockchain transport\n        let snowball_path = \"/dev/shm/snowball_session.log\";\n\n        let mut file = OpenOptions::new()\n            .create(true)\n            .append(true)\n            .open(snowball_path)?;\n\n        file.write_all(entry.as_bytes())?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_notarize_arrival_rejects_missing_schema() {\n        // No /dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat by default in test env\n        // We test the error path directly: missing file => rejection\n        let result = AnnaScribe::notarize_arrival(\"test-pubkey-abc\");\n        assert!(result.is_err());\n        assert!(result\n            .unwrap_err()\n            .contains(\"Missing Schema. Connection Rejected\"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n"}}

lower.contains(needle))\n}\n\nfn simple_schema(\n    name: &str,\n    description: &str,\n    dependencies: &[&str],\n    fields: Vec<(&str, FieldSchema)>,\n) -> PluginSchema {\n    let mut builder = PluginSchema::builder(name)\n        .version(\"1.0.0\")\n        .description(description);\n    for dep in dependencies {\n        builder = builder.dependency(dep);\n    }\n    for (field_name, validate_field(name: &str, value: &Value, schema: &FieldSchema) -> Result<(), String> {\n    validate_value_against_type(name, value, &schema.field_type)?;\n\n    // Validate constraints\n    for constraint in &schema.constraints {\n        match constraint {\n            Constraint::Min { value: min } => {\n                if let Some(n) = value.as_f64() {\n                    if n < *min {\n                        return Err(format!(\"Field '{}' must be >= {}\", name, min));\n                    }\n                }\n                if let Some(s) = value.as_str() {\n Constraint::Max { value: max } => {\n                if let Some(n) = value.as_f64() {\n                    if n > *max {\n                        return Err(format!(\"Field '{}' must be <= {}\", name, max));\n                    }\n                }\n                if let Some(s) = value.as_str() {\n                    if (s.len() as f64) > *max {\n                        return Err(format!(\"Field '{}' length must be <= {}\", name, max));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Constraint::Pattern { regex } => {\n                if let Some(s) = value.as_str() {\n                    if let Ok(re) = regex::Regex::new(regex) {\n                        if !re.is_match(s) {\n                            return Err(format!(\"Field '{}' must match pattern: {}\", name, regex));\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Constraint::OneOf { values } if !values.contains(value) => {\n                return Err(format!(\"Field '{}' must be one of: {:?}\", name, values));\n            }\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn validate_value_against_type(\n    name: &str,\n    value: &Value,\n    field_type: &FieldType,\n) -> Result<(), String> {\n    match field_type {\n        FieldType::String => {\n            if !value.is_str() {\n                return Err(format!(\"Field '{}' must be a string\", name));\n            }\n        }\n        FieldType::Integer => {\n            if !value.is_i64() && !value.is_u64() {\n                return Err(format!(\"Field '{}' must be an integer\", name));\n            }\n        }\n        FieldType::Float => {\n            if !value.is_f64() && !value.is_i64() {\n                return Err(format!(\"Field '{}' must be a number\", name));\n            }\n        }\n        FieldType::Boolean => {\n            if !value.is_bool() {\n                return Err(format!(\"Field '{}' must be a boolean\", name));\n            }\n        }\n        FieldType::Array(_) => {\n            if !value.is_array() {\n                return Err(format!(\"Field '{}' must be an array\", name));\n            }\n            if let Some(items) = value.as_array() {\n                if let FieldType::Array(item_type) = field_type {\n                    for (index, item) in items.iter().enumerate() {\n                        validate_value_against_type(\n                            &format!(\"{}[{}]\", name, index),\n                            item,\n                            item_type,\n                        )?;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        FieldType::Object(fields) => {\n            if !value.is_object() {\n                return Err(format!(\"Field '{}' must be an object\", name));\n            }\n            validate_object_fields(name, value, fields)?;\n        }\n"}}
