Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n"}},"realtime_active":false,"effort":"medium","summary":"none","user_instructions":"### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}

Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. {"timestamp":"2026-05-22T04:56:24.996Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Here’s the current state, split the way the work actually landed.\n\n**Network**\n- The gRPC path is live inside the `wg-xray` container on `10.200.0.2:50051`.\n- `grpcurl` is installed there and reflection works, so the bridge is discoverable and callable.\n- Auth is still enforced the way we want: unauthenticated calls are rejected by A.N.N.A. Scribe, and authenticated calls with `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` plus `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` succeed.\n- Xray is running in the container and listening on the expected ports, including `:443` and the local SOCKS/MCP ports.\n- The host/container veth setup was rebuilt and corrected so the host side and container side are cleanly separated, with the host using `grpc-uplink` and the container using `grpc-phys`.\n- The OVS/AF_XDP path was moved away from shell-scripted `ip`/`ovs-vsctl` style setup toward native Rust helpers.\n- Old mistrial services were pruned or recycled instead of staying in the active `s6` tree, and the network bring-up scripts are being normalized around the rebuilt topology.\n\n**Schema**\n- I added an OSCAL-style header directly onto `op-state-store::PluginSchema`.\n- That header now includes:\n  - `uuid`\n  - `subid`\n  - `control_source`\n  - `control_refs`\n  - `statement_refs`\n- `PluginSchemaBuilder` now supports setting those fields explicitly.\n- If they are omitted, the builder normalizes them automatically:\n  - `uuid` is derived deterministically from `category + name + version`\n  - `subid` is derived as `sch.<category>.<name>@v<major>`\n  - `control_source` defaults to `NIST_SP_800_53_R5`\n- `SchemaRegistry::register()` also normalizes direct schema literals, so old-style schema construction doesn’t bypass the header.\n- I added regression tests for:\n  - build-time header normalization\n  - direct-literal normalization through the registry\n- I also threaded the new header into the Qdrant semantic shuttle render path, so the schema embedding text now includes:\n  - `schema_uuid`\n  - `schema_subid`\n  - `control_source`\n  - `control_refs`\n  - `statement_refs`\n\n**Verification**\n- `cargo check -p op-state-store -p op-cognitive-mcp -p op-plugins` passed.\n- `cargo test -p op-state-store --lib` passed.\n\n**Git**\n- The local commit exists as `d4b6c456` with message `Add OSCAL headers to plugin schemas`.\n- Push is still blocked by repository auth on the current machine because the remote is HTTPS and Git can’t prompt for credentials in this environment.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n"}},"realtime_active":false,"effort":"medium","summary":"none","user_instructions":"### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-05-22T04:57:17.782Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"The header is the identity layer; the tags are the routing layer.\n\nWhat I changed gives every `PluginSchema` a stable OSCAL-like identity:\n- `uuid`: stable schema identity\n- `subid`: human-meaningful stable schema ID\n- `control_source`: where the compliance mapping comes from\n- `control_refs` / `statement_refs`: the audit/control links\n\nThat does **not** replace tag-based routing. It makes tag-based routing auditable and stable.\n\nThe flow should work like this:\n\n1. A plugin schema is loaded or built.\n2. The schema is normalized, so it always has a header.\n3. The router looks at `schema.tags` plus the route-specific fields on schemas like `XrayRoute` or `PrivacyRoute`.\n4. Those tags decide the actual routing behavior:\n   - Xray `routing.rules`\n   - OpenFlow entries on `ovsbr0`\n   - XDP steering state\n5. The emitted runtime records carry the schema header back along with the route action:\n   - `schema_uuid`\n   - `schema_subid`\n   - `tags_touched`\n   - `actor_id`\n   - `capability_id`\n   - `event_hash`\n\nSo the tags say **where traffic goes**. The header says **which schema authorized it, which revision it came from, and what compliance controls it satisfies**.\n\nPractically, this means:\n- `tags` remain the selector for routing decisions.\n- `subid` becomes the stable reference used in events, logs, and materialization records.\n- `uuid` is the immutable identity for the schema object itself.\n- `control_refs` are for evidence and governance, not for packet steering.\n\nThe important architectural consequence is that route materialization is no longer “some tags happened to produce some rules.” It becomes:\n- schema header identifies the source,\n- tags define the policy,\n- route controller materializes the policy,\n- event chain records the result.\n\nThat is the bridge from schema-as-data to schema-driven routing.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. {"timestamp":"2026-05-22T04:59:45.825Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes. That is the right mental model.\n\nThe `PluginSchema` header is the anchor. The tags are the intersection layer between:\n- what the schema says exists\n- what the router is allowed to materialize\n- what the runtime emits as evidence\n\nSo the schema is not just a description document. It becomes the canonical object that:\n- declares the route-relevant tags\n- carries the stable identity for that object\n- carries the compliance trail for that object\n- gives the controller something deterministic to project into Xray/OpenFlow/XDP\n\nHow it gets used:\n\n1. **Schema admission**\n   - A plugin schema is built or loaded.\n   - The OSCAL header is normalized.\n   - That gives the object a stable `uuid` and `subid`.\n\n2. **Schema-to-route selection**\n   - The route controller inspects `schema.tags`.\n   - It compares those tags with route schemas like `XrayRoute` or `PrivacyRoute`.\n   - The intersection of those sets determines what should be materialized.\n   - Example: a schema with `[\"uds\", \"mail\", \"egress\"]` intersects a route schema that targets `[\"mail\", \"egress\"]`.\n\n3. **Materialization**\n   - The controller converts that intersection into actual runtime state:\n     - Xray routing rules\n     - OpenFlow flows\n     - XDP steering\n   - This is where tags stop being abstract labels and become programmable intent.\n\n4. **Identity injection**\n   - Every emitted action or event carries the schema header back out:\n     - `schema_uuid`\n     - `schema_subid`\n     - `control_refs`\n     - `statement_refs`\n   - That means the runtime rule is traceable to the exact schema object that authorized it.\n\n5. **Audit and replay**\n   - If a route changes later, you can compare:\n     - what schema was active\n     - which tags matched\n     - what materialization happened\n     - which actor/capability caused it\n   - That is what makes the schema the cornerstone instead of just a config blob.\n\nSo the clean way to say it is:\n\n- **Tags** decide routing.\n- **Schema header** decides identity.\n- **The intersection of schema tags and route tags** decides what gets programmed.\n- **The emitted identity metadata** proves why it was programmed.\n\nThat is why the schema is the cornerstone. It is the stable thing everything else hangs off of. The routing layer should never invent identity on its own; it should only consume schema identity and schema tags, then project them into the network stack.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-05-22T05:00:32.352Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes. The identity injection is the part where the schema stops being passive and becomes the source for outbound metadata.\n\nSpecifically:\n\n1. **Schema is loaded**\n   - `PluginSchema` now carries `uuid`, `subid`, `control_source`, `control_refs`, `statement_refs`.\n\n2. **Router resolves the match**\n   - It intersects `schema.tags` with the route tags from something like `XrayRoute` or `PrivacyRoute`.\n   - That decides whether this object is eligible for a route.\n\n3. **Identity is stamped at the boundary**\n   - The proxy / bridge layer injects identity into the outbound call context.\n   - Today that is already partly happening as:\n     - `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`\n     - `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID`\n   - The missing piece is the schema-linked identity becoming part of that same injection path, usually as one of:\n     - `schema_subid`\n     - `schema_uuid`\n     - `X-WireGuard-Pubkey` when the route is bound to a peer\n\n4. **Materialization uses the schema identity**\n   - The route controller records that the emitted Xray/OpenFlow/XDP action came from a specific schema identity.\n   - That means the runtime rule is not just “tag matched.” It is “tag matched under schema `subid` X, version Y, controls Z.”\n\nSo the schema is not injected directly into packets. The schema is the authority that tells the injection layer:\n- which identity to stamp,\n- which peer to bind,\n- which route to materialize,\n- which audit headers to carry.\n\nThe clean model is:\n\n- `PluginSchema` = authoritative identity and policy anchor\n- `tags` = routing selectors\n- interceptor / proxy = identity injector\n- Xray/OpenFlow/XDP = consumers of the injected identity and materialized tags\n\nIf you want the strictest version of this, the outbound metadata should carry both:\n- the live transport identity: `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`, footprint, trace ID\n- the schema identity: `schema_uuid`, `schema_subid`\n\nThat gives you both sides of the chain:\n- who the connection is\n- what schema authorized the route\n\nThat is the specific role of identity injection here.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

The schema is the authority that tells the injection layer:\n- which identity to stamp,\n- which peer to bind,\n- which route to materialize,\n- which audit headers to carry.\n\nThe clean model is:\n\n- `PluginSchema` = authoritative identity and policy anchor\n- `tags` = routing selectors\n- interceptor / proxy = identity injector\n- Xray/OpenFlow/XDP = consumers of the injected identity and materialized tags\n\nIf you want the strictest version of this, the outbound metadata should carry both:\n- the live transport identity: `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`, footprint, trace ID\n- the schema identity: `schema_uuid`, `schema_subid`\n\nThat gives you both sides of the chain:\n- who the connection is\n- what schema authorized the route\n\nThat is the specific role of identity injection here."}],"phase":"final_answer"}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. {"timestamp":"2026-05-22T05:03:03.064Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_UbRfCrruW19STjQUGPJlHbDT","output":"Chunk ID: b0a144\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1218\nOutput:\n# Network Source Of Truth\n\nThis folder documents the rebuilt network stack as it exists after the Btrfs\nvolume loss and ground-up network rebuild. Treat live s6 service definitions,\nlive Incus configuration, and live OVS/Xray state as the operational source of\ntruth. Older repo scripts and snapshots are historical unless they match the\nlive topology described here.\n\n## Current Topology\n\nThe active data path is:\n\n1. Host `eth0` provides the public uplink.\n2. Host OVS runs `ovsdb-server` and `ovs-vswitchd` under s6.\n3. `ovsbr0` is the OVS bridge boundary.\n4. The gRPC veth pair is `grpc-uplink` on the host and `grpc-phys` as the peer\n   consumed by Incus.\n5. Incus attaches `grpc-phys` to the `wg-xray` container as `eth0`.\n6. Inside `wg-xray`, the visible NIC is `eth0`, not `grpc-phys`.\n7. Xray owns gRPC routing for containers. OVS/OpenFlow and XDP own steering and\n   obfuscation policy.\n\nConfirmed live naming:\n\n| Role | Live name |\n| --- | --- |\n| Host uplink | `eth0` |\n| OVS bridge | `ovsbr0` |\n| Host gRPC veth end | `grpc-uplink` |\n| Incus-consumed veth peer | `grpc-phys` |\n| Container | `wg-xray` |\n| Container-visible gRPC NIC | `eth0` |\n\nNames such as `grpc-pipe`, `grpc-bridge`, `grpc-uplink0`, and `vop-br0` belong\nto older experiments unless live s6 or live Incus state reintroduces them.\n\n## Native Replacement Crates\n\nThe rebuilt stack should not rely on shell helpers such as `ovs-vsctl`,\n`ovs-ofctl`, `ovsdb-client`, raw `socat` JSON-RPC, or ad hoc `ip` commands for\nservice logic. The replacement crates are:\n\n| Old surface | Replacement |\n| --- | --- |\n| `ovsdb-client transact ...` | `op-ovsdb` backed by `rovs-ovsdb` |\n| raw OVSDB JSON-RPC over `socat` | `rovs-ovsdb` through `rovs-jsonrpc` and `rovs-transport` |\n| `ovs-vsctl add-br`, `add-port`, `set Interface`, `list-ports` | `op-ovsdb::OvsdbClient` typed methods |\n| `ovs-ofctl add-flow`, `del-flows`, `dump-flows` | `op-network::openflow` backed by `rovs-openflow` |\n| `ip link`, `ip addr`, `ip route` | `op-network::rtnetlink` |\n| `ip link ... xdp` | `op-network::xdp` backed by `libbpf-rs` |\n\n`op-ovsdb` is the main OVSDB replacement. It uses `rovs-ovsdb` for persistent\nUnix socket connections, native `transact`, typed `Transaction` builders, and an\nIDL-backed in-memory OVSDB replica. This replaces both `ovsdb-client` and most\n`ovs-vsctl` usage.\n\n`op-network::openflow` is the OpenFlow replacement. It re-exports\n`rovs-openflow`, including `VConn`, `Flow`, `Match`, `ActionList`,\n`FlowStatsRequest`, `PacketIn`, and `PacketOut`. This replaces `ovs-ofctl`\nmechanics. The owner process still matters: the target architecture keeps Xray\nas the routing controller, with OpenFlow messages emitted over the Xray-owned\ncontroller path rather than an ad hoc TCP controller.\n\n## Known Gaps Before Full Cutover\n\n`ovs-vsctl --no-wait init` is still present in the live `ovs-vswitchd` s6\nservice. `op-ovsdb::ensure_initialized()` currently verifies connectivity and\nwarns when the `Open_vSwitch` root table is empty, but it does not yet create\nthe initial root row. Add a native root-row initializer before removing that\nlast `ovs-vsctl` call.\n\n`bpftool map update` replacement is not confirmed yet. `op-network::xdp` covers\nnative XDP program load, attach, and detach. If any live service updates BPF\nmaps, add or identify a native map writer before deleting the shell path.\n\n`op-of-controller` exists as a Rust binary using `rovs-openflow`, but live\narchitecture needs confirmation before it is treated as the controller of\nrecord. Current intent is that Xray owns gRPC routing and OpenFlow policy\nmaterialization.\n\n## s6 Cleanup Rules\n\nActive s6 services should be small launchers for native binaries. They should\nnot contain OVSDB JSON payloads, OpenFlow command strings, or imperative network\nsetup logic that belongs in Rust.\n\nKeep only services needed for the live topology. Disabled mistrials should be\narchived or removed after confirming they are not referenced by the active\ns6-rc database.\n\nDescriptive service names should identify the thing being managed:\n\n| Current or proposed name | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `ovsdb-server` | OVSDB daemon |\n| `ovs-vswitchd` | OVS switch daemon |\n| `ovsbr0-afxdp` | `ovsbr0` plus AF_XDP uplink bootstrap |\n| `ovs-vethpair` | host/container gRPC veth pair bootstrap |\n| `xray-routing` | Xray routing controller service, if moved into s6 |\n| `grpc-identity-bridge` | Rust gRPC bridge service, if moved into s6 |\n\n## Next Documentation Files\n\nPlanned files for this folder:\n\n| File | Purpose |\n| --- | --- |\n| `live-topology.md` | Exact live addresses, interfaces, routes, and container mapping |\n| `s6-services.md` | Active s6 service graph and cleanup decisions |\n| `native-replacements.md` | Command-by-command migration from shell helpers to Rust crates |\n| `xray-openflow.md` | Xray, OpenFlow table A/B, and obfuscation steering contract |\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-05-22T05:03:14.489Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call","status":"completed","call_id":"call_KmhRfcbdHIs95o6LAJfVKNgY","name":"apply_patch","input":"*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/docs/network/schema-routing-handoff.md\n+# Schema Routing Handoff\n+\n+This document captures the current working model for the rebuilt network stack:\n+how `PluginSchema` becomes the identity sled baseline, how tags participate in\n+routing, and how identity is injected at the gRPC boundary.\n+\n+## Core Model\n+\n+`PluginSchema` is the anchor. Its OSCAL-style header is the stable metadata that\n+identifies the schema object itself:\n+\n+- `uuid`: immutable schema identity\n+- `subid`: stable human-readable schema id\n+- `control_source`: compliance family source\n+- `control_refs`: control mappings for evidence\n+- `statement_refs`: narrative or policy references\n+\n+That header is not the routing decision. It is the baseline metadata for the\n+identity sled and the provenance layer that follows every materialization.\n+\n+## Tag-Based Routing\n+\n+Tags are the intersection between schema intent and route intent.\n+\n+The route controller should compare:\n+\n+- `schema.tags`\n+- route tags carried by schemas such as `XrayRoute` and `PrivacyRoute`\n+\n+The intersection determines whether a route is eligible for materialization.\n+Once eligible, the controller can project that route into:\n+\n+- Xray routing rules\n+- OpenFlow rules on `ovsbr0`\n+- XDP steering state\n+\n+So the flow is:\n+\n+1. Load and normalize the schema.\n+2. Resolve the relevant tag intersection.\n+3. Materialize the route into live network state.\n+4. Emit the result with schema identity attached.\n+\n+## Identity Injection\n+\n+Identity injection happens at the boundary, not inside the packet path.\n+\n+The live transport identity currently includes:\n+\n+- `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`\n+- `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID`\n+\n+The target model adds schema identity to the same boundary record so the route\n+can be traced back to the schema that authorized it.\n+\n+That means the injected metadata should carry both:\n+\n+- live transport identity: WireGuard pubkey, footprint, trace id\n+- schema identity: `schema_uuid`, `schema_subid`\n+\n+This is the right split:\n+\n+- schema decides what exists\n+- tags decide what can route\n+- the injector stamps identity at the gRPC edge\n+- Xray/OpenFlow/XDP consume the materialized result\n+\n+## What Changed Already\n+\n+The codebase now has:\n+\n+- OSCAL header fields on `op-state-store::PluginSchema`\n+- deterministic normalization during schema build and registry registration\n+- Qdrant shuttle rendering that includes the new schema header fields\n+\n+That makes the schema usable as the provenance anchor for later routing work.\n+\n+## Current Interpretation\n+\n+The clean mental model is:\n+\n+- `PluginSchema` header = identity sled baseline metadata\n+- `schema.tags` = route selection surface\n+- route schemas = steering intent\n+- injector = metadata carrier at the boundary\n+- network backends = projection targets\n+\n+The schema is the cornerstone. The tags are the overlap between schema and\n+routing policy. The live identity injection is the proof that the route came\n+from that schema.\n+\n+## Next Step\n+\n+The next implementation layer should teach the route controller to read the\n+schema header and tag set together, then emit route materializations with the\n+schema identity attached to each event.\n*** Update File: /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/docs/network/README.md\n@@\n | File | Purpose |\n | --- | --- |\n+| `schema-routing-handoff.md` | Current model for schema identity, tag-based routing, and boundary identity injection |\n | `live-topology.md` | Exact live addresses, interfaces, routes, and container mapping |\n | `s6-services.md` | Active s6 service graph and cleanup decisions |\n | `native-replacements.md` | Command-by-command migration from shell helpers to Rust crates |\n | `xray-openflow.md` | Xray, OpenFlow table A/B, and obfuscation steering contract |\n*** End Patch\n"}}
{"timestamp":"2026-05-22T05:03:14.499Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"patch_apply_end","call_id":"call_KmhRfcbdHIs95o6LAJfVKNgY","turn_id":"019e4e10-aaf4-7931-aeca-b1394d72da8d","stdout":"Success. Updated the following files:\nA /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/docs/network/schema-routing-handoff.md\nM /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/docs/network/README.md\n","stderr":"","success":true,"changes":{"/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/docs/network/README.md":{"type":"update","unified_diff":"@@ -107,2 +107,3 @@\n | --- | --- |\n+| `schema-routing-handoff.md` | Current model for schema identity, tag-based routing, and boundary identity injection |\n | `live-topology.md` | Exact live addresses, interfaces, routes, and container mapping |\n","move_path":null},"/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/docs/network/schema-routing-handoff.md":{"type":"add","content":"# Schema Routing Handoff\n\nThis document captures the current working model for the rebuilt network stack:\nhow `PluginSchema` becomes the identity sled baseline, how tags participate in\nrouting, and how identity is injected at the gRPC boundary.\n\n## Core Model\n\n`PluginSchema` is the anchor. Its OSCAL-style header is the stable metadata that\nidentifies the schema object itself:\n\n- `uuid`: immutable schema identity\n- `subid`: stable human-readable schema id\n- `control_source`: compliance family source\n- `control_refs`: control mappings for evidence\n- `statement_refs`: narrative or policy references\n\nThat header is not the routing decision. It is the baseline metadata for the\nidentity sled and the provenance layer that follows every materialization.\n\n## Tag-Based Routing\n\nTags are the intersection between schema intent and route intent.\n\nThe route controller should compare:\n\n- `schema.tags`\n- route tags carried by schemas such as `XrayRoute` and `PrivacyRoute`\n\nThe intersection determines whether a route is eligible for materialization.\nOnce eligible, the controller can project that route into:\n\n- Xray routing rules\n- OpenFlow rules on `ovsbr0`\n- XDP steering state\n\nSo the flow is:\n\n1. Load and normalize the schema.\n2. Resolve the relevant tag intersection.\n3. Materialize the route into live network state.\n4. Emit the result with schema identity attached.\n\n## Identity Injection\n\nIdentity injection happens at the boundary, not inside the packet path.\n\nThe live transport identity currently includes:\n\n- `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`\n- `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID`\n\nThe target model adds schema identity to the same boundary record so the route\ncan be traced back to the schema that authorized it.\n\nThat means the injected metadata should carry both:\n\n- live transport identity: WireGuard pubkey, footprint, trace id\n- schema identity: `schema_uuid`, `schema_subid`\n\nThis is the right split:\n\n- schema decides what exists\n- tags decide what can route\n- the injector stamps identity at the gRPC edge\n- Xray/OpenFlow/XDP consume the materialized result\n\n## What Changed Already\n\nThe codebase now has:\n\n- OSCAL header fields on `op-state-store::PluginSchema`\n- deterministic normalization during schema build and registry registration\n- Qdrant shuttle rendering that includes the new schema header fields\n\nThat makes the schema usable as the provenance anchor for later routing work.\n\n## Current Interpretation\n\nThe clean mental model is:\n\n- `PluginSchema` header = identity sled baseline metadata\n- `schema.tags` = route selection surface\n- route schemas = steering intent\n- injector = metadata carrier at the boundary\n- network backends = projection targets\n\nThe schema is the cornerstone. The tags are the overlap between schema and\nrouting policy. The live identity injection is the proof that the route came\nfrom that schema.\n\n## Next Step\n\nThe next implementation layer should teach the route controller to read the\nschema header and tag set together, then emit route materializations with the\nschema identity attached to each event.\n"}},"status":"completed"}}

Today it does only half of that — `tags_touched` is an opaque `Vec<String>` populated by a hardcoded `compute_tags` ladder, and the `ChainEvent` broadcast (`OperationGrpcServer::chain_events`) is wired up but never sent to, so even the `SubscribeEvents` half of the streaming contract is dead. To make the chain real, this crate must (a) introduce a typed `XrayRouteService` whose `Materialize`/`Withdraw` RPCs read schema-validated `tags[]` and emit `ChainEvent`s carrying `tags_touched[]` and `subid` (`mut.network.xray-route.materialize@v1`); (b) extend `SubscribeRequest`/`SubscribeSignalsRequest`/`SubscribeEventsRequest` filters with a typed `tags[]` parameter bound to the `XrayRoute`/`PrivacyRoute` plugin-schema tag namespace (not free strings); (c) bridge `SchemaEngine::change_tx` → `OperationGrpcServer::chain_events` so every steer_v4 / ovsbr0 / Xray-rules materialization fires both a `StateChange` and a `ChainEvent`; and (d) add `actor_id`+`capability_id` enforcement so that only credentials carrying `cap.xray.route.materialize` can append `XrayRoute` rows. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. };\n    let ptr = mmap.as_ptr() as *const IdentitySled;\n    Ok((ptr, mmap))\n}\n\n// ── Xray config generator ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nfn write_xray_config(\n    footprint: &str,\n    trace_id: &str,\n    nextdns_profile: &str,\n    uuid: &str,\n    private_key: &str,\n    short_id: &str,\n) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    // WireGuard identity is read into the sled before this config is written.\n    // Xray is the carrier: it stamps outbound metadata and routes DNS over DoH.\n    let config = format!(\n        r#\"{{\n  \"log\": {{ \"loglevel\": \"warning\" }},\n  \"dns\": {{\n    \"servers\": [ \"https://dns.nextdns.io/{profile}/Ghostbridge-Incus\" ],\n    \"tag\": \"nextdns-in\"\n  }},\n  \"inbounds\": [\n    {{\n      \"tag\": \"reality-in\",\n      \"port\": 443,\n      \"listen\": \"0.0.0.0\",\n      \"protocol\": \"vless\",\n      \"settings\": {{\n        \"clients\": [{{ \"id\": \"{uuid}\", \"flow\": \"xtls-rprx-vision\" }}],\n        \"decryption\": \"none\"\n      }},\n      \"streamSettings\": {{\n        \"network\": \"tcp\",\n        \"security\": \"reality\",\n        \"realitySettings\": {{\n          \"show\": false,\n          \"dest\": \"www.microsoft.com:443\",\n          \"serverNames\": [\"www.microsoft.com\"],\n          \"privateKey\": \"{private_key}\",\n          \"shortIds\": [\"{short_id}\"]\n        }}\n      }}\n    }},\n    {{\n      \"tag\": \"ovs-socks-in\",\n      \"port\": 1080,\n      \"listen\": \"10.88.88.1\",\n      \"protocol\": \"socks\",\n      \"settings\": {{ \"auth\": \"noauth\", \"udp\": true }}\n"}}

Stamp into environment — zero Btrfs, zero disk I/O\n    env::set_var(\"GB_FOOTPRINT\", &footprint_hex);\n    env::set_var(\"GB_TRACE_ID\", &trace_id);\n\n    // 4. {"timestamp":"2026-05-22T05:12:37.878Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"I couldn’t check the live Incus container from this shell because the Incus socket is permission-locked here, but the checked-in config is clear.\n\nThe intended WireGuard DNS is **NextDNS first, with fallbacks currently still present**:\n\n- `wg0.service` sets DNS on the interface to `45.90.28.38` and `45.90.30.38` first, then falls back to `1.1.1.1` and `8.8.8.8`:\n  - [wg0.service](</home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/deploy/wg-xray-configs/wg0.service:16>)\n- The Xray config generator uses **NextDNS DoH directly**:\n  - [schema_bridge.rs](</home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-identity/src/schema_bridge.rs:89>)\n  - [schema_bridge.rs](</home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-identity/src/schema_bridge.rs:327>)\n\nSo the answer is:\n\n- **Yes, NextDNS is in the intended path.**\n- **No, the WireGuard service is not NextDNS-only right now.** It still includes Cloudflare and Google as fallback resolvers.\n\nIf your laptop is still having DNS trouble over WireGuard, the likely culprits are:\n1. the client is not accepting pushed DNS,\n2. the client config is overriding DNS locally,\n3. the container’s interface DNS is falling back instead of staying pinned to NextDNS,\n4. or the laptop is resolving outside the tunnel and never hitting this path.\n\nThe one thing I can say confidently from the repo is that the clean NextDNS-only target is already present in Xray, but the WireGuard service is still mixed.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-05-22T05:12:37.882Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"I couldn’t check the live Incus container from this shell because the Incus socket is permission-locked here, but the checked-in config is clear.\n\nThe intended WireGuard DNS is **NextDNS first, with fallbacks currently still present**:\n\n- `wg0.service` sets DNS on the interface to `45.90.28.38` and `45.90.30.38` first, then falls back to `1.1.1.1` and `8.8.8.8`:\n  - [wg0.service](</home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/deploy/wg-xray-configs/wg0.service:16>)\n- The Xray config generator uses **NextDNS DoH directly**:\n  - [schema_bridge.rs](</home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-identity/src/schema_bridge.rs:89>)\n  - [schema_bridge.rs](</home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-identity/src/schema_bridge.rs:327>)\n\nSo the answer is:\n\n- **Yes, NextDNS is in the intended path.**\n- **No, the WireGuard service is not NextDNS-only right now.** It still includes Cloudflare and Google as fallback resolvers.\n\nIf your laptop is still having DNS trouble over WireGuard, the likely culprits are:\n1. the client is not accepting pushed DNS,\n2. the client config is overriding DNS locally,\n3. the container’s interface DNS is falling back instead of staying pinned to NextDNS,\n4. or the laptop is resolving outside the tunnel and never hitting this path.\n\nThe one thing I can say confidently from the repo is that the clean NextDNS-only target is already present in Xray, but the WireGuard service is still mixed."}],"phase":"final_answer"}}

The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via Assistant Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n*   **Important:** Always execute npm commands within the specified subdirectories; never run them in the root directory.\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}

That means the sled has to be enough on its own to authenticate and stamp:\n- `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`\n- `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID`\n- `schema_uuid`\n- `schema_subid`\n\nSo the clean split is:\n\n- **Short term:** keep WireGuard, let Xray do routing and header injection.\n- **Later:** if the sled is fully authoritative and the injector can derive trusted identity without `wg_pubkey`, then WireGuard can be removed from the runtime path.\n\nThe important constraint is this: you cannot remove WireGuard just because Xray is present. {"timestamp":"2026-05-22T05:15:02.339Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes, that is the right layering.\n\nWireGuard is the doorman:\n- it admits the client\n- gives you the peer identity\n- establishes the trusted entry point\n\nAfter that, Xray becomes the carrier:\n- it forwards the request onward\n- injects the boundary metadata\n- routes to gRPC\n- the WireGuard transport itself is no longer part of the internal path\n\nSo the clean model is:\n\n1. **WireGuard ingress**\n   - authenticate the peer\n   - establish trust\n   - derive the live transport identity\n\n2. **Xray boundary**\n   - stamp `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`\n   - stamp `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID`\n   - stamp schema identity when available\n   - apply routing policy\n\n3. **gRPC backend**\n   - receives forwarded calls\n   - never needs to know about WireGuard transport details directly\n\nThat means WireGuard is not the application path. It is the entrance. Once traffic is inside Xray, the protocol boundary shifts and WireGuard is effectively left behind.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

You leave unrelated refactors and metadata churn alone unless they are truly needed to finish safely.\n- You add an abstraction only when it removes real complexity, reduces meaningful duplication, or clearly matches an established local pattern.\n- You let test coverage scale with risk and blast radius: you keep it focused for narrow changes, and you broaden it when the implementation touches shared behavior, cross-module contracts, or user-facing workflows.\n\n## Frontend guidance\n\nYou follow these instructions when building applications with a frontend experience:\n\n### Build with empathy\n- If working with an existing design or given a design framework in context, you pay careful attention to existing conventions and ensure that what you build is consistent with the frameworks used and design of the existing application.\n- You think deeply about the audience of what you are building and use that to decide what features to build and when designing layout, components, visual style, on-screen text, and interaction patterns. For example, SaaS, CRM, and other operational tools should feel quiet, utilitarian, and work-focused rather than illustrative or editorial: avoid oversized hero sections, decorative card-heavy layouts, and marketing-style composition, and instead prioritize dense but organized information, restrained visual styling, predictable navigation, and interfaces built for scanning, comparison, and repeated action. A game can be more illustrative, expressive, animated, and playful.\n- You make sure that common workflows within the app are ergonomic and efficient, yet comprehensive -- the user of your application should be able to seamlessly navigate in and out of different views and pages in the application.\n\n### Design instructions\n- You make sure to use icons in buttons for tools, swatches for color, segmented controls for modes, toggles/checkboxes for binary settings, sliders/steppers/inputs for numeric values, menus for option sets, tabs for views, and text or icon+text buttons only for clear commands (unless otherwise specified). The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Safe to re-run.\n# After running, reboot to verify the full boot sequence.\nset -eu\n\nREPO=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/..\" && pwd)\"\nlog() { printf '\\033[1;32m[apply]\\033[0m %s\\n' \"$*\"; }\ndie() { printf '\\033[1;31m[ERROR]\\033[0m %s\\n' \"$*\" >&2; exit 1; }\n\n[ \"$(id -u)\" = 0 ] || die \"run as root (sudo sh deploy/apply-afxdp-boot.sh)\"\n\n# ── 1. Recompile s6-rc database ──────────────────────────────────────────────\nlog \"recompiling s6-rc database\"\ntmp=\"$(mktemp -d)\"\ns6-rc-compile \"$tmp/db\" /etc/s6/sv /etc/s6/adminsv\ns6-rc-db -c \"$tmp/db\" check && log \"database check passed\"\nstamp=\"$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)\"\n[ -e /etc/s6/rc/compiled ] && mv /etc/s6/rc/compiled \"/etc/s6/rc/compiled.prev-${stamp}\" || true\ncp -a \"$tmp/db\" /etc/s6/rc/compiled\nrm -rf \"$tmp\"\nlog \"s6-rc database updated\"\n\nlog \"\"\nlog \"===== Done =====\"\nlog \"Boot sequence after reboot:\"\nlog \"  ovsbr0-setup   — creates OVS bridge (ovs-vswitchd dependency)\"\nlog \"  ovsbr0-netdev-verify — confirms ovsbr0 stayed netdev\"\nlog \"  ovsbr0-static  — sets 148.113.204.83/32 on ovsbr0, default route onlink\"\nlog \"  ovsbr0-afxdp   — adds eth0 as AF_XDP (IP already on bridge, no gap)\"\nlog \"\"\nlog \"To test NOW without rebooting:\"\nlog \"  sh /etc/s6/sv/ovsbr0-static/shell_up\"\nlog \"  /usr/local/bin/op-ovsbr0-afxdp up\"\nlog \"  ip addr show ovsbr0 && ip route show\"\n"}}

Safe to re-run.\n# After running, reboot to verify the full boot sequence.\nset -eu\n\nREPO=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/..\" && pwd)\"\nREPO_DIR=\"$REPO\"\nlog() { printf '\\033[1;32m[apply]\\033[0m %s\\n' \"$*\"; }\ndie() { printf '\\033[1;31m[ERROR]\\033[0m %s\\n' \"$*\" >&2; exit 1; }\n\n[ \"$(id -u)\" = 0 ] || die \"run as root (sudo sh deploy/apply-afxdp-boot.sh)\"\n\n# ── 1. Build the fixed op-ovsbr0-afxdp binary ────────────────────────────────\nlog \"building op-ovsbr0-afxdp (reordered: set IP on bridge BEFORE adding eth0)\"\ncd \"$REPO\"\nsudo -u jeremy cargo build --release -p op-network --bin op-ovsbr0-afxdp\ninstall -m 755 target/release/op-ovsbr0-afxdp /usr/local/bin/op-ovsbr0-afxdp\nlog \"installed /usr/local/bin/op-ovsbr0-afxdp\"\n\n# ── 2. Fix ovsbr0-afxdp shell_up — remove --dhcp flag ────────────────────────\n# The --dhcp flag caused the binary to skip all IP/route setup after adding\n# eth0 to the bridge, leaving the host with no default route.\nlog \"fixing /etc/s6/sv/ovsbr0-afxdp/shell_up (removing --dhcp)\"\ncat > /etc/s6/sv/ovsbr0-afxdp/shell_up <<'SHELL'\n#!/bin/sh\nset -eu\nexec /usr/local/bin/op-ovsbr0-afxdp up\nSHELL\nchmod +x /etc/s6/sv/ovsbr0-afxdp/shell_up\n\n# ── 3. Install ovsbr0-netdev-verify oneshot service ───────────────────────────\n# Verifies that ovsbr0 survived boot with datapath_type=netdev before we move\n# the host IP onto the bridge.\nlog \"installing ovsbr0-netdev-verify s6 service\"\nmkdir -p /etc/s6/sv/ovsbr0-netdev-verify/dependencies.d\ninstall -m 644 \"$REPO_DIR/deploy/s6/ovsbr0-netdev-verify/type\" /etc/s6/sv/ovsbr0-netdev-verify/type\ninstall -m 755 \"$REPO_DIR/deploy/s6/ovsbr0-netdev-verify/up\" /etc/s6/sv/ovsbr0-netdev-verify/up\ninstall -m 755 \"$REPO_DIR/deploy/s6/ovsbr0-netdev-verify/shell_up\" /etc/s6/sv/ovsbr0-netdev-verify/shell_up\ntouch /etc/s6/sv/ovsbr0-netdev-verify/dependencies.d/ovsbr0-setup\n\n# ── 4. Install ovsbr0-static oneshot service ─────────────────────────────────\n# Runs after ovsbr0-netdev-verify and before ovsbr0-afxdp (eth0 migration).\n# Sets 148.113.204.83/32 + default route onlink on ovsbr0 so there is no window\n"}}

Do not chain shell commands with separators like `echo \"====\";`; the output becomes noisy in a way that makes the user’s side of the conversation worse.\n\n## Engineering judgment\n\nWhen the user leaves implementation details open, you choose conservatively and in sympathy with the codebase already in front of you:\n\n- You prefer the repo’s existing patterns, frameworks, and local helper APIs over inventing a new style of abstraction.\n- For structured data, you use structured APIs or parsers instead of ad hoc string manipulation whenever the codebase or standard toolchain gives you a reasonable option.\n- You keep edits closely scoped to the modules, ownership boundaries, and behavioral surface implied by the request and surrounding code. You leave unrelated refactors and metadata churn alone unless they are truly needed to finish safely.\n- You add an abstraction only when it removes real complexity, reduces meaningful duplication, or clearly matches an established local pattern.\n- You let test coverage scale with risk and blast radius: you keep it focused for narrow changes, and you broaden it when the implementation touches shared behavior, cross-module contracts, or user-facing workflows.\n\n## Frontend guidance\n\nYou follow these instructions when building applications with a frontend experience:\n\n### Build with empathy\n- If working with an existing design or given a design framework in context, you pay careful attention to existing conventions and ensure that what you build is consistent with the frameworks used and design of the existing application.\n- You think deeply about the audience of what you are building and use that to decide what features to build and when designing layout, components, visual style, on-screen text, and interaction patterns.
