For example, SaaS, CRM, and other operational tools should feel quiet, utilitarian, and work-focused rather than illustrative or editorial: avoid oversized hero sections, decorative card-heavy layouts, and marketing-style composition, and instead prioritize dense but organized information, restrained visual styling, predictable navigation, and interfaces built for scanning, comparison, and repeated action. A game can be more illustrative, expressive, animated, and playful.\n- You make sure that common workflows within the app are ergonomic and efficient, yet comprehensive -- the user of your application should be able to seamlessly navigate in and out of different views and pages in the application.\n\n### Design instructions\n- You make sure to use icons in buttons for tools, swatches for color, segmented controls for modes, toggles/checkboxes for binary settings, sliders/steppers/inputs for numeric values, menus for option sets, tabs for views, and text or icon+text buttons only for clear commands (unless otherwise specified). Cards are kept at 8px border radius or less unless the existing design system requires otherwise.\n- You do not use rounded rectangular UI elements with text inside if you could use a familiar symbol or icon instead (examples include arrow icons for undo/redo, B/I icons for bold/italics, save/download/zoom icons). You build tooltips which name/describe unfamiliar icons when the user hovers over it.\n- You use lucide icons inside buttons whenever one exists instead of manually-drawn SVG icons. If there is a library enabled in an existing application, you use icons from that library.\n- You build feature-complete controls, states, and views that a target user would naturally expect from the application.\n- You do not use visible, in-app text to describe the application's features, functionality, keyboard shortcuts, styling, visual elements, or how to use the application.\n- You should not make a landing page unless absolutely required; when asked for a site, app, game, or tool, build the actual usable experience as the first screen, not marketing or explanatory content.\n- When making a hero page, you use a relevant image, generated bitmap image, or immersive full-bleed interactive scene as the background with text over it that is not in a card; never use a split text/media layout where a card is one side and text is on another side, never put hero text or the primary experience in a card, never use a gradient/SVG hero page, and do not create an SVG hero illustration when a real or generated image can carry the subject.\n- On branded, product, venue, portfolio, or object-focused pages, the brand/product/place/object must be a first-viewport signal, not only tiny nav text or an eyebrow. Hero content must leave a hint of the next section's content visible on every mobile and desktop viewport, including wide desktop.\n- For landing-page heroes, make the H1 the brand/product/place/person name or a literal offer/category; put descriptive value props in supporting copy, not the headline.\n- Websites and games must use visual assets. Move it to a new line if needed, and if it still does not fit inside the UI element, use dynamic sizing so the longest word fits. Text must also not occlude preceding or subsequent content.  \u0000\u0000s6 live subcommand [ subcommand options ] [ services... ] Type \"s6 live help\" for details.\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000timeout must be an integer (milliseconds)\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000s6 process [ process options ] subcommand [ subcommand options ] services... Type \"s6 process help\" for details.\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000s6 repository subcommand [ subcommand options ] [ services... ] Type \"s6 repository help\" for details.\u0000\u0000s6 set subcommand [ subcommand options ] [ services... ] Type \"s6 set help\" for details.\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000s6 system subcommand [ subcommand options ] [ services... ] Type \"s6 system help\" for details.\u0000\u0000Usage: s6 live subcommand [ options ] services...\n\nSubcommands:\n  help\t\t\tthis message\n  status\t\tread the status of a list of services\n  start\t\t\tstart a service (with all its dependencies)\n  stop\t\t\tstop a service (and everything depending on it)\n  restart\t\tstop, then start, a service, with dependencies\n  install\t\tinstall the latest committed service set\n  start-everything\tstart all the services enabled at boot\n  stop-everything\tstop all the non-essential services\n\ns6 live status options:\n  -e\t\t--without-essentials\tignore essential services (default)\n  -E\t\t--with-essentials\talso list essential services\n\ns6 live start, s6 live stop, s6 live restart, s6 live stop-everything options:\n  -n\t\t--dry-run\t\tonly show what would be done, don't do it\n  -t TIMEOUT\t--timeout=TIMEOUT\tif not done after TIMEOUT milliseconds, abort\n\ns6 live install options:\n  -b\t\t--block\t\t\ton contention, wait rather than fail\n  -K\t\t--keep-old\t\tkeep the old db and write its path to stdout\n  -e\t\t--force-essentials\tstop old essential services if needed (default)\n  -E\t\t--no-force-essentials\tkeep obsolete essential services up\n  -f FILE\t--conversion-file=FILE\tuse a conversion file from current to new set\n\t\t--init\t\t\tinstall the initial db. DO NOT USE WHEN LIVE.\n\ns6 live start-everything options:\n  -n\t\t--dry-run\t\tonly show what would be done, don't do it\n  -t TIMEOUT\t--timeout=TIMEOUT\tif not done after TIMEOUT milliseconds, abort\n  -D BUN\t--default-bundle=BUN\tname of the bundle to start (\"default\")\n\n\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000Usage: s6 [ global_options... ] command subcommand [ subcommand_options... ] [ args... ]\n\nFor details about a command and its options, try: s6 command help (e.g.: s6 live help)\n\nCommands:\n  help\t\tthis message\n  version\tprint the version of this package\n  system\tboot and shutdown the system\n  live\t\tstart and stop services and their dependencies\n  process\tcontrol individual long-running processes\n  set\t\tmanipulate sets of services (offline, to later install them live)\n  repository\tmanipulate the service repository itself\n\nGlobal options:\n  -h\t\t--help\t\t\tequivalent to \"s6 help\"\n  -V\t\t--version\t\tequivalent to \"s6 version\"\n\n\t\t--color=yes|no|auto\tdisplay fancy or boring-but-parsable text.\n\t\t\t\t\tauto is the default: fancy if in a terminal.\n\n These options override the values set in s6-frontend.conf:\n  -v V\t\t--verbosity=V\t\tverbosity (0 is terse, 1 is normal/default, more is verbose)\n  -s SCANDIR\t--scandir=SCANDIR\twhere s6-svscan is running\n  -l LIVEDIR\t--livedir=LIVEDIR\ts6-rc live directory\n  -r REPODIR\t--repodir=REPODIR\ts6-rc service set repository\n  -c BOOTDB\t--bootdb=BOOTDB\t\tlive database the system is booting on\n\t\t--stmpdir=STMPDIR\troot-only temporary directory\n\t\t--storelist=LIST\tlist of service stores\n\n\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000Usage: s6 process subcommand [ options ] longruns...\n\n Send commands to *processes* at the s6 supervision level.\n(supervised long-running processes only - not services at the\ns6-rc level. This is useful e.g. to restart a process without\nstopping then starting things depending on it.)\n\nSubcommands:\n  help\t\tthis message\n  start\t\tstart a supervised process without impacting its official state\n  stop\t\tstop a supervised process without impacting its official state\n  restart\trestart a supervised process\n  kill\t\tsend a signal to a supervised process\n  status\tread the status of a supervised process\n\ns6 process start and s6 process stop options:\n  -P\t\t--no-permanent\t\tdon't override the official state if the daemon dies\n\t\t\t\t\t(i.e. if the service manager says the service should be\n\t\t\t\t\tdown, do not restart the daemon; if it says the service\n\t\t\t\t\tshould be up, do restart it). This is the default.\n  -p\t\t--permanent\t\toverride the official state: \"s6 process start foo\" will\n\t\t\t\t\tkeep foo up even if the live status says otherwise\n  -W\t\t--no-wait\t\texit without waiting for service readiness\n  -w\t\t--wait\t\t\tonly exit once the daemon is ready or confirmed dead\n  -t TIMEOUT\t--timeout=TIMEOUT\tif -w: give up if not ready after TIMEOUT milliseconds\n\ns6 process restart options:\n  -W\t\t--no-wait\t\texit without waiting for service readiness\n  -w\t\t--wait\t\t\tonly exit once the daemon is ready again\n  -t TIMEOUT\t--timeout=TIMEOUT\tif -w: give up if not ready after TIMEOUT milliseconds\n\ns6 process kill options:\n  -W\t\t--no-wait\t\texit without waiting for service readiness\n  -w\t\t--wait\t\t\tonly exit once the daemon is ready again, if applicable\n  -t TIMEOUT\t--timeout=TIMEOUT\tif -w: give up if not ready after TIMEOUT milliseconds\n  -s SIGNAL\t--signal=SIGNAL\t\tsend signal SIGNAL rather than the default (prob. SIGTERM)\n\ns6 process status options:\n\n  -L\t\t--without-logs\t\tonly list the status of longruns given as arguments (default)\n  -l\t\t--with-logs\t\talso list status for service/log. This has no effect\n\t\t\t\t\ton services that have loggers declared in s6-rc, for these\n\t\t\t\t\tyou need to list the logger explicitly.\n\n\u0000\u0000\u0000Usage: s6 repository subcommand [ options ]\n\nSubcommands:\n  help\t\tthis message\n  init\t\tinitialize a service repository\n  sync\t\tsynchronize repository with stores\n  list\t\tlist names of saved service sets\n  check         check all sets and fix inconsistencies\n\n\ns6 repository init options:\n  -f\t\t--force\t\t\tOverwrite existing repository\n  -U\t\t--update-stores\t\tUpdate existing repository with new stores\n  -h USER\t--fdholder-user\t\tSet USER as reference fdholder owner\n\ns6 repository sync options:\n  -h USER\t--fdholder-user\t\tSet USER as reference fdholder owner\n\ns6 repository list options: none\n\ns6 repository check options:\n  -E\t\t--no-force-essential\t\tdo not allow manual changes to essential services (default)\n  -e\t\t--force-essential\t\tallow manual changes to essential services\n  -f\t\t--fix\t\t\t\ttry to fix inconsistencies automatically\n  -d\t\t--down\t\t\t\tfix by disabling or masking services if necessary (default)\n  -u\t\t--up\t\t\t\tfix by enabling services if necessary\n\n\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000Usage: s6 set subcommand [ options ] [ arguments... ]\n\nSubcommands:\n  help\t\tthis message\n  save\t\tsave the current set under a user-provided name\n  load\t\tload a previously saved set\n  list\t\tlist services in the working set\n  status\tlist services in the working set with their rx\n  enable\tenable services\n  disable\tdisable services\n  mask\t\tmask services (hide them from the db entirely)\n  unmask\tunmask services (equivalent to \"disable\")\n  check\t\tcheck working set and fix inconsistencies\n  commit\tcommit working set (can then be installed)\n\n\ns6 set save options:\n  -f\t\t--force\t\t\t\toverwrite named set if existing\n\ns6 set load options: none\n\ns6 set list options: none\n\ns6 set status options:\n  -E\t\t--with-essentials\t\tshow all services, even essential ones (default)\n  -e\t\t--without-essentials\t\tdon't show essential services\n\ns6 set enable|disable|mask|unmask options:\n  -f\t\t--ignore-dependencies\t\tonly change listed services\n  -n\t\t--dry-run\t\t\tshow what would happen, don't do\n  -I WHAT\t--if-dependencies-found=WHAT\tWHAT=warn (default) | fail | pull (dependencies will be brought to the same rx)\n\ns6 set check options:\n  -E\t\t--no-force-essential\t\tdo not allow manual changes to essential services (default)\n  -e\t\t--force-essential\t\tallow manual changes to essential services\n  -F\t\t--fix\t\t\t\ttry to fix inconsistencies automatically\n  -d\t\t--down\t\t\t\tfix by disabling or masking services if necessary (default)\n  -u\t\t--up\t\t\t\tfix by enabling services if necessary\n\ns6 set commit options:\n  -f\t\t--force\t\t\t\tcompile db even if up-to-date\n  -K\t\t--keep-old\t\t\tkeep old db if any, print its path to stdout\n  -D BUN\t--default-bundle=BUN\t\tname of the bundle containing enabled+essential services\n  -h USER\t--fdholder-user=USER\t\tuser for the s6-fdholderd process (default=root, it's fine)\n\n\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000Usage: s6 system subcommand\n\nSubcommands:\n  help\t\tthis message\n  boot\t\tinitialize the service manager and start default services\n\n plus, if s6-frontend has been built with s6-linux-init support:\n  halt\t\thalt the system (without powering it off)\n  poweroff\thalt the system, powering it off\n  shutdown\tsynonymous with poweroff\n  reboot\treboot the system\n\nNo options.\n\n\u0000\u0000 [ --ignore-dependencies ] [ --dry-run ] [ --if-dependencies-found=fail|warn|pull ] services...\u0000--if-dependencies-found= argument must be fail, warn or pull\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000the global state has not changed.\n\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000: info: the following atomic services have been brought \u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000timeout must be an unsigned integer (in milliseconds)\u0000\u0000\u0000 is not registered as a supervised service in \u0000\u0000s6 process restart [ -W|--no-wait | -w|--wait ] [ -t timeout | --timeout=timeout ] services...\u0000\u0000--timeout= argument must be an unsigned integer (in milliseconds)\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000s6 process start [ --permanent ] [ --wait ] [ --timeout=millisecs ] services...\u0000s6 process stop [ --permanent ] [ --wait ] [ --timeout=millisecs ] services...\u0000\u0000s6 process status [ -L | -l ] services...\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000  /usr/lib/s6-frontend-helper-echo\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000 /usr/lib/s6-frontend-helper-echo\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000s6 process kill [ --signal=sig ] [ --timeout=millisecs ] [ --wait | --no-wait ] services...\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000--signal= argument must be the name or number of a signal\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000 is not natively supported by s6-svc, cannot ensure reliability\u0000/usr/lib/s6-frontend-helper-kill\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000/usr/share/s6-frontend/s6-rc/sources:/etc/s6-frontend/s6-rc/sources\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000verbosity must be an unsigned integer\u0000\u0000\u0000--color value must be yes, no, or auto\u0000\u0000s6 [ generic options ] command [ command options ] command_arguments... You maintain a pragmatic mindset when discussing these tradeoffs, and so are willing to work with the user after concerns have been noted.\n\n\n# General\nYou bring a senior engineer’s judgment to the work, but you let it arrive through attention rather than premature certainty. Do not chain shell commands with separators like `echo \"====\";`; the output becomes noisy in a way that makes the user’s side of the conversation worse.\n\n## Engineering judgment\n\nWhen the user leaves implementation details open, you choose conservatively and in sympathy with the codebase already in front of you:\n\n- You prefer the repo’s existing patterns, frameworks, and local helper APIs over inventing a new style of abstraction.\n- For structured data, you use structured APIs or parsers instead of ad hoc string manipulation whenever the codebase or standard toolchain gives you a reasonable option.\n- You keep edits closely scoped to the modules, ownership boundaries, and behavioral surface implied by the request and surrounding code. You leave unrelated refactors and metadata churn alone unless they are truly needed to finish safely.\n- You add an abstraction only when it removes real complexity, reduces meaningful duplication, or clearly matches an established local pattern.\n- You let test coverage scale with risk and blast radius: you keep it focused for narrow changes, and you broaden it when the implementation touches shared behavior, cross-module contracts, or user-facing workflows.\n\n## Frontend guidance\n\nYou follow these instructions when building applications with a frontend experience:\n\n### Build with empathy\n- If working with an existing design or given a design framework in context, you pay careful attention to existing conventions and ensure that what you build is consistent with the frameworks used and design of the existing application.\n- You think deeply about the audience of what you are building and use that to decide what features to build and when designing layout, components, visual style, on-screen text, and interaction patterns. Using your application should feel rich and sophisticated.\n- You make sure that the frontend design is tailored for the domain and subject matter of the application. For example, SaaS, CRM, and other operational tools should feel quiet, utilitarian, and work-focused rather than illustrative or editorial: avoid oversized hero sections, decorative card-heavy layouts, and marketing-style composition, and instead prioritize dense but organized information, restrained visual styling, predictable navigation, and interfaces built for scanning, comparison, and repeated action. A game can be more illustrative, expressive, animated, and playful.\n- You make sure that common workflows within the app are ergonomic and efficient, yet comprehensive -- the user of your application should be able to seamlessly navigate in and out of different views and pages in the application.\n\n### Design instructions\n- You make sure to use icons in buttons for tools, swatches for color, segmented controls for modes, toggles/checkboxes for binary settings, sliders/steppers/inputs for numeric values, menus for option sets, tabs for views, and text or icon+text buttons only for clear commands (unless otherwise specified). Cards are kept at 8px border radius or less unless the existing design system requires otherwise.\n- You do not use rounded rectangular UI elements with text inside if you could use a familiar symbol or icon instead (examples include arrow icons for undo/redo, B/I icons for bold/italics, save/download/zoom icons). You build tooltips which name/describe unfamiliar icons when the user hovers over it.\n- You use lucide icons inside buttons whenever one exists instead of manually-drawn SVG icons. If there is a library enabled in an existing application, you use icons from that library.\n- You build feature-complete controls, states, and views that a target user would naturally expect from the application.\n- You do not use visible, in-app text to describe the application's features, functionality, keyboard shortcuts, styling, visual elements, or how to use the application.\n- You should not make a landing page unless absolutely required; when asked for a site, app, game, or tool, build the actual usable experience as the first screen, not marketing or explanatory content.\n- When making a hero page, you use a relevant image, generated bitmap image, or immersive full-bleed interactive scene as the background with text over it that is not in a card; never use a split text/media layout where a card is one side and text is on another side, never put hero text or the primary experience in a card, never use a gradient/SVG hero page, and do not create an SVG hero illustration when a real or generated image can carry the subject.\n- On branded, product, venue, portfolio, or object-focused pages, the brand/product/place/object must be a first-viewport signal, not only tiny nav text or an eyebrow. Hero content must leave a hint of the next section's content visible on every mobile and desktop viewport, including wide desktop.\n- For landing-page heroes, make the H1 the brand/product/place/person name or a literal offer/category; put descriptive value props in supporting copy, not the headline.\n- Websites and games must use visual assets. You can use image search, known relevant images, or generated bitmap images instead of SVGs, unless making a game. Primary images and media should reveal the actual product, place, object, state, gameplay, or person; you refrain from dark, blurred, cropped, stock-like, or purely atmospheric media when the user needs to inspect the real thing. For highly specific game assets you use custom SVG/Three.js/etc.\n- For games or interactive tools with well-established rules, physics, parsing, or AI engines, you use a proven existing library for the core domain logic instead of hand-rolling it, unless the user explicitly asks for a from-scratch implementation.\n- You use Three.js for 3D elements, and make the primary 3D scene full-bleed or unframed and not inside a decorative card/preview container. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. exit 1 ;;\n        *) TARGET=\"$arg\" ;;\n    esac\ndone\n\n[[ \"$EUID\" -eq 0 ]] || { echo \"Run with sudo.\" >&2; exit 1; }\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Logging\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nlog()   { echo -e \"\\033[0;32m[DEPLOY]\\033[0m $*\"; }\nwarn()  { echo -e \"\\033[1;33m[WARN]\\033[0m $*\"; }\nerror() { echo -e \"\\033[0;31m[ERROR]\\033[0m $*\"; exit 1; }\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Helpers\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nappend_env_if_missing() {\n    local file=\"$1\" key=\"$2\" value=\"$3\"\n    grep -q \"^${key}=\" \"$file\" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s=%s\\n' \"$key\" \"$value\" >> \"$file\"\n}\n\ns6_restart() {\n    local svc=\"$1\"\n    if [[ -d \"/run/service/${svc}\" ]]; then\n        s6-svc -r \"/run/service/${svc}\" && log \"Restarted s6 service: ${svc}\"\n    else\n        warn \"s6 service not running: ${svc}\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# STEP 1: System files\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ninstall_system_files() {\n    log \"Installing system files...\"\n\n    # D-Bus policy\n    install -d /etc/dbus-1/system.d\n    install -m 0644 \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/dbus/org.opdbus.conf\"  /etc/dbus-1/system.d/org.opdbus.conf\n    install -m 0644 \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/dbus/org.dbusmcp.conf\" /etc/dbus-1/system.d/org.dbusmcp.conf\n    dbus-send --system --type=method_call \\\n        --dest=org.freedesktop.DBus /org/freedesktop/DBus \\\n        org.freedesktop.DBus.ReloadConfig 2>/dev/null || true\n    log \"Installed D-Bus policy\"\n\n    # s6 service definitions\n    for svc_dir in \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/s6\"/*/; do\n        svc=\"$(basename \"$svc_dir\")\"\n        install -d \"${S6_SV}/${svc}\"\n        cp -a \"${svc_dir}/.\" \"${S6_SV}/${svc}/\"\n        chmod 0755 \"${S6_SV}/${svc}/run\" 2>/dev/null || true\n        chmod 0755 \"${S6_SV}/${svc}/up\" 2>/dev/null || true\n        chmod 0755 \"${S6_SV}/${svc}/shell_up\" 2>/dev/null || true\n        log \"Installed s6 service: ${svc}\"\n    done\n\n    # op-mcp-proxy-select3\n    install -m 0755 \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/op-mcp-proxy-select3\" \"${INSTALL_BIN}/op-mcp-proxy-select3\"\n    log \"Installed op-mcp-proxy-select3\"\n\n    # systemd-networkd units\n    if [[ -d \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/systemd/networkd\" ]]; then\n        install -d /etc/systemd/network\n        find \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/systemd/networkd\" -maxdepth 1 -type f | while read -r f; do\n            install -m 0644 \"$f\" \"/etc/systemd/network/$(basename \"$f\")\"\n        done\n        log \"Installed systemd-networkd units\"\n    fi\n\n    # Netplan\n    install -d /etc/netplan\n    install -m 0600 \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/netplan/01-ovsbr0.yaml\" /etc/netplan/01-ovsbr0.yaml\n    log \"Installed /etc/netplan/01-ovsbr0.yaml\"\n\n    # wgcf — never overwrite the live key\n    if [[ -f /etc/wireguard/wgcf.conf ]]; then\n        log \"/etc/wireguard/wgcf.conf present — not overwriting\"\n    else\n        warn \"/etc/wireguard/wgcf.conf not found. Skipping WARP checks.\"\n    fi\n\n    # App environment\n    install -d /etc/op-dbus\n    if [[ ! -f /etc/op-dbus/environment ]]; then\n        install -m 0640 \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/environment.default\" /etc/op-dbus/environment\n        log \"Installed /etc/op-dbus/environment\"\n    else\n        # Merge: add keys from default that aren't already present\n        while IFS= read -r line; do\n            [[ \"$line\" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue\n            [[ -z \"$line\" ]] && continue\n            key=\"${line%%=*}\"\n            grep -q \"^${key}=\" /etc/op-dbus/environment 2>/dev/null \\\n                || { echo \"$line\" >> /etc/op-dbus/environment; log \"Added ${key} to environment\"; }\n        done < \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/environment.default\"\n    fi\n\n    # Ensure runtime dirs exist\n    local state_dir\n    state_dir=\"$(awk -F= '$1==\"OP_DBUS_STATE_DIR\"{print $2;exit}' /etc/op-dbus/environment)\"\n    state_dir=\"${state_dir:-/var/lib/op-dbus}\"\n    install -d -m 0750 \"${state_dir}/cache\" /run/op-dbus\n    append_env_if_missing /etc/op-dbus/environment \"OP_DBUS_CACHE_DIR\" \"${state_dir}/cache\"\n\n    log \"System files installed.\"\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# STEP 2: Network bootstrap\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nrun_network_bootstrap() {\n    [[ \"$SKIP_NETWORK\" == \"true\" ]] && { log \"Skipping network bootstrap.\"; return 0; }\n    local script=\"${DEPLOY_DIR}/deploy-network.sh\"\n    [[ -x \"$script\" ]] || error \"${script} not found or not executable\"\n    log \"Running network bootstrap...\"\n    \"$script\"\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# STEP 3: Build + install service binaries\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nbuild_and_install() {\n    local crate=\"$1\" binary=\"$2\"\n    log \"Building ${binary}...\"\n    cargo build --release -p \"$crate\" --bin \"$binary\" \\\n        || error \"Build failed: ${binary}\"\n    install -m 0755 \"${PROJECT_ROOT}/target/release/${binary}\" \"${INSTALL_BIN}/${binary}\"\n    log \"Installed ${binary} → ${INSTALL_BIN}/${binary}\"\n}\n\ndeploy_service() {\n    local crate=\"$1\" binary=\"$2\" service=\"$3\"\n    build_and_install \"$crate\" \"$binary\"\n    s6_restart \"$service\"\n    log \"✅ ${service} deployed\"\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Main\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ncommand -v cargo >/dev/null || warn \"cargo not found — service builds will fail\"\ncommand -v s6-svc >/dev/null || warn \"s6-svc not found\"\n\ninstall_system_files\nrun_network_bootstrap\n\nfor entry in \"${SERVICES[@]}\"; {"timestamp":"2026-05-27T02:07:34.371Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_xY3EAigwghma8S90IL1YhiRu","output":"Chunk ID: b31f13\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 364\nOutput:\n#!/bin/sh\n# Safely compile and activate an s6-rc source tree.\n#\n# Never repoints /etc/s6/rc/compiled before s6-rc-update succeeds. Doing so\n# leaves /run/s6-rc/state from the old database paired with a new compiled DB,\n# which makes future s6-rc commands fail with \"unable to read valid state\".\nset -eu\n\nS6_SV=${S6_SV:-/etc/s6/sv}\nS6_ADMIN=${S6_ADMIN:-/etc/s6/adminsv}\nS6_COMPILED_LINK=${S6_COMPILED_LINK:-/etc/s6/rc/compiled}\nS6_DB_ROOT=${S6_DB_ROOT:-/etc/s6/rc}\nLABEL=${1:-local}\n\nif ! command -v s6-rc-compile >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"s6-rc-compile not found\" >&2\n    exit 127\nfi\n\nif ! command -v s6-rc-update >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"s6-rc-update not found\" >&2\n    exit 127\nfi\n\nif [ ! -d \"$S6_SV\" ]; then\n    echo \"service source directory not found: $S6_SV\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif [ ! -d \"$S6_ADMIN\" ]; then\n    echo \"admin source directory not found: $S6_ADMIN\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nold_db=\"$(readlink -f \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\nnew_db=\"${S6_DB_ROOT}/compiled-${LABEL}-$(date +%s%N)\"\n\necho \"Compiling s6-rc database: $new_db\"\ns6-rc-compile \"$new_db\" \"$S6_SV\" \"$S6_ADMIN\"\ns6-rc-db -c \"$new_db\" check\n\necho \"Updating live s6-rc state to: $new_db\"\nif ! s6-rc-update \"$new_db\"; then\n    echo \"s6-rc-update failed; leaving $S6_COMPILED_LINK unchanged\" >&2\n    [ -n \"$old_db\" ] && echo \"current compiled DB remains: $old_db\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nln -sfnT \"$new_db\" \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\"\necho \"Activated s6-rc database: $new_db\"\n\n"}}

The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. }\n}\n\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\nimpl Transport for HttpTransport {\n    async fn serve<H: McpHandler + 'static>(self, handler: Arc<H>) -> Result<()> {\n        info!(addr = %self.bind_addr,  }\n\n    /// Get tool definition\n    pub async fn get_definition(&self, name: &str) -> Option<ToolDefinition> {\n        self.definitions.read().await.get(name).cloned()\n    }\n\n    /// List all Stdio Transport\n//!\n//! Standard MCP transport over stdin/stdout.\n\nuse super::{McpHandler, Transport};\nuse crate::{JsonRpcError, McpRequest, McpResponse};\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tokio::io::{AsyncBufReadExt, AsyncWriteExt, BufReader};\nuse tracing::{debug, error, info};\n\n/// Stdio transport - reads JSON-RPC from stdin, writes to stdout\npub struct StdioTransport;\n\nimpl StdioTransport {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for StdioTransport {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\nimpl Transport for StdioTransport {\n    async fn serve<H: McpHandler + 'static>(self, handler: Arc<H>) -> Result<()> {\n        info!(\"Starting MCP stdio transport\");\n\n        let stdin = tokio::io::stdin();\n        let mut stdout = tokio::io::stdout();\n        let mut reader = BufReader::new(stdin).lines();\n\n        while let Some(line) = reader.next_line().await? {\n            let line = line.trim();\n            if line.is_empty() {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            debug!(request = %line, \"Received request\");\n\n            let mut line_mut = line.to_string();\n            let response = match unsafe { simd_json::from_str::<McpRequest>(&mut line_mut) } {\n                Ok(request) => handler.handle_request(request).await,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    error!(error = %e, \"Parse error\");\n                    McpResponse::error(None, JsonRpcError::parse_error(e.to_string()))\n                }\n            };\n\n            let response_json = simd_json::to_string(&response)?;\n            debug!(response = %response_json, \"Sending response\");\n\n            stdout.write_all(response_json.as_bytes()).await?;\n            stdout.write_all(b\"\\n\").await?;\n            stdout.flush().await?;\n        }\n\n        info!(\"Stdio transport shutting down\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n"}}

Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}

sled loaded\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            warn!(\"Identity sled present but is_valid=false — headers will be omitted\");\n        }\n    } else {\n        warn!(\"Identity sled not self.sessions.read().await;\n            for (session_id, session) in sessions.iter() {\n                // Sessions expire after 1 hour of inactivity\n                if now - session.last_used > {"timestamp":"2026-05-27T02:17:28.371Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes, route by schema tags is the right design.\n\nThe corrected architecture should be:\n\n`PluginSchema.tags` -> SchemaEngine route decision -> Xray outbound/inbound tag or gRPC metadata -> target MCP/gRPC service\n\nNot:\n\n`OVS OpenFlow` decides MCP routing.\n\nOVS/ROVS should stay in its lane: obfuscation, walled garden, local bridge enforcement, AF_XDP/netdev setup. Xray is the control-plane router for service traffic. The code mostly agrees with that:\n\n- `op-network` has the `rovs-*` suite for OVSDB/OpenFlow.\n- Xray config already has `to-grpc-bridge` and Ghostbridge metadata injection.\n- `SchemaEngine` already computes and carries `tags_touched`.\n- gRPC subscriptions already support tag filters.\n- `op-mcp-proxy` injects `x-ghostbridge-footprint` and `x-ghostbridge-trace-id`, but not schema tags.\n- Xray config is currently catch-all: all tcp/udp goes to `to-grpc-bridge`; it is not schema-tag aware yet.\n\nSo the missing link is: schema tags are not being projected into the Xray route decision.\n\nFor cognitive MCP specifically, tags like `mcp`, `cognitive`, `notebooklm`, `qdrant`, or `accountability` should select the cognitive route, likely `op-cognitive-mcp` on `3003` or `50052`, instead of falling into generic `op-dbus`/bridge routing.\n\nThe fix should be in the controller/gateway layer, probably:\n\n1. Add `x-ghostbridge-schema-tags` metadata from `PluginSchema.tags` or `tags_touched`.\n2. Extend the gateway route table so tags map to route targets:\n   - `cognitive`, `notebooklm`, `qdrant` -> `op-cognitive-mcp`\n   - `state`, `ovsdb`, `network` -> `op-dbus` / SchemaEngine\n   - `llm`, `external` -> Xray egress\n3. Generate or select the Xray outbound tag from that decision.\n4. Keep ROVS/OpenFlow only for local bridge constraints and obfuscation.\n\nCurrent state explains the symptom: Xray and MCP are running, and tools exist, but the route layer is not schema-tag selecting cognitive MCP.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. internal_type,\n            property,\n            old_value,\n            new_value,\n            tags,\n            source,\n            ChangeSource::Internal,\n        )\n        .await\n        .map(|_| ())\n        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(e))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl SchemaEngine {\n    /// Create a new authoritative Schema Engine\n    pub fn new(\n        event_chain: ChangeSource,\n    ) -> Result<StateChange, String> {\n        if tags.is_empty() {\n            tags = self.compute_tags(&plugin_id, &object_path);\n        }\n\n        let event = {\n            let mut chain = self.event_chain.write().await;\n            let op = match change_type {\n                ChangeType::PropertySet => OperationType::PropertySet,\n                ChangeType::ObjectRemoved => OperationType::Custom(\"delete\".to_string()),\n                _ => OperationType::EmitSignal,\n            };\n            let event = chain.record(\n                actor_id.clone(),\n                plugin_id.clone(),\n                \"1.0.0\".to_string(),\n                op,\n                object_path.clone(),\n                tags.clone(),\n                Decision::Allow,\n                &new_value,\n            );\n            event.clone()\n        };\n\n        self.update_cached_plugin_state(\n            &plugin_id,\n            &object_path,\n };\n\n        let _ = self.change_tx.send(change.clone());\n        Ok(change)\n    }\n\n    /// Start the Schema Engine background tasks.\n    /// Subscribes to authoritative RCP stores and hex::encode(hasher.finalize());\n            let uuid          = std::env::var(\"SCHEMA_UUID\").unwrap_or_default();\n            let subid         = \"NIST_SP_800_53_R5\".into());\n            let ctrl_refs     = std::env::var(\"SCHEMA_CONTROL_REFS\").unwrap_or_default();\n            let stmt_refs     = object_path.starts_with(\"schema/\") {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        let mut cache = self.state_cache.write().await;\n\n        match change_type {\n            ChangeType::ObjectRemoved => {\n                cache.remove(plugin_id);\n            }\n            ChangeType::PropertySet => {\n                if let Some(property) = property {\n                    let entry = cache\n If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. {"timestamp":"2026-05-27T02:32:05.206Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes. From inside `wg-xray`, `busctl` can now see and call the host cognitive MCP D-Bus tree, and `ListTools` returns the tool list.\n\nI also found the host projection services were installed but not in the active s6 graph. #[zbus(signal)]\n    async fn updated(emitter: &SignalEmitter<'_>, data_json: &str) -> zbus::Result<()>;\n}\n\n/// Derives the D-Bus object path from a projection's entity_type and /org/opdbus/identity/sled\n/// entity_type \"ovsdb_bridge\"     → /org/opdbus/ovsdb/bridge/<entity_id>\npub fn projection_path(entity_type: &str, entity_id: &str) -> String {\n    // Replace dots and underscores in type with slashes for the path prefix\n    let type_path = entity_type\n        .replace('.', \"/\")\n        .replace('_', \"/\")\n        .to_lowercase();\n\n    // For singleton objects (memory, cpu, filesystems, network) the entity_id\n    // is typically the same as the type — omit it to avoid redundancy.\n    let is_singleton = entity_id == entity_type\n        ||        .chars()\n            .map(|c| if c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '_' || c == '-' { c } else { '_' })\n            .collect();\n        format!(\"/org/opdbus/{}/{}\", type_path, safe_id)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Manages the set of D-Bus objects served for all projections.\npub struct ProjectionDbusServer {\n    conn: Connection,\n    /// path → data/state handles so we can update in place\n    objects: HashMap<String, (Arc<RwLock<String>>, Arc<RwLock<String>>)>,\n}\n\nimpl ProjectionDbusServer {\n    pub async fn new() -> Result<Self> {\n        let conn = Builder::session()?\n  conn,\n            objects: HashMap::new(),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Register a projection as a D-Bus object (or update it if already registered).\n    pub async fn upsert(&mut self, projection: .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"{}\".to_string());\n        let state_str = format!(\"{:?}\", projection.state);\n\n        if let Some((data_handle, state_handle)) = self.objects.get(&path) {\n            // Update existing object in place\n            *data_handle.write().await = data_json.clone();\n            *state_handle.write().await = state_str;\n\n            // Emit the updated signal\n ProjectedObject::updated(iface_ref.signal_emitter(), &data_json).await?;\n\n            debug!(path, \"updated D-Bus projection object\");\n        } else {\n            // Register new object\n            let data_arc = Arc::new(RwLock::new(data_json));\n            let state_arc = Arc::new(RwLock::new(state_str));\n\n            let obj = ProjectedObject {\n                entity_type:          self.conn\n                .object_server()\n                .at(&path, obj)\n                .await?;\n\n            self.objects.insert(path.clone(), (data_arc, state_arc));\n            info!(path, entity_type = %projection.entity_type, \"registered D-Bus projection object\");\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Remove a projection's D-Bus object.\n    pub async fn remove(&mut self, entity_type: &str, entity_id: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        let path = projection_path(entity_type, entity_id);\n        if self.objects.remove(&path).is_some() {\n            self.conn\n                .object_server()\n                .remove::<ProjectedObject, _>(&path)\n                .await?;\n            info!(path, \"removed D-Bus projection object\");\n        }\n This module implements the `JsonStreamServer` trait, providing SSE/WebSocket\n//! server functionality for streaming projections to the UI using Axum.\n\nuse crate::data_models::*;\nuse crate::interfaces::{JsonStreamServer, JsonStreamStatus};\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse axum::{\n    extract::State,\n    response::sse::{Event, Sse},\n    routing::get,\n    Router,\n};\nuse dashmap::DashMap;\nuse futures::stream::{self, Stream};\nuse std::convert::Infallible;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tokio::sync::broadcast;\nuse tokio_stream::wrappers::BroadcastStream;\nuse tokio_stream::StreamExt;\nuse tracing::{info, warn};\n\n/// Internal state for the Axum server\nstruct ServerState {\n    tx: broadcast::Sender<ProjectionUpdate>,\n    client_count: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize>,\n    total_clients: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,\n    snapshot: Arc<DashMap<String, Projection>>,\n}\n\n/// Server that streams projection updates to connected clients.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct ProjectionStreamServer {\n    /// Port to listen on\n    port: u16,\n    /// Whether the server is running\n    running: bool,\n    /// Channel for broadcasting updates\n    tx: broadcast::Sender<ProjectionUpdate>,\n    /// Number of connected clients\n    client_count: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize>,\n    /// Total clients served\n    total_clients: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,\n    /// Total messages sent\n    messages_sent: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,\n    /// Latest known projection set for batch-on-connect delivery\n    snapshot: Arc<DashMap<String, Projection>>,\n}\n\nimpl ProjectionStreamServer {\n    /// Creates a new ProjectionStreamServer\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        let (tx, _) = broadcast::channel(1024);\n        Self {\n            port: 0,\n            running: false,\n            tx,\n            client_count: Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0)),\n            total_clients: Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0)),\n            messages_sent: Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0)),\n            snapshot: Arc::new(DashMap::new()),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for ProjectionStreamServer {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl JsonStreamServer for ProjectionStreamServer {\n    fn start(&mut self, port: u16) -> Result<()> {\n        self.port = port;\n        self.running = true;\n\n        let state = Arc::new(ServerState {\n            tx: self.tx.clone(),\n            client_count: self.client_count.clone(),\n            total_clients: self.total_clients.clone(),\n            snapshot: self.snapshot.clone(),\n        });\n\n        let app = Router::new()\n            .route(\"/events\", get(sse_handler))\n            .with_state(state);\n\n        let addr = std::net::SocketAddr::from(([0, 0, 0, 0], port));\n\n        info!(port = port, \"Starting JSON-stream SSE server\");\n\n        tokio::spawn(async move {\n            let listener = match tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(addr).await {\n                Ok(l) => l,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    warn!(error = %e, \"Failed to bind JSON-stream server\");\n                    return;\n                }\n            };\n\n            if let Err(e) = axum::serve(listener, app).await {\n                warn!(error = %e, \"JSON-stream server error\");\n            }\n        });\n\n        info!(port = port, \"JSON-stream server started in background\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn broadcast(&self, update: &ProjectionUpdate) {\n        match update.update_type {\n            UpdateType::Deleted => {\n                self.snapshot.remove(&update.projection.id);\n            }\n            _ => {\n                self.snapshot\n                    .insert(update.projection.id.clone(), update.projection.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        if !self.running {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        if let Err(_e) = self.tx.send(update.clone()) {\n            // This is expected if no clients are connected\n        } else {\n            self.messages_sent\n                .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn handle_client(&self, client_id: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        info!(client_id = client_id, \"New client connected to JSON-stream\");\n        self.client_count\n            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);\n        self.total_clients\n            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn disconnect_client(&self, client_id: &str) {\n        info!(\n            client_id = client_id,\n            \"Client disconnected from JSON-stream\"\n        );\n        self.client_count\n            .fetch_sub(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);\n    }\n\n    fn client_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.client_count.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst)\n    }\n\n    fn status(&self) -> JsonStreamStatus {\n        JsonStreamStatus {\n            running: self.running,\n            port: self.port,\n            client_count: self.client_count(),\n            total_clients: self.total_clients.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst),\n            messages_sent: self.messages_sent.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// SSE handler for Axum\nasync fn sse_handler(\n    State(state): State<Arc<ServerState>>,\n) -> Sse<impl Stream<Item = Result<Event, Infallible>>> {\n    state\n        .client_count\n        .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);\n    state\n        .total_clients\n        .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);\n\n    let rx = state.tx.subscribe();\n    let mut snapshot = state\n        .snapshot\n        .iter()\n        .map(|projection| projection.value().clone())\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n    snapshot.sort_by(|left, right| left.id.cmp(&right.id));\n\n    let initial = stream::iter(snapshot.into_iter().map(|projection| {\n        let data = serde_json::to_string(&ProjectionUpdate {\n            update_type: UpdateType::Created,\n            projection,\n            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now(),\n        })\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n        Ok(Event::default().event(\"projection_update\").data(data))\n    }));\n\n    let live = BroadcastStream::new(rx).filter_map(|result| match result {\n        Ok(update) => {\n            let data = serde_json::to_string(&update).unwrap_or_default();\n            Some(Ok(Event::default().event(\"projection_update\").data(data)))\n        }\n        Err(_) => None,\n    });\n\n    // Add keepalive\n    let keepalive = stream::repeat_with(|| Ok(Event::default().comment(\"keepalive\")))\n        .throttle(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30));\n\n    let combined = If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n"}},"realtime_active":false,"summary":"none","user_instructions":"### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}
