    input_schema: tool.input_schema(),\n            schema_version: String::new(),\n            category: tool.category().to_string(),\n            tags: tool.tags(),\n            namespace: tool.namespace().to_string(),\n        };\n\n        self.tools.write().await.insert(name.clone(), tool);\n        self.definitions\n            .write()\n            .await\n            .insert(name.clone(), definition);\n\n        debug!(\"Registered tool: {}\", name);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Get a tool by name (instant lookup, no loading)\n    pub async fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<BoxedTool> {\n        self.tools.read().await.get(name).cloned()\n    }\n\n    /// Execute a tool by name\n    pub async fn execute(&self, name: &str, input: Value) -> Result<Value> {\n        let tool = self\n            .get(name)\n            .await\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Tool not found: {}\", name))?;\n        tool.execute(input).await\n    }\n\n    /// Get tool definition\n    pub async fn get_definition(&self, name: &str) -> Option<ToolDefinition> {\n        self.definitions.read().await.get(name).cloned()\n    }\n\n    /// List all tools (paginated)\n    pub async fn list(\n        &self,\n        offset: usize,\n        limit: usize,\n        category: Option<&str>,\n    ) -> Vec<ToolDefinition> {\n        let defs = self.definitions.read().await;\n\n        let filtered: Vec<_> = defs\n            .values()\n            .filter(|d| category.map_or(true, |c| d.category == c))\n            .cloned()\n            .collect();\n\n        filtered.into_iter().skip(offset).take(limit).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Search tools by query\n    pub async fn search(&self, query: &str) -> Vec<ToolDefinition> {\n        let query_lower = query.to_lowercase();\n        let defs = self.definitions.read().await;\n\n        defs.values()\n            .filter(|d| {\n                d.name.to_lowercase().contains(&query_lower)\n                    || d.description.to_lowercase().contains(&query_lower)\n                    || d.category.to_lowercase().contains(&query_lower)\n Reasonable limit for search results\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Total tool count\n    pub async fn count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.tools.read().await.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Get all categories\n    pub async fn categories(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        let defs = self.definitions.read().await;\n        let mut cats: Vec<String> = defs\n            .values()\n            .map(|d| d.category.clone())\n            .filter(|c| !c.is_empty())\n            .collect();\n        cats.sort();\n        cats.dedup();\n        cats\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for ToolRegistry {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Registry executor for CompactServer\npub struct RegistryExecutor {\n    registry: Arc<ToolRegistry>,\n}\n\nimpl RegistryExecutor {\n    pub fn new(registry: Arc<ToolRegistry>) -> Self {\n        Self { registry }\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl ToolExecutor for RegistryExecutor {\n    async fn execute_tool(&self, tool_name: &str, self.registry.list(0, 1000, None).await;\n        Ok(tools\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|t| ToolInfo {\n                name: t.name,\n                description: t.description,\n usize) -> Result<Vec<ToolInfo>> {\n        let tools = self.registry.search(query).await;\n        Ok(tools\n            .into_iter()\n            .take(limit)\n            .map(|t| ToolInfo {\n                name: t.name,\n                description: t.description,\n                input_schema: t.input_schema,\n                annotations: None,\n            })\n            .collect())\n    }\n}\n"}}

bus\n        let services = self.scanner.list_services(self.bus_type).await?;\n\n        // Filter for agent services\n        let agent_services: Vec<_> = services\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|s| s.name.starts_with(\"org.dbusmcp.Agent.\"))\n            .collect();\n\n        info!(\"Found {} agent services on D-Bus\", agent_services.len());\n\n        let mut discovered = agent.operations.len());\n\n                    // Create tools for each operation\n                    for op in &agent.operations {\n                        let tool = AgentTool {\n                            name: format!(\"{}_{}\", agent.id, op),\n                            description: format!(\n                                \"[{}] {} - {} operation\",\n discovered.insert(agent.id.clone(), agent);\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    warn!(\"  ✗ Failed to introspect {}: {}\", service.name, e);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        info!(\n            \"Discovered {} agents with {} total tools\",\n            discovered.len(),\n            tools.len()\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    ///            }\n            }\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Execute a tool by calling the D-Bus agent\n    pub async fn execute_tool(&self, tool_name: &str, arguments: Value) -> Result<Value> {\n self.discovered_agents.read().await;\n        let agent = agents\n            .get(&tool.agent_id)\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Agent not found: {}\", tool.agent_id))?;\n\n        if proxy = zbus::Proxy::new(\n            conn,\n            &*agent.service_name,\n            &*agent.object_path,\n            \"org.dbusmcp.Agent\",\n        )\n        .await?;\n\n        // Build task JSON\n        let task = json!({\n            \"task_type\": agent.agent_type,\n            \"operation\": tool.operation,\n            \"path\": arguments.get(\"path\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()),\n            \"args\": arguments.get(\"args\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()),\n            \"config\": arguments.get(\"config\").cloned().unwrap_or(json!({}))\n        });\n\n        let Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. object: &'static str,\n    created: i64,\n    owned_by: &'static str,\n}\n\n#[derive(Serialize)]\nstruct ModelList {\n    object: &'static str,\n    data: Vec<ModelObject>,\n}\n\n// ── Handlers data: models\n            .iter()\n            .map(|id| ModelObject {\n                id: id.to_string(),\n                object: \"model\",\n                created: 1700000000,\n                owned_by: \"google\",\n            })\n            .collect(),\n    })\n}\n\nasync fn chat_completions(\n    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,\n    Json(req): Json<ChatCompletionRequest>,\n) -> Response {\n    // Rate limit before touching Vertex AI.\n    {\n        let wait = state.rate_limiter.lock().await.try_consume().err();\n        if let Some(delay) = wait {\n            if delay.as_secs() > 5 {\n                // Backlog too deep — reject rather than queue indefinitely.\n                warn!(wait_ms = delay.as_millis(), \"rate limit: rejecting request\");\n .iter()\n        .map(|m| serde_json::json!({ \"role\": m.role, \"content\": m.content }))\n        .collect();\n\n    // Vertex AI gRPC path.\n    if let Some(ref vertex) = state.vertex {\n { \"message\": e.to_string() } });\n                    return (StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY, Json(body)).into_response();\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // CloudAI companion fallback.\n    if let Some(ref llm) = state.llm {\n        let mcp_req = simd_json::json!({\n            \"jsonrpc\": \"2.0\",\n            \"id\": \"http-1\",\n            \"method\": llm_resp = llm.handle(&mcp_req).await;\n\n        if let Some(err) = llm_resp.get(\"error\") {\n            let msg = err.get(\"message\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or(\"llm error\");\n            let code = err.get(\"code\").and_then(|v| v.as_i64()).unwrap_or(-1);\n            let body = serde_json::json!({ \"error\": { \"message\": msg, \"code\": code } });\n            return (StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY, Json(body)).into_response();\n        }\n\n        let text = llm_resp[\"result\"][\"completion\"]\n            .as_str()\n            .unwrap_or(\"\")\n            .to_string();\n\n        if req.stream {\n            return single_chunk_sse(text, req.model, id, created);\n        }\n        return ok_response(text, req.model, id, created);\n    }\n\n"}}

Set session context (called by gateway after auth)\n    pub async fn set_session(&self, ctx: SessionContext) {\n        info!(\n            session_id = ?ctx.session_id,\n            is_controller = %ctx.is_controller,\n            \"Session context set\"\n        );\n        *self.session.write().await = ctx;\n    }\n\n    /// Check if current session can execute controller-only tools\n    pub async fn can_execute_controller_tools(&self) -> bool {\n        self.session.read().await.is_controller\n    }\n\n    /// Handle MCP request\n    pub async fn handle_request(&self, request: McpRequest) -> McpResponse {\n        debug!(method = %request.method, \"Handling compact MCP request\");\n\n        match request.method.as_str() {\n            \"initialize\" => self.handle_initialize(request).await,\n            \"initialized\" => McpResponse::success(request.id, json!({})),\n            \"ping\" => McpResponse::success(request.id, json!({})),\n        let mut ctx = self.create_context(request_id);\n        \n        if let Err(e) = self.load_tools(&mut ctx).await {\n            error!(\"Failed to load tools: {}\", e);\n            return McpResponse::error(\n                request.id.clone(),\n                JsonRpcError::new(-32000, format!(\"Failed to load tools: {}\", e), None),\n            );\n        }\n\n        let params = request.params.as_ref();\n        \n        let tool_name = params\n            .and_then(|p| p.get(\"name\"))\n            .and_then(|n| n.as_str())\n            .unwrap_or(\"\");\n        \n        let arguments = params\n            .and_then(|p| p.get(\"arguments\"))\n            .cloned()\n            .unwrap_or(json!({}));\n\n        info!(\n            request_id = %request_id,\n            tool = %tool_name,\n            turn = ctx.turn_count() + 1,\n            max_turns = self.config.max_turns,\n            \"Executing tool\"\n        );\n\n        // Execute based on meta-tool name\n        let result = match tool_name {\n            \"execute_tool\" => self.meta_execute_tool(&ctx, arguments).await,\n            \"list_tools\" => self.meta_list_tools(&ctx, arguments),\n            \"search_tools\" => self.meta_search_tools(&ctx, arguments),\n            \"get_tool_schema\" => self.meta_get_tool_schema(&ctx, arguments),\n            \"respond\" => self.meta_respond(arguments),\n            _ => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"Unknown meta-tool: {}\", tool_name)),\n        };\n\n        let summary = ctx.summary();\n        \n        // Context is dropped here, unloading tools\n        match result {\n            Ok(value) => McpResponse::success(\n                request.id.clone(),\n                json!({\n                    \"content\": [{\n                        \"type\": \"text\",\n                        \"text\": simd_json::to_string_pretty(&value).unwrap_or_default()\n                    }],\n                    \"_meta\": {\n                        \"request_id\": summary.request_id,\n                        \"turn\": summary.turns_used,\n                        \"max_turns\": summary.max_turns,\n                        \"remaining\": summary.max_turns - summary.turns_used,\n                        \"elapsed_secs\": summary.elapsed_secs\n                    }\n                }),\n            ),\n            Err(e) => McpResponse::error(\n request_id: &str) -> RequestContext {\n        let config = RequestConfig {\n            max_turns: self.config.max_turns as u32,\n            timeout_secs: 300,\n            preload_all: true,\n        };\n        RequestContext::new(request_id.to_string(), config)\n    }\n\n    /// Load all tools into context\n    async fn load_tools(&self, ctx: &mut RequestContext) -> Result<()> {\n        // Response tools\n        ctx.load_tool(Arc::new(tools::response::RespondToUserTool));\n        ctx.load_tool(Arc::new(tools::response::CannotPerformTool));\n        ctx.load_tool(Arc::new(tools::response::RequestClarificationTool));\n        \n        // Filesystem tools\n        ctx.load_tool(Arc::new(tools::filesystem::ReadFileTool));\n        ctx.load_tool(Arc::new(tools::filesystem::WriteFileTool));\n        ctx.load_tool(Arc::new(tools::filesystem::ListDirectoryTool));\n        \n        // Shell tools\n        ctx.load_tool(Arc::new(tools::shell::ShellExecuteTool::new()));\n        \n        // System tools\n        ctx.load_tool(Arc::new(tools::system::ListNetworkInterfacesTool));\n        \n        // Systemd tools\n        ctx.load_tool(Arc::new(tools::systemd::SystemdUnitStatusTool));\n        ctx.load_tool(Arc::new(tools::systemd::SystemdListUnitsTool));\n        ctx.load_tool(Arc::new(tools::systemd::SystemdStartUnitTool));\n        ctx.load_tool(Arc::new(tools::systemd::SystemdStopUnitTool));\n        ctx.load_tool(Arc::new(tools::systemd::SystemdRestartUnitTool));\n"}}

=============================================================================\n\n/// Tool-name substring patterns that require controller privileges to execute.\nconst BLOCKED_PATTERNS: &[&str] = &[\n    \"systemd_enable\",\n    \"systemd_disable\",\n    \"systemd_apply\",\n    // OVS mutations\n    \"ovs_create\",\n    \"ovs_delete\",\n    \"ovs_add\",\n    \"ovs_set\",\n    \"ovs_del\",\n    // Plugin mutations (matches any *_apply pattern)\n    \"_apply\",\n    // Btrfs mutations\n    \"btrfs_create\",\n    \"btrfs_delete\",\n    \"btrfs_snapshot\",\n];\n\n/// Tool names that are always permitted, regardless of session privilege.\n/// These tools have no system side effects and are required for the LLM to\n/// communicate with the user at the end of a turn.\nconst ALWAYS_ALLOWED: &[&str] = &[\n    \"respond_to_user\",\n    \"cannot_perform\",\n    \"request_clarification\",\n];\n\nfn is_response_tool(name: &str) -> bool {\n    ALWAYS_ALLOWED.contains(&name)\n}\n\nfn is_tool_blocked(name: &str) -> bool {\n    if is_response_tool(name) {\n        return false;\n    }\n    BLOCKED_PATTERNS.iter().any(|pat| name.contains(pat))\n}\n\n/// Configuration for request handling\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct RequestConfig {\n    /// Maximum tool calls per REQUEST (not session)\n    pub max_turns: u32,\n    /// Request timeout in seconds\n    pub timeout_secs: u64,\n    /// Whether to preload all tools at request start\n    pub preload_all: bool,\n}\n\nimpl Default for RequestConfig {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            max_turns: 75,\n RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Check if caller can access controller-only tools\n    pub fn can_access_controller_tools(&self) -> bool {\n        self.is_controller\n    }\n\n    /// Check if caller has any valid session\n    pub fn is_authenticated(&self) -> bool {\n        self.session_id.is_some()\n    }\n\n    /// Load a tool into this request context\n    pub fn load_tool(&mut self, tool: BoxedTool) {\n        let name = tool.name().to_string();\n        let definition = ToolDefinition {\n            name: name.clone(),\n            description: self.tools.insert(name.clone(), tool);\n        self.definitions.insert(name.clone(), definition);\n        debug!(\"Loaded tool into request context: {}\", name);\n    }\n\n    /// Load all tools from a factory function\n    pub async fn load_all_tools<F, Fut>(&mut self, factory: F) -> Result<usize>\n    where\n        F: FnOnce() -> Fut,\n        Fut: std::future::Future<Output = Result<Vec<BoxedTool>>>,\n    {\n        let tools = factory().await?;\n        let count = tools.len();\n        \n        for tool in tools {\n            self.load_tool(tool);\n        }\n        \n        info!(\n            request_id = %self.request_id,\n            tool_count = count,\n            \"Loaded all tools for request\"\n        );\n        \n        Ok(count)\n    }\n\n    /// exceeded\n    pub fn increment_turn(&self) -> Result<u32, TurnLimitError> {\n        let current = self.turn_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) + 1;\n        \n        if current > self.config.max_turns {\n            warn!(\n                request_id = %self.request_id,\n                current = current,\n                max = self.config.max_turns,\n                \"Turn debug!(\n            request_id = %self.request_id,\n            turn = current,\n            remaining = self.config.max_turns - current,\n            \"Turn {} of {}\",\n            current,\n            self.config.max_turns\n        );\n        \n        Ok(current)\n    }\n\n    /// Check if request has timed out\n    pub fn is_timed_out(&self) -> bool {\n        self.started_at.elapsed().as_secs() > self.config.timeout_secs\n    }\n\n    /// Get remaining turns\n    pub fn remaining_turns(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.config.max_turns.saturating_sub(self.turn_count())\n    }\n\n    /// Get a tool by name\n    pub fn get_tool(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&BoxedTool> {\n        self.tools.get(name)\n    }\n\n    /// Get tool definition\n    pub fn get_definition(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&ToolDefinition> {\n        self.definitions.get(name)\n    }\n\n    /// Execute a tool.\n    ///\n    /// This is the **single choke point** for all tool execution in compact\n    /// mode. Both the verbose `tools/call` path and the compact-mode\n    /// `execute_tool` meta-tool route through here, so the security check\n    /// below covers both.\n    pub async fn execute_tool(&self, name: &str, input: Value) -> Result<Value> {\n        // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n        // SECURITY GATE (audit item #7)\n        // -----------------------------------------------------------------\n        // Reject blocked tools unless the session is an authenticated\n        // controller (i.e. the operator's session, validated by the gateway).\n        if is_tool_blocked(name) {\n            if !self.is_controller {\n                warn!(\n                    request_id = %self.request_id,\n                    session_id = ?self.session_id,\n                    tool = %name,\n                    \"Rejected blocked tool: non-controller session\"\n                );\n                anyhow::bail!(\n                    \"Tool '{}' is restricted to controller sessions and cannot be invoked from compact mode\",\n                    name\n                );\n            }\n            // Controller is allowed, but we still log every privileged\n            // invocation so the audit trail records it.\n            info!(\n                request_id = %self.request_id,\n                session_id = ?self.session_id,\n                tool = %name,\n                \"Controller session invoking privileged tool\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Check turn limit\n        self.increment_turn()?;\n        \n        // Check timeout\n        if self.is_timed_out() {\n            anyhow::bail!(\"Request timed out after {} seconds\", self.config.timeout_secs);\n        }\n        \n"}}

The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. tool.name.to_lowercase().contains(&query)\n                    || tool.description.to_lowercase().contains(&query)\n                    || tool.category.to_lowercase().contains(&query)\n  async fn handle_initialize(&self, request: McpRequest) -> McpResponse {\n        info!(\"Compact MCP initialized\");\n\n        McpResponse::success(\n            request.id,\n            json!({\n       let port = cli\n                .grpc_port\n                .unwrap_or(if cli.mode == \"grpc\" { 50051 } else { 50052 });\n            let addr: std::net::SocketAddr = format!(\"0.0.0.0:{}\", transport\");\n            HttpSseTransport::new(addr).serve(server).await\n        }));\n    }\n\n    // Spawn WebSocket transport\n    if let Some(addr) = ws_addr {\n        let server = server.clone();\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-05-27T03:07:14.329Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_JimonnLLDWLGyVuTuXLrtPJn","output":"Chunk ID: 5e35cb\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 890\nOutput:\n# op-dbus MCP Server Configuration Examples\n\nThis directory contains example MCP server configurations for various AI clients.\n\n## MCP Endpoints\n\nThe op-dbus MCP server exposes three main modes at `https://op-dbus.ghostbridge.tech`:\n\n| Mode | SSE Endpoint | POST Endpoint | Description |\n|------|--------------|---------------|-------------|\n| **Compact** | `/mcp/compact` | `/mcp/compact/message` | 4 meta-tools for efficient tool discovery |\n| **Standard** | `/mcp/sse` | `/mcp/message` | All tools exposed directly |\n| **Agents** | `/mcp/agents` | `/mcp/agents/message` | Specialized AI agents |\n\n### Compact Mode (Recommended for AI Clients)\nExposes 4 meta-tools instead of the full tool list:\n- `list_tools` - Browse tools with pagination\n- `search_tools` - Search tools by keyword\n- `get_tool_schema` - Get schema for a specific tool\n- `execute_tool` - Execute any underlying tool\n\n### Standard Mode\nExposes all tools directly via `tools/list`. Best for clients that can handle large tool lists.\n\n### Agents Mode\nSpecialized AI agents for enhanced capabilities:\n- `memory` - Key-value memory (remember, recall, forget)\n- `context_manager` - Context persistence (save, load, list, delete)\n- `sequential_thinking` - Step-by-step reasoning\n- `mem0` - Semantic memory (add, search, get_all, delete, update)\n- `search_specialist` - Code/docs/web search\n- `deployment` - Service deployment (deploy, rollback, status)\n- `python_pro` - Python analysis and refactoring\n- `debugger` - Error analysis and tracing\n- `prompt_engineer` - Prompt generation and optimization\n\n## Configuration Files\n\n| File | Client | Notes |\n|------|--------|-------|\n| `cursor-mcp.json` | Cursor IDE | Uses `url` key |\n| `codex-mcp.json` | Codex Client | Uses `mcpServers` with SSE transport |\n| `vscode-mcp.json` | VS Code (Copilot Chat) | Uses `mcp.servers` structure |\n| `claude-desktop-mcp.json` | Claude Desktop | Prefers stdio transport |\n| `openai-mcp.json` | OpenAI tools | Array-based servers list |\n| `generic-mcp.json` | Reference | Complete with all endpoints |\n\n## Installation\n\n### System-wide (Recommended)\n```bash\nsudo mkdir -p /etc/mcp\nsudo cp *.json /etc/mcp/\n```\n\n### Cursor\n```bash\n# Project-level\nmkdir -p .cursor\ncp cursor-mcp.json .cursor/mcp.json\n\n# User-level\ncp cursor-mcp.json ~/.cursor/mcp.json\n```\n\n### VS Code\nAdd the contents of `vscode-mcp.json` to your VS Code `settings.json`:\n```json\n{\n  \"mcp\": {\n{\n  \"$schema\": \"https://spec.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/mcp-config.json\",\n  \"name\": \"op-dbus\",\n  \"description\": \"op-dbus MCP Server - System administration tools\",\n  \"version\": \"2.0.0\",\n  \n  \"endpoints\": {\n    \"sse\": {\n      \"url\": \"http://localhost:8080/mcp/sse\",\n      \"description\": \"SSE transport for LLM clients (Gemini CLI, Claude, etc.)\"\n    },\n    \"compact\": {\n      \"url\": \"http://localhost:8080/mcp/compact\",\n      \"description\": \"Compact mode - 4 meta-tools for efficient discovery\"\n    },\n    \"agents\": {\n      \"url\": \"http://localhost:8080/mcp/agents\",\n      \"description\": \"AI agents endpoint\"\n    }\n  },\n  \n  \"tools_summary\": {\n    \"total\": 145,\n    \"categories\": {\n      \"dbus_systemd\": \"Service management (start, stop, restart, status)\",\n      \"dbus_packagekit\": \"Package installation\",\n      \"ovs\": \"Open vSwitch bridge/port management\",\n      \"openflow\": \"OpenFlow rule management\",\n      \"rtnetlink\": \"Kernel network interface configuration\",\n      \"lxc\": \"Container management\",\n      \"file\": \"File operations\"\n    }\n  },\n  \n  \"authentication\": {\n    \"type\": \"none\",\n    \"note\": \"Add Bearer token auth for production\"\n  }\n}\n"}}

HTTP Transport\n//!\n//! HTTP/REST transport with SSE support.\n//! Provides three variants:\n//! - HttpTransport: REST only\n//! - SseTransport: SSE only (for clients that use separate SSE + POST)\n//! - HttpSseTransport: Combined bidirectional (recommended)\n//!\n//! Authentication (audit item #3):\n//!   - `/health` is always open.\n//!   - Real socket-loopback callers bypass auth (Host header is NEVER trusted).\n//!   - All other callers must present `Authorization: Bearer <token>` AND the\n//!     token must be accepted by the configured [`AuthValidator`].\n//!   - The default validator is fail-secure: it only accepts tokens listed in\n//!     `OPDBUS_MCP_ALLOWED_PEERS`. If that env var is unset/empty, every\n//!     bearer token is rejected.\n\nuse super::{McpHandler, Transport};\nuse crate::McpRequest;\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse axum::{\n    extract::{ConnectInfo, State},\n    http::{HeaderMap, StatusCode},\n    middleware,\n    response::{\n        sse::{Event, Sse},\n        IntoResponse, Json, Response,\n    },\n    routing::{get, post},\n    Router,\n};\nuse futures::stream::{self, Stream};\nuse simd_json::{json, OwnedValue as Value};\nuse std::convert::Infallible;\nuse std::net::SocketAddr;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::time::Duration;\nuse tokio::sync::broadcast;\nuse tower_http::cors::{Any, CorsLayer};\nuse tracing::{debug, info, warn};\nuse uuid::Uuid;\n\n// =============================================================================\n// AuthValidator (audit item #3)\n//\n// The previous implementation accepted ANY token that matched the *shape* of a\n// WireGuard pubkey or a UUID. That was not authentication; it was a regex.\n// Real authorization now goes through an `AuthValidator`. The default\n// `EnvAllowListValidator` is fail-secure: with no entries, it rejects every\n// bearer token, and only loopback callers can reach the handlers.\n// =============================================================================\n\n/// Validates an opaque bearer token against an authoritative source\n/// (WireGuard peer DB, A.N.N.A. Scribe session ledger, etc.).\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\npub trait AuthValidator: Send + Sync + 'static {\n    async fn validate(&self, token: &str) -> bool;\n}\n\n/// Default validator backed by the `OPDBUS_MCP_ALLOWED_PEERS` env var\n/// (comma-separated list of allowed pubkeys and/or session UUIDs).\n///\n/// * If the env var is unset or empty, **every** bearer token is rejected.\n/// * Comparisons are constant-time over the candidate's length to prevent\n///   timing oracles on partial matches.\npub struct EnvAllowListValidator {\n    allowed: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl EnvAllowListValidator {\n    /// Read the allow-list from `OPDBUS_MCP_ALLOWED_PEERS`.\n    pub fn from_env() -> Self {\n        let raw = std::env::var(\"OPDBUS_MCP_ALLOWED_PEERS\").unwrap_or_default();\n        let allowed: Vec<String> = raw\n            .split(',')\n            .map(|s| s.trim().to_string())\n            .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())\n            .collect();\n        if allowed.is_empty() {\n            warn!(\n                \"OPDBUS_MCP_ALLOWED_PEERS is empty; bearer-token auth will reject all tokens. \\\n                 Only loopback callers will be accepted.\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            info!(count = allowed.len(), \"Loaded MCP peer allow-list\");\n        }\n        Self { allowed }\n    }\n\n    /// Construct an allow-list directly (primarily for tests and embedders).\n    pub fn new<I, S>(entries: I) -> Self\n    where\n        I: IntoIterator<Item = S>,\n        S: Into<String>,\n    {\n        Self {\n            allowed: entries.into_iter().map(Into::into).collect(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\nimpl AuthValidator for EnvAllowListValidator {\n    async fn validate(&self, token: &str) -> bool {\n        // Cheap defense-in-depth pre-filter: reject anything that cannot\n        // possibly be a WireGuard pubkey or session UUID before we even\n        // touch the allow-list.\n        if !is_wireguard_auth_token_shape(token) {\n            return false;\n        }\n        let token_bytes = token.as_bytes();\n        // OR the comparison results so total work is independent of which\n        // (if any) entry matches. `ct_eq` itself runs in time proportional\n        // only to the shared length of its inputs.\n        let mut matched = false;\n        for entry in &self.allowed {\n            matched |= ct_eq(token_bytes, entry.as_bytes());\n        }\n        matched\n    }\n}\n\n/// Constant-time byte-slice equality. Returns false on length mismatch\n/// (length is not considered secret; the contents are).\nfn ct_eq(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> bool {\n    if a.len() != b.len() {\n        return false;\n    }\n    let mut diff: u8 = 0;\n    for (x, y) in a.iter().zip(b.iter()) {\n        diff |= x ^ y;\n    }\n    diff == 0\n}\n\nfn extract_bearer_token(headers: &HeaderMap) -> Option<&str> {\n    headers\n        .get(\"authorization\")\n        .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())\n        .and_then(|value| value.trim().strip_prefix(\"Bearer \"))\n        .map(str::trim)\n        .filter(|token| !token.is_empty())\n}\n\nfn is_wireguard_pubkey_shape(token: &str) -> bool {\n    token.len() == 44\n        && token.ends_with('=')\n        && token\n            .chars()\n            .all(|ch| ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(ch, '+' | '/' | '='))\n}\n\nfn is_wireguard_session_id_shape(token: &str) -> bool {\n    Uuid::parse_str(token).is_ok()\n}\n\n/// **Shape check only.** Used as a cheap pre-filter inside the validator.\n/// MUST NOT be used as an authorization decision on its own.\nfn is_wireguard_auth_token_shape(token: &str) -> bool {\n    is_wireguard_pubkey_shape(token) || is_wireguard_session_id_shape(token)\n}\n\nfn is_loopback_addr(addr: &SocketAddr) -> bool {\n    addr.ip().is_loopback()\n}\n\n/// Authentication middleware.\n///\n/// Loopback bypass uses the **actual socket peer address**, not the\n/// attacker-controlled `Host` header. Any non-loopback caller must present a\n/// bearer token accepted by the configured [`AuthValidator`].\nasync fn wireguard_auth_middleware(\n    State(validator): State<Arc<dyn AuthValidator>>,\n    connect_info: Option<ConnectInfo<SocketAddr>>,\n    headers: HeaderMap,\n    mut request: axum::extract::Request,\n    next: axum::middleware::Next,\n) -> Result<axum::response::Response, StatusCode> {\n    // /health is always open\n    if request.uri().path() == \"/health\" {\n        return Ok(next.run(request).await);\n    }\n\n    // Loopback bypass uses the real peer IP. The Host header is never trusted.\n    if let Some(ConnectInfo(peer)) = connect_info {\n        if is_loopback_addr(&peer) {\n            return Ok(next.run(request).await);\n        }\n    }\n\n    let Some(token) = extract_bearer_token(&headers) else {\n        warn!(\"Rejected HTTP MCP request without bearer token\");\n        return Err(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED);\n    };\n\n    if !validator.validate(token).await {\n        warn!(\"Rejected HTTP MCP request: bearer token not in allow-list\");\n        return Err(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED);\n    }\n\n    debug!(\"Accepted HTTP MCP request with validated bearer token\");\n    request.extensions_mut().insert(token.to_string());\n    Ok(next.run(request).await)\n}\n\n/// Shared state for HTTP handlers\nstruct HttpState<H> {\n    handler: Arc<H>,\n    event_tx: broadcast::Sender<String>,\n}\n\nfn default_validator() -> Arc<dyn AuthValidator> {\n    Arc::new(EnvAllowListValidator::from_env())\n}\n\n/// HTTP-only transport (REST endpoints)\npub struct HttpTransport {\n    bind_addr: String,\n    enable_cors: bool,\n    validator: Arc<dyn AuthValidator>,\n}\n\nimpl HttpTransport {\n    pub fn new(bind_addr: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            bind_addr: bind_addr.into(),\n            enable_cors: true,\n            validator: default_validator(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn without_cors(mut self) -> Self {\n        self.enable_cors = false;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Inject a custom authorization backend (e.g. a live WireGuard peer DB).\n    /// Defaults to [`EnvAllowListValidator::from_env`].\n    pub fn with_auth_validator(mut self, validator: Arc<dyn AuthValidator>) -> Self {\n        self.validator = validator;\n        self\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\nimpl Transport for HttpTransport {\n    async fn serve<H: McpHandler + 'static>(self, handler: Arc<H>) -> Result<()> {\n        info!(addr = %self.bind_addr, Doing so\n# leaves /run/s6-rc/state from the old database paired with a new compiled DB,\n# which makes future s6-rc commands fail with \"unable to read valid state\".\nset -eu\n\nS6_SV=${S6_SV:-/etc/s6/sv}\nS6_ADMIN=${S6_ADMIN:-/etc/s6/adminsv}\nS6_COMPILED_LINK=${S6_COMPILED_LINK:-/etc/s6/rc/compiled}\nS6_DB_ROOT=${S6_DB_ROOT:-/etc/s6/rc}\nLABEL=${1:-local}\n\nif ! If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}

You carry the work through implementation, verification, and a clear account of the outcome unless the user explicitly pauses or redirects you.\\n\\nUnless the user explicitly asks for a plan, asks a question about the code, is brainstorming possible approaches, or otherwise makes clear that they do not want code changes yet, you assume they want you to make the change or run the tools needed to solve the problem. In those cases, do not stop at a proposal; implement the fix. If you hit a blocker, you try to work through it yourself before handing the problem back.\\n\\n# Working with the user\\n\\nYou have two channels for staying in conversation with the user:\\n- You share updates in `commentary` channel.\\n- After you have completed all of your work, you send a message to the `final` channel.\\n\\nThe user may send messages while you are working. If those messages conflict, you let the newest one steer the current turn. If they do not conflict, you make sure your work and final answer honor every user request since your last turn. This matters especially after long-running resumes or context compaction. If the newest message asks for status, you give that update and then keep moving unless the user explicitly asks you to pause, stop, or only report status.\\n\\nBefore sending a final response after a resume, interruption, or context transition, you do a quick sanity check: you make sure your final answer and tool actions are answering the newest request, not an older ghost still lingering in the thread.\\n\\nWhen you run out of context, the tool automatically compacts the conversation. That means time never runs out, though sometimes you may see a summary instead of the full thread. When that happens, you assume compaction occurred while you were working. Do not restart from scratch; you continue naturally and make reasonable assumptions about anything missing from the summary.\\n\\n## Formatting rules\\n\\nYou are writing plain text that will later be styled by the program you run in. Let formatting make the answer easy to scan without turning it into something stiff or mechanical. Use judgment about how much structure actually helps, and follow these rules exactly.\\n\\n- You may format with GitHub-flavored Markdown.\\n- You add structure only when the task calls for it. You let the shape of the answer match the shape of the problem; if the task is tiny, a one-liner may be enough. Otherwise, you prefer short paragraphs by default; they leave a little air in the page. You order sections from general to specific to supporting detail.\\n- Avoid nested bullets unless the user explicitly asks for them. Keep lists flat. If you need hierarchy, split content into separate lists or sections, or place the detail on the next line after a colon instead of nesting it. For numbered lists, use only the `1. 2. 3.` style, never `1)`. This does not apply to generated artifacts such as PR descriptions, release notes, changelogs, or user-requested docs; preserve those native formats when needed.\\n- Headers are optional; you use them only when they genuinely help. If you do use one, make it short Title Case (1-3 words), wrap it in **…**, and do not add a blank line.\\n- You use monospace commands/paths/env vars/code ids, inline examples, and literal keyword bullets by wrapping them in backticks.\\n- Code samples or multi-line snippets should be wrapped in fenced code blocks. Avoid long-winded explanation. In casual conversation, you just talk like a person. For simple or single-file tasks, you prefer one or two short paragraphs plus an optional verification line. {"timestamp":"2026-05-27T07:08:07.669Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_mYR6xM6MO8vLYbVyzvcWCfRn","output":"Chunk ID: a1f5a5\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 2752\nOutput:\n> ## Documentation Index\n> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.factory.ai/llms.txt\n> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.\n\n# Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)\n\n> Connect your own API keys, use open source models, or run local models\n\nThe Droid CLI supports custom model configurations through BYOK (Bring Your Own Key). Use your own OpenAI or Anthropic keys, connect to any open source model providers, or run models locally on your hardware. Once configured, switch between models using the `/model` command.\n\nFor Factory-managed models and multipliers, see [Available Models](/models).\n\n<Note>\n  Your API keys remain local and are not uploaded to Factory servers. Custom models are only available in the CLI and won't appear in Factory's web or mobile platforms.\n</Note>\n\n<img src=\"https://mintcdn.com/factory/76eHQsYrywYjfJno/images/custom_models.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=76eHQsYrywYjfJno&q=85&s=5e8af07b3c42614e2c32c43e8a04d146\" alt=\"Model selector showing custom models\" width=\"1376\" height=\"1166\" data-path=\"images/custom_models.png\" />\n\n[Install the CLI with the 5-minute quickstart →](/cli/getting-started/quickstart)\n\n***\n\n## Configuration Reference\n\nAdd custom models to `~/.factory/settings.json` under the `customModels` array:\n\n```json theme={null}\n{\n  \"customModels\": [\n    {\n      \"model\": \"your-model-id\",\n      \"displayName\": \"My Custom Model\",\n      \"baseUrl\": \"https://api.provider.com/v1\",\n      \"apiKey\": \"${PROVIDER_API_KEY}\",\n      \"provider\": \"generic-chat-completion-api\",\n      \"maxOutputTokens\": 16384\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n<Tip>\n  In `settings.json` (and `settings.local.json`), `apiKey` supports environment variable references using `${VAR_NAME}` syntax. For example, `\"apiKey\": \"${PROVIDER_API_KEY}\"` reads from the environment variable named `PROVIDER_API_KEY` (for example: `export PROVIDER_API_KEY=your_key_here`).\n</Tip>\n\n<Note>\n  **Legacy support**: Custom models in `~/.factory/config.json` using snake\\_case field names (`custom_models`, `base_url`, etc.) are still supported for backwards compatibility. Both files are loaded and merged, with `settings.json` taking priority. Env var expansion for `apiKey` applies to `settings.json`/`settings.local.json` and not to legacy `config.json`.\n</Note>\n\n### Supported Fields\n\n| Field             | Type      | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                    |\n| ----------------- | --------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `model`           | `string`  | ✓        | Model identifier sent via API (e.g., `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`, `gpt-5-codex`, `qwen3:4b`)                                                                                                  |\n| `displayName`     | `string`  |          | Human-friendly name shown in model selector                                                                                                                                                    |\n| `baseUrl`         | `string`  | ✓        | API endpoint base URL                                                                                                                                                                          |\n| `apiKey`          | `string`  | ✓        | Your API key for the provider. Can't be empty. Supports `${VAR_NAME}` in `settings.json`/`settings.local.json` (e.g., `${PROVIDER_API_KEY}` uses the `PROVIDER_API_KEY` environment variable). |\n| `provider`        | `string`  | ✓        | One of: `anthropic`, `openai`, or `generic-chat-completion-api`                                                                                                                                |\n| `maxOutputTokens` | `number`  |          | Maximum output tokens for model responses                                                                                                                                                      |\n| `noImageSupport`  | `boolean` |          | Set to `true` to disable image inputs for this model                                                                                                                                           |\n| `extraArgs`       | `object`  |          | Additional provider-specific arguments to include in API requests                                                                                                                              |\n| `extraHeaders`    | `object`  |          | Additional HTTP headers to send with requests                                                                                                                                                  |\n\n### Using extraArgs\n\nPass provider-specific parameters like temperature or top\\_p:\n\n```json theme={null}\n{\n  \"customModels\": [\n    {\n      \"model\": \"your-model\",\n      \"displayName\": \"Custom Model\",\n      \"baseUrl\": \"https://your-provider.com/v1\",\n      \"apiKey\": \"YOUR_API_KEY\",\n      \"provider\": \"generic-chat-completion-api\",\n      \"extraArgs\": {\n        \"temperature\": 0.7,\n        \"top_p\": 0.9\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n### Using extraHeaders\n\nAdd custom HTTP headers to API requests:\n\n```json theme={null}\n{\n  \"customModels\": [\n    {\n      \"model\": \"your-model\",\n      \"displayName\": \"Custom Model\",\n      \"baseUrl\": \"https://your-provider.com/v1\",\n      \"apiKey\": \"YOUR_API_KEY\",\n      \"provider\": \"generic-chat-completion-api\",\n      \"extraHeaders\": {\n        \"X-Custom-Header\": \"value\",\n        \"Authorization\": \"Bearer YOUR_TOKEN\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n***\n\n## Understanding Providers\n\nFactory supports three provider types that determine API compatibility:\n\n| Provider                      | API Format                           | Use For                                                                                                               | Documentation                                                                      |\n| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `anthropic`                   | Anthropic Messages API (v1/messages) | Anthropic models on their official API or compatible proxies                                                          | [Anthropic Messages API](https://docs.claude.com/en/api/messages)                  |\n| `openai`                      | OpenAI Responses API                 | OpenAI models on their official API or compatible proxies. Required for the newest models like GPT-5 and GPT-5-Codex. | [OpenAI Responses API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses)   |\n| `generic-chat-completion-api` | OpenAI Chat Completions API          | OpenRouter, Fireworks, Together AI, Ollama, vLLM, and most open-source providers                                      | [OpenAI Chat Completions API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat) |\n\n<Warning>\n  Factory is actively verifying Droid's performance on popular models, but we cannot guarantee that all custom models will work out of the box. Only Anthropic and OpenAI models accessed via their official APIs are fully tested and benchmarked.\n</Warning>\n\n<Note>\n  **Model Size Consideration**: Models below 30 billion parameters have shown significantly lower performance on agentic coding tasks. While these smaller models can be useful for experimentation and learning, they are generally not recommended for production coding work or complex software engineering tasks.\n</Note>\n\n***\n\n## Prompt Caching\n\nThe Droid CLI automatically uses prompt caching when available to reduce API costs:\n\n* **Official providers (`anthropic`, `openai`)**: Factory attempts to use prompt caching via the official APIs. Caching behavior follows each provider's implementation and requirements.\n* **Generic providers (`generic-chat-completion-api`)**: Prompt caching support varies by provider and cannot be guaranteed. Some providers may support caching, while others may not.\n\n### Verifying Prompt Caching\n\nTo check if prompt caching is working correctly with your custom model:\n\n1. Run a conversation with your custom model\n2. Use the `/cost` command in the Droid CLI to view cost breakdowns\n3. Look for cache hit rates and savings in the output\n\nIf you're not seeing expected caching savings, consult your provider's documentation about their prompt caching support and requirements.\n\n***\n\n## Quick Start\n\nChoose a provider from the left navigation to see specific configuration examples:\n\n* **[Baseten](/cli/byok/baseten)** - Deploy and serve custom models\n* **[DeepInfra](/cli/byok/deepinfra)** - Cost-effective inference for open-source models\n* **[Fireworks AI](/cli/byok/fireworks)** - High-performance inference for open-source models\n* **[Google Gemini](/cli/byok/google-gemini)** - Access Google's Gemini models\n* **[Groq](/cli/byok/groq)** - Ultra-fast inference with Groq's LPU™ Inference Engine\n* **[Hugging Face](/cli/byok/huggingface)** - Connect to models on HF Inference API\n* **[Ollama](/cli/byok/ollama)** - Run models locally or in the cloud\n* **[OpenAI & Anthropic](/cli/byok/openai-anthropic)** - Use your own API keys for official models\n* **[OpenRouter](/cli/byok/openrouter)** - Access multiple providers through a single interface\n\n***\n\n## Using Custom Models\n\nOnce configured, access your custom models in the CLI:\n\n1. Use the `/model` command\n2. Your custom models appear in a separate \"Custom models\" section below Factory-provided models\n3. Select any model to start using it\n\nCustom models display with the name you set in `displayName`, making it easy to identify different providers and configurations.\n\n***\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### Model not appearing in selector\n\n* Check JSON syntax in `~/.factory/settings.json` (or `config.json` if using legacy format)\n* Settings changes are detected automatically via file watching\n* Verify all required fields are present\n\n### \"Invalid provider\" error\n\n* Provider must be exactly `anthropic`, `openai`, or `generic-chat-completion-api`\n* Check for typos and ensure proper capitalization\n\n### Authentication errors\n\n* Verify your API key is valid and has available credits\n* Check that the API key has proper permissions\n* Confirm the base URL matches your provider's documentation\n\n### Local model won't connect\n\n* Ensure your local server is running (e.g., `ollama serve`)\n* Verify the base URL is correct and includes `/v1/` suffix if required\n* Check that the model is pulled/available locally\n\n### Rate limiting or quota errors\n\n* Check your provider's rate limits and usage quotas\n* Monitor your usage through your provider's dashboard\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-05-27T07:08:07.973Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_4B29BEg18YLNYxgWEaLy84dA","output":"Chunk ID: dec0ab\nWall time: 0.2490 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 5955\nOutput:\n> ## Documentation Index\n> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.factory.ai/llms.txt\n> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.\n\n# Settings\n\n> Configure how droid behaves and integrates with your workflow.\n\n## Accessing settings\n\nTo configure droid settings:\n\n1. Run `droid`\n2. Enter `/settings`\n3. Adjust your preferences interactively\n\nChanges take effect immediately and are saved to your settings file.\n\n## Where settings live\n\n| OS            | Location                               |\n| ------------- | -------------------------------------- |\n| macOS / Linux | `~/.factory/settings.json`             |\n| Windows       | `%USERPROFILE%\\.factory\\settings.json` |\n\nIf the file doesn't exist, it's created with defaults the first time you run **droid**.\n\n### Local overrides\n\nYou can create a `settings.local.json` alongside `settings.json` in any `.factory/` folder:\n\n* `~/.factory/settings.local.json` (user-level)\n* `<project>/.factory/settings.local.json` (project-level)\n\nLocal overrides merge on top of the corresponding `settings.json` at the same level and follow the same hierarchy precedence. Add `settings.local.json` to `.gitignore` if you want to keep machine-specific preferences out of version control.\n\n## Legacy Droid YAML configuration\n\n`.droid.yaml` was an older project configuration surface. Use the current `.factory/` files instead:\n\n* Use `settings.json` and `settings.local.json` for Droid preferences and local overrides.\n* Use [AGENTS.md](/cli/configuration/agents-md) for repository instructions, conventions, and validation commands.\n* Use [MCP servers](/cli/configuration/mcp), [hooks](/cli/configuration/hooks-guide), and [skills](/cli/configuration/skills) for integrations, automation, and reusable workflows.\n\n## Available settings\n\n| Setting                                  | Options                                                                    | Default                       | Description                                                                    |\n| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `model`                                  | Any [available model ID](/models)                                          | Product default               | The default AI model used by droid                                             |\n| `reasoningEffort`                        | `off`, `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high` (availability depends on the model) | Model-dependent default       | Controls how much structured thinking the model performs.                      |\n| `sessionDefaultSettings.interactionMode` | `auto`, `spec`                                                             | `auto`                        | Sets whether new sessions start in Auto or Spec Mode.                          |\n| `sessionDefaultSettings.autonomyLevel`   | `off`, `low`, `medium`, `high`                                             | `off`                         | Sets the default [Autonomy Level](/cli/user-guides/auto-run) for new sessions. |\n| `cloudSessionSync`                       | `true`, `false`                                                            | `true`                        | Mirror CLI sessions to Factory web.                                            |\n| `diffMode`                               | `github`, `unified`                                                        | `github`                      | Choose between split GitHub-style diffs and a single-column view.              |\n| `completionSound`                        | `off`, `bell`, `fx-ok01`, `fx-ack01`, or custom file path                  | `fx-ok01`                     | Audio cue when a response finishes.                                            |\n| `awaitingInputSound`                     | `off`, `bell`, `fx-ok01`, `fx-ack01`, or custom file path                  | `fx-ack01`                    | Audio cue when droid is waiting for user input.                                |\n| `soundFocusMode`                         | `always`, `focused`, `unfocused`                                           | `always`                      | When to play sound notifications.                                              |\n| `commandAllowlist`                       | Array of commands                                                          | Safe defaults provided        | Commands that run without extra confirmation.                                  |\n| `commandDenylist`                        | Array of commands                                                          | Restrictive defaults provided | Commands that always require confirmation.                                     |\n| `includeCoAuthoredByDroid`               | `true`, `false`                                                            | `true`                        | Automatically append the Droid co-author trailer to commits.                   |\n| `enableDroidShield`                      | `true`, `false`                                                            | `true`                        | Enable secret scanning and git guardrails.                                     |\n| `hooksDisabled`                          | `true`, `false`                                                            | `false`                       | Globally disable all hooks execution.                                          |\n| `ideAutoConnect`                         | `true`, `false`                                                            | `false`                       | Auto-connect to IDE from external terminals.                                   |\n| `showThinkingInMainView`                 | `true`, `false`                                                            | `false`                       | Display AI thinking/reasoning blocks in the main chat view.                    |\n| `customModels`                           | Array of model configs                                                     | `[]`                          | Custom model configurations for BYOK. See [BYOK docs](/cli/byok/overview).     |\n\n### Model\n\nSet `model` to a [model ID from Available Models](/models). For custom models, see [Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)](/cli/byok/overview).\n\n### Reasoning effort\n\n`reasoningEffort` adjusts how much structured thinking the model performs before replying. Available values depend on the model, but typically include:\n\n* **`off` / `none`** – disable structured reasoning (fastest).\n* **`low`**, **`medium`**, **`high`** – progressively increase deliberation time for more complex reasoning.\n\nAnthropic models default to `off`, while GPT-5 starts on `medium`.\n\n### Autonomy level\n\nUse `sessionDefaultSettings.interactionMode` to choose whether new sessions start in Auto or Spec Mode, and `sessionDefaultSettings.autonomyLevel` to set the default [Autonomy Level](/cli/user-guides/auto-run). `off` keeps manual approvals; `low`, `medium`, and `high` pre-authorize work at or below that risk level.\n\n`sessionDefaultSettings.autonomyMode` is deprecated and retained for older configurations.\n\n### Diff mode\n\nControl how droid displays code changes:\n\n* **`github`** – Side-by-side, higher fidelity render (recommended).\n* **`unified`** – Traditional single-column diff format.\n\n### Cloud session sync\n\nWhen this switch is on, every CLI session is mirrored to Factory web so you can revisit conversations in the browser:\n\n* **`true`** – Sync sessions to the web app.\n* **`false`** – Keep sessions local only.\n\n### Sound notifications\n\nConfigure audio feedback for droid events:\n\n**Completion sound** (`completionSound`) - plays when a response finishes:\n\n* **`fx-ok01`** – Built-in completion sound (default) - soft success bloop\n* **`fx-ack01`** – Alternative built-in sound effect - tactile ripple feedback\n* **`bell`** – Use the system terminal bell\n* **`off`** – No sound notifications\n* **Custom path** – Provide a file path to your own sound file (e.g., `\"/path/to/sound.wav\"`)\n\n**Awaiting input sound** (`awaitingInputSound`) - plays when droid is waiting for user input. Same options as completion sound, defaults to `fx-ack01`.\n\n**Sound focus mode** (`soundFocusMode`) - controls when sounds play:\n\n* **`always`** – Play sounds regardless of window focus (default)\n* **`focused`** – Only play sounds when the terminal is focused\n* **`unfocused`** – Only play sounds when the terminal is not focused\n\n<Note>Access sound settings via `/settings` or `Shift+Tab` → **Settings** in the TUI.</Note>\n\n### Hooks\n\nThe `hooksDisabled` setting provides a global toggle to disable all hooks execution without removing your hook configurations:\n\n* **`false`** – Hooks are enabled and will execute normally (default)\n* **`true`** – All hooks are disabled globally\n\nYou can also toggle this from the `/hooks` menu or `/settings`.\n\n### IDE auto-connect\n\nThe `ideAutoConnect` setting controls whether droid automatically connects to your IDE when running from external terminals (outside the IDE's built-in terminal):\n\n* **`false`** – Only auto-connect when running inside IDE terminal (default)\n* **`true`** – Auto-connect to IDE from any terminal\n\n## Command allowlist & denylist\n\nUse these settings to control which commands droid can execute automatically and which it must never run:\n\n* **`commandAllowlist`** – Commands in this array are treated as safe and run without additional confirmation, regardless of autonomy prompts. Include only low-risk utilities you rely on frequently (for example `ls`, `pwd`, `dir`).\n* **`commandDenylist`** – Commands in this array always require confirmation and are typically blocked because they are destructive or unsafe (for example recursive `rm`, `mkfs`, or privileged system operations).\n\nCommands that appear in both lists default to the denylist behavior. Any command that is in neither list falls back to the autonomy level you selected for the session.\n\n### Example allow/deny configuration\n\n```json theme={null}\n{\n  \"commandAllowlist\": [\"ls\", \"pwd\", \"dir\"],\n  \"commandDenylist\": [\"rm -rf /\", \"mkfs\", \"shutdown\"]\n}\n```\n\nReview and update these arrays periodically to match your workflow and security posture, especially when sharing configurations across teams.\n\n## Session defaults\n\nDefaults applied when a new session starts. See also `sessionDefaultSettings.interactionMode` and `sessionDefaultSettings.autonomyLevel` in the table above.\n\n| Setting                                          | Type   | Options                                | Default        | Description                                               |\n| ------------------------------------------------ | ------ | -------------------------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `sessionDefaultSettings.specModeModel`           | string | Any [available model ID](/models)      | Inherits model | Override the model used when sessions start in Spec Mode. |\n| `sessionDefaultSettings.specModeReasoningEffort` | string | `off`, `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high` | Model default  | Reasoning effort applied to the spec model.               |\n\n## Display and UI\n\nTune how droid renders content in the terminal.\n\n| Setting                   | Type    | Options                  | Default      | Description                                                                |\n| ------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------ | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `toolResultDisplay`       | string  | `expanded`, `compact`    | `expanded`   | How tool results are rendered in the transcript.                           |\n| `showTokenUsageIndicator` | boolean | `true`, `false`          | `false`      | Show the live token usage indicator at the bottom of the input.            |\n| `logoAnimation`           | string  | `once`, `always`, `off`  | `once`       | Animate the droid logo on startup.                                         |\n| `theme`                   | string {\n        llm,\n        vertex,\n        rate_limiter: Arc::new(Mutex::new(TokenBucket::new(rpm))),\n    });\n    let app = Router::new()\n        .route(\"/v1/chat/completions\", post(chat_completions))\n        .route(\"/v1/models\", get(list_models))\n        .with_state(state)\n        .layer(middleware::from_fn(log_request));\n\n    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(addr).await?;\n    info!(\"HTTP server listening on {}\", addr);\n    axum::serve(listener, app).await?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n"}}

Invoked by /security-review when the user opts into \\\"thorough\\\" mode. Uses a heterogeneous multi-model jury (latest Opus + latest GPT + latest Gemini). A mandatory 3-pass floor (line-anchor verification, vendor prior-art, deep prior-art) runs against every Pass 0 lieutenant-seeded candidate; a conditional escalation tier (dataflow + reachability, exploit construction, adversarial red-team disprove) fires on per-finding triggers. Produces FINDINGS.md, JUDGE.md, STATUS.md, severity-sorted master list, and optional PoC + evidence artifacts for that repo.
