Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\\n\\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \\\"Snowball\\\" session.\\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\\\"Law Firm\\\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \\\"The Sled\\\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \\\"The Shuttle\\\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \\\"The Snowball\\\" (appended session ledger), and \\\"The Strike/Etch\\\" (generating the hash).\\n\\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \\\"Reality\\\")\\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\\n\\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\\n\\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\\n\\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\\n**Rust Workspace**\\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\\n\\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\\n\\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\\n\\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\\n\\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\\n\\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\\n</coding_guidelines>\"}],\"designGuidelinesInfo\":[]},\"uiRenderCutoffMessageId\":\"53e38b86-7670-4bfe-8993-f28dd88a8a2d\"}\n"}}

The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}

Codex CLI backend for the local OpenAI-compatible proxy.\n//!\n//! This keeps ChatGPT/Codex OAuth in `~/.codex/auth.json`. Factory Droid only sees\n//! the loopback proxy and a dummy BYOK token.\n\nuse anyhow::{anyhow, Context};\nuse serde_json::Value;\nuse std::process::Stdio;\nuse tokio::io::AsyncWriteExt;\nuse tokio::process::Command;\nuse tokio::time::{timeout, Duration};\n\nconst DEFAULT_PROXY_MODEL: &str = \"codex-gpt-5.5\";\nconst DEFAULT_CODEX_MODEL: &str = \"gpt-5.5\";\n\npub fn enabled() -> bool {\n    env_flag(\"CODEX_PROXY_ENABLE\", false) || std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_MODEL\").is_ok()\n}\n\npub fn advertised_model() -> String {\n    std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_ADVERTISED_MODEL\")\n        .or_else(|_| std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_MODEL\"))\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| DEFAULT_PROXY_MODEL.to_string())\n}\n\npub fn is_codex_model(model: &str) -> bool {\n    let norm = model.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();\n    enabled()\n        && (norm == advertised_model().to_ascii_lowercase()\n            || norm.starts_with(\"codex:\")\n            || norm.starts_with(\"codex-\"))\n}\n\npub async fn generate(model: &str, messages: &[Value]) -> anyhow::Result<String> {\n    let prompt = render_messages(messages);\n    let codex_model = resolve_codex_model(model);\n    let codex_bin = std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_BIN\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \"codex\".to_string());\n    let cwd = std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_CWD\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \"/tmp\".to_string());\n    let timeout_secs = std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_TIMEOUT_SECS\")\n        .ok()\n        .and_then(|v| v.parse::<u64>().ok())\n        .filter(|v| *v >= 5)\n        .unwrap_or(180);\n\n    let mut child = Command::new(codex_bin)\n        .arg(\"exec\")\n        .arg(\"--ephemeral\")\n        .arg(\"--skip-git-repo-check\")\n        .arg(\"--ignore-rules\")\n        .arg(\"--sandbox\")\n        .arg(\"read-only\")\n        .arg(\"--cd\")\n        .arg(cwd)\n        .arg(\"-m\")\n        .arg(codex_model)\n        .arg(\"-\")\n        .stdin(Stdio::piped())\n        .stdout(Stdio::piped())\n        .stderr(Stdio::piped())\n        .spawn()\n        .context(\"failed to run codex exec\")?;\n\n    if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {\n        stdin\n            .write_all(prompt.as_bytes())\n            .await\n            .context(\"failed to write prompt to codex stdin\")?;\n    } else {\n        return Err(anyhow!(\"failed to open codex stdin\"));\n    }\n\n    let output = timeout(Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs), child.wait_with_output())\n        .await\n        .map_err(|_| anyhow!(\"codex exec timed out after {timeout_secs}s\"))?\n        .context(\"failed to wait for codex exec\")?;\n\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n        return Err(anyhow!(\n            \"codex exec failed with status {}: {}{}{}\",\n            output.status,\n            stderr.trim(),\n            if stderr.trim().is_empty() || stdout.trim().is_empty() {\n                \"\"\n            } else {\n                \" | \"\n            },\n            stdout.trim()\n        ));\n    }\n\n    let text = String::from_utf8(output.stdout)\n        .context(\"codex exec returned non-utf8 stdout\")?\n        .trim()\n        .to_string();\n\n    if text.is_empty() {\n        Err(anyhow!(\"codex exec returned an empty response\"))\n    } else {\n        Ok(text)\n    }\n}\n\nfn resolve_codex_model(model: &str) -> String {\n    if let Ok(explicit) = std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_CODEX_MODEL\") {\n        return explicit;\n    }\n\n    let norm = model.trim();\n    if let Some(rest) = norm.strip_prefix(\"codex:\") {\n        return rest.to_string();\n    }\n\n    if norm == DEFAULT_PROXY_MODEL {\n        return DEFAULT_CODEX_MODEL.to_string();\n    }\n\n    norm.strip_prefix(\"codex-\")\n        .map(|rest| rest.to_string())\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| DEFAULT_CODEX_MODEL.to_string())\n}\n\nfn render_messages(messages: &[Value]) -> String {\n    messages\n        .iter()\n        .filter_map(|m| {\n            let role = m.get(\"role\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or(\"user\");\n            let content = render_content(m.get(\"content\")?);\n            if content.trim().is_empty() {\n                None\n            } else {\n                Some(format!(\"{role}: {content}\"))\n            }\n        })\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        .join(\"\\n\\n\")\n}\n\nfn render_content(content: &Value) -> String {\n    if let Some(s) = content.as_str() {\n        return s.to_string();\n    }\n\n    if let Some(items) = content.as_array() {\n        return items\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|item| {\n                item.get(\"text\")\n                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                    .or_else(|| item.get(\"content\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()))\n            })\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(\"\\n\");\n    }\n\n    content.to_string()\n}\n\nfn env_flag(name: &str, default: bool) -> bool {\n    std::env::var(name)\n        .ok()\n        .map(|v| {\n            matches!(\n                v.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str(),\n                \"1\" | \"true\" | \"yes\" | \"on\"\n            )\n        })\n        .unwrap_or(default)\n}\n"}}

    List available tools for the selected model and exit\n  -h, --help                  display help for command\n\nAutonomy Levels:\n  Droid exec uses a tiered autonomy system to control what operations the agent can perform.\n  By default, it runs in read-only mode, requiring explicit flags to enable modifications.\n\n  DEFAULT (no flags)         Read-only mode - The safest mode for reviewing planned changes without execution\n                             • Reading files or logs: cat, less, head, tail, systemctl status\n                             • Display commands: echo, pwd\n Directory listing: ls, find (without -delete or -exec)\n                             ✗ No modifications to files or system\n                             Use case: Safe for reviewing what changes would be made\n\n  --auto low                 Low-risk operations - Basic file operations while blocking system changes\n                             • File creation/modification in non-system directories: touch, mkdir, mv, cp\n                             ✗ No system modifications or package installations\n                             Use case: Documentation updates, code formatting, adding comments\n\n  --auto medium              Development operations - Significant but recoverable side effects\n                             • Installing packages from trusted sources: npm install, pip install (without sudo)\n                             • Network requests to trusted endpoints: curl, wget to known APIs\n                             • Git operations (local only): git commit, git checkout, git pull\n                             • Building code: make, npm run build, mvn compile\n                             ✗ No git push, sudo commands, or production changes\n                             Use case: Local development, testing, dependency management\n\n  --auto high                Production operations - Security implications or major side effects\n                             • Running arbitrary/untrusted code: curl | bash, eval, downloaded scripts\n                             • Exposing ports or modifying firewall rules\n                             • Git push operations: git push, git push --force\n                             • Production deployments, database migrations, sensitive operations\n                             • Commands accessing/modifying passwords or keys\n                             ✗ Still blocks: sudo rm -rf /, system-wide changes\n                             Use case: CI/CD pipelines, automated deployments\n\n  --skip-permissions-unsafe  Bypass all checks - DANGEROUS!\n                             • Allows ALL operations without confirmation\n                             • Can execute irreversible Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n"}},"realtime_active":false,"summary":"none","user_instructions":"### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}

Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n"}},"realtime_active":false,"summary":"none","user_instructions":"### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}

  env_flag(\"CODEX_PROXY_ENABLE\", false) || std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_MODEL\").is_ok()\n}\n\npub fn advertised_model() -> String {\n    std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_ADVERTISED_MODEL\")\n        .or_else(|_| std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_MODEL\"))\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| DEFAULT_PROXY_MODEL.to_string())\n}\n\npub fn is_codex_model(model: &str) -> bool {\n    let norm = model.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();\n    enabled()\n        && (norm == advertised_model().to_ascii_lowercase()\n            || norm.starts_with(\"codex:\")\n            || norm.starts_with(\"codex-\"))\n}\n\npub async fn generate(model: &str, messages: &[Value]) -> anyhow::Result<String> {\n    let prompt = render_messages(messages);\n    let codex_model = resolve_codex_model(model);\n    let codex_bin = std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_BIN\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \"codex\".to_string());\n    let cwd = std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_CWD\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \"/tmp\".to_string());\n    let timeout_secs = std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_TIMEOUT_SECS\")\n        .ok()\n        .and_then(|v| v.parse::<u64>().ok())\n        .filter(|v| *v >= 5)\n        .unwrap_or(180);\n\n    let mut child = Command::new(codex_bin)\n        .arg(\"exec\")\n        .arg(\"--ephemeral\")\n        .arg(\"--skip-git-repo-check\")\n        .arg(\"--ignore-rules\")\n        .arg(\"--sandbox\")\n        .arg(\"read-only\")\n        .arg(\"--cd\")\n        .arg(cwd)\n        .arg(\"-m\")\n        .arg(codex_model)\n        .arg(\"-\")\n        .stdin(Stdio::piped())\n        .stdout(Stdio::piped())\n        .stderr(Stdio::piped())\n        .spawn()\n        .context(\"failed to run codex exec\")?;\n\n    if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {\n        stdin\n            .write_all(prompt.as_bytes())\n            .await\n            .context(\"failed to write prompt to codex stdin\")?;\n    } else {\n        return Err(anyhow!(\"failed to open codex stdin\"));\n    }\n\n    let output = timeout(Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs), child.wait_with_output())\n        .await\n        .map_err(|_| anyhow!(\"codex exec timed out after {timeout_secs}s\"))?\n        .context(\"failed to wait for codex exec\")?;\n\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n        return Err(anyhow!(\n            \"codex exec failed with status {}: {}{}{}\",\n            output.status,\n            stderr.trim(),\n            if stderr.trim().is_empty() || stdout.trim().is_empty() {\n                \"\"\n            } else {\n                \" | \"\n            },\n            stdout.trim()\n        ));\n    }\n\n    let text = String::from_utf8(output.stdout)\n        .context(\"codex exec returned non-utf8 stdout\")?\n        .trim()\n        .to_string();\n\n    if text.is_empty() {\n        Err(anyhow!(\"codex exec returned an empty response\"))\n    } else {\n        Ok(text)\n    }\n}\n\nfn resolve_codex_model(model: &str) -> String {\n    if let Ok(explicit) = std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_CODEX_MODEL\") {\n        return explicit;\n    }\n\n    let norm = model.trim();\n    if let Some(rest) = norm.strip_prefix(\"codex:\") {\n        return rest.to_string();\n    }\n\n    if norm == DEFAULT_PROXY_MODEL {\n        return DEFAULT_CODEX_MODEL.to_string();\n    }\n\n    norm.strip_prefix(\"codex-\")\n        .map(|rest| rest.to_string())\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| DEFAULT_CODEX_MODEL.to_string())\n}\n\nfn render_messages(messages: &[Value]) -> String {\n    messages\n        .iter()\n        .filter_map(|m| {\n            let role = m.get(\"role\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or(\"user\");\n            let content = render_content(m.get(\"content\")?);\n            if content.trim().is_empty() {\n                None\n            } else {\n                Some(format!(\"{role}: {content}\"))\n            }\n        })\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        .join(\"\\n\\n\")\n}\n\nfn render_content(content: &Value) -> String {\n    if let Some(s) = item.get(\"text\")\n                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                    .or_else(|| item.get(\"content\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()))\n            })\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n {"timestamp":"2026-05-27T07:27:16.833Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_E6Y8oJpBWTqW4Yi1k5jVhKCz","output":"Chunk ID: 6ff0d8\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1491\nOutput:\n//! Codex CLI backend for the local OpenAI-compatible proxy.\n//!\n//! This keeps ChatGPT/Codex OAuth in `~/.codex/auth.json`. Factory Droid only sees\n//! the loopback proxy and a dummy BYOK token.\n\nuse anyhow::{anyhow, Context};\nuse serde_json::Value;\nuse std::fmt::Write;\nuse std::process::Stdio;\nuse tokio::io::AsyncWriteExt;\nuse tokio::process::Command;\nuse tokio::time::{timeout, Duration};\n\nconst DEFAULT_PROXY_MODEL: &str = \"codex-gpt-5.5\";\nconst DEFAULT_CODEX_MODEL: &str = \"gpt-5.5\";\n\npub fn enabled() -> bool {\n    env_flag(\"CODEX_PROXY_ENABLE\", false) || std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_MODEL\").is_ok()\n}\n\npub fn advertised_model() -> String {\n    std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_ADVERTISED_MODEL\")\n        .or_else(|_| std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_MODEL\"))\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| DEFAULT_PROXY_MODEL.to_string())\n}\n\npub fn is_codex_model(model: &str) -> bool {\n    let norm = model.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();\n    enabled()\n        && (norm == advertised_model().to_ascii_lowercase()\n            || norm.starts_with(\"codex:\")\n            || norm.starts_with(\"codex-\"))\n}\n\npub async fn generate(model: &str, messages: &[Value]) -> anyhow::Result<String> {\n    let prompt = render_messages(messages);\n    let codex_model = resolve_codex_model(model);\n    let codex_bin = std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_BIN\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \"codex\".to_string());\n    let cwd = std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_CWD\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \"/tmp\".to_string());\n    let timeout_secs = std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_TIMEOUT_SECS\")\n        .ok()\n        .and_then(|v| v.parse::<u64>().ok())\n        .filter(|v| *v >= 5)\n        .unwrap_or(180);\n\n    let mut child = Command::new(codex_bin)\n        .arg(\"exec\")\n        .arg(\"--ephemeral\")\n        .arg(\"--skip-git-repo-check\")\n        .arg(\"--ignore-rules\")\n        .arg(\"--sandbox\")\n        .arg(\"read-only\")\n        .arg(\"--cd\")\n        .arg(cwd)\n        .arg(\"-m\")\n        .arg(codex_model)\n        .arg(\"-\")\n        .stdin(Stdio::piped())\n        .stdout(Stdio::piped())\n        .stderr(Stdio::piped())\n        .kill_on_drop(true)\n        .spawn()\n        .context(\"failed to run codex exec\")?;\n\n    if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {\n        stdin\n            .write_all(prompt.as_bytes())\n            .await\n            .context(\"failed to write prompt to codex stdin\")?;\n    } else {\n        return Err(anyhow!(\"failed to open codex stdin\"));\n    }\n\n    let output = match timeout(Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs), child.wait_with_output()).await {\n        Ok(result) => result.context(\"failed to wait for codex exec\")?,\n        Err(_) => return Err(anyhow!(\"codex exec timed out after {timeout_secs}s\")),\n    };\n\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n        return Err(anyhow!(\n            \"codex exec failed with status {}: {}{}{}\",\n            output.status,\n            stderr.trim(),\n            if stderr.trim().is_empty() || stdout.trim().is_empty() {\n                \"\"\n            } else {\n                \" | \"\n            },\n            stdout.trim()\n        ));\n    }\n\n    let text = String::from_utf8(output.stdout)\n        .context(\"codex exec returned non-utf8 stdout\")?\n        .trim()\n        .to_string();\n\n    if text.is_empty() {\n        Err(anyhow!(\"codex exec returned an empty response\"))\n    } else {\n        Ok(text)\n    }\n}\n\nfn resolve_codex_model(model: &str) -> String {\n    if let Ok(explicit) = std::env::var(\"CODEX_PROXY_CODEX_MODEL\") {\n        return explicit;\n    }\n\n    let norm = model.trim();\n    if let Some(rest) = norm.strip_prefix(\"codex:\") {\n        return rest.to_string();\n    }\n\n    if norm == DEFAULT_PROXY_MODEL {\n        return DEFAULT_CODEX_MODEL.to_string();\n    }\n\n    norm.strip_prefix(\"codex-\")\n        .map(|rest| rest.to_string())\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| DEFAULT_CODEX_MODEL.to_string())\n}\n\nfn render_messages(messages: &[Value]) -> String {\n    let turns = messages\n        .iter()\n        .rev()\n        .filter_map(|m| {\n            let role = m.get(\"role\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or(\"user\");\n            if role != \"user\" && role != \"assistant\" {\n                return None;\n            }\n            let content = render_content(m.get(\"content\")?);\n            if content.trim().is_empty() {\n                None\n            } else {\n                Some((role, content))\n            }\n        })\n        .take(8)\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        .into_iter()\n        .rev()\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n\n    let mut prompt = String::from(\n        \"You are answering through a local OAuth proxy. Reply directly and concisely. \\\nDo not call tools; the host application owns tool execution.\\n\\n\",\n    );\n\n    for (role, content) in turns {\n        let trimmed = truncate_chars(content.trim(), 12_000);\n        let _ = writeln!(prompt, \"{role}: {trimmed}\\n\");\n    }\n\n    prompt\n}\n\nfn render_content(content: &Value) -> String {\n    if let Some(s) = content.as_str() {\n        return s.to_string();\n    }\n\n    if let Some(items) = content.as_array() {\n        return items\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|item| {\n                item.get(\"text\")\n                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                    .or_else(|| item.get(\"content\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()))\n            })\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(\"\\n\");\n    }\n\n    content.to_string()\n}\n\nfn truncate_chars(s: &str, max_chars: usize) -> String {\n    if s.chars().count() <= max_chars {\n        return s.to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut out = s.chars().take(max_chars).collect::<String>();\n    out.push_str(\"\\n[truncated by local proxy]\");\n    out\n}\n\nfn env_flag(name: &str, default: bool) -> bool {\n    std::env::var(name)\n        .ok()\n        .map(|v| {\n            matches!(\n                v.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str(),\n                \"1\" | \"true\" | \"yes\" | \"on\"\n            )\n        })\n        .unwrap_or(default)\n}\n"}}

The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n"}},"realtime_active":false,"summary":"none","user_instructions":"### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}

The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\\n\\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\\n\\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\\n\\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\\n**Rust Workspace**\\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\\n\\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\\n\\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\\n\\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\\n\\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\\n\\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\\n</coding_guidelines>\"}],\"designGuidelinesInfo\":[]},\"uiRenderCutoffMessageId\":\"53e38b86-7670-4bfe-8993-f28dd88a8a2d\"}\n/home/jeremy/.factory/sessions/-home-jeremy-git-operation-dbus-proto/6591b55d-4016-4a10-9759-43dcf9b8fc2e.jsonl:683:{\"type\":\"message\",\"id\":\"4849e2c4-949f-47ae-bf15-36750361c031\",\"timestamp\":\"2026-05-27T06:59:13.376Z\",\"message\":{\"role\":\"assistant\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"tool_use\",\"id\":\"chatcmpl-tool-87c30bc264a38555\",\"name\":\"Read\",\"input\":{\"file_path\":\"/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/grpc_server.rs\",\"limit\":50,\"offset\":4395}}],\"openaiMessageId\":\"chatcmpl-3168925cae674cadbb6bae45d7a0c44c\"},\"parentId\":\"f3e9eda8-c31f-4a37-8b5b-3423bcf282e5\",\"compactionSummaryId\":\"524b3743-d4cb-4c81-ade9-7e1cc5364ced\"}\n/home/jeremy/.factory/sessions/-home-jeremy-git-operation-dbus-proto/6591b55d-4016-4a10-9759-43dcf9b8fc2e.jsonl:685:{\"type\":\"message\",\"id\":\"34faa349-13c0-439b-8c78-a3b05b8d978a\",\"timestamp\":\"2026-05-27T06:59:15.263Z\",\"message\":{\"role\":\"assistant\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"Now let me check the actual zbus version used in the project and what API is available:\"},{\"type\":\"tool_use\",\"id\":\"chatcmpl-tool-9537edcce7457720\",\"name\":\"Grep\",\"input\":{\"pattern\":\"zbus\",\"path\":\"/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-grpc-bridge/Cargo.toml\",\"output_mode\":\"content\",\"line_numbers\":true}}],\"openaiMessageId\":\"chatcmpl-4eb7e229d4834e5887e9b1e0fb855f76\"},\"parentId\":\"1c7d0cfc-4d29-4062-99b1-81a2bc247980\",\"compactionSummaryId\":\"524b3743-d4cb-4c81-ade9-7e1cc5364ced\"}\n"}}

Memory/Soul/Namespace backed by CozoDB via op-cognitive-mcp. Deploy as s6 service. Wire the axon-trace-ui to the backend via D-Bus passthrough through op-grpc-bridge.\\n\\n3. Approach\\n   - Standalone crate following op-grpc-bridge conventions\\n   - 9 proto files compiled by tonic-build\\n   - Layered: gRPC → Transport (D-Bus | HTTP-RPC) → wg-xray container's op-grpc-bridge\\n   - Schema-tag header injection for Xray OpenFlow routing\\n   - Soul/Namespace/Memory bypass RPC, call CozoDB in-process via op-cognitive-mcp\\n   - D-Bus passthrough service on op-grpc-bridge as UI extension point (no new gRPC protos needed for new D-Bus services)\\n   - Artix s6-rc with producer-for/consumer-for log pipeline\\n\\n4. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the 31-crate workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Chimera Linux.\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`serde_json`).\n*   Avoid new serialization formats without justification.\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}
