Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n"}},"realtime_active":false,"summary":"none","user_instructions":"### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Known mode names are Default and Plan.\n\n## request_user_input availability\n\nUse the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.\n\nIn Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n</collaboration_mode>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<apps_instructions>\n## Apps (Connectors)\nApps (Connectors) can be explicitly triggered in user messages in the format `[$app-name](app://{connector_id})`. Apps can also be implicitly triggered as long as the context suggests usage of available apps.\nAn app is equivalent to a set of MCP tools within the `codex_apps` MCP.\nAn installed app's MCP tools are either provided to you already, or can be lazy-loaded through the `tool_search` tool. If `tool_search` is available, the apps that are searchable by `tools_search` will be listed by it.\nDo not additionally call list_mcp_resources or list_mcp_resource_templates for apps.\n</apps_instructions>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<skills_instructions>\n## Skills\nA skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n"}},"realtime_active":false,"summary":"none","user_instructions":"### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Chat API routes\n\nuse axum::{extract::Extension, http::StatusCode, response::IntoResponse, Json};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tracing::{error, info};\n\nuse crate::state::AppState;\nuse op_llm::{ChatMessage, ProviderType};\n\n/// Chat message request\n#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]\npub struct ChatRequest {\n    pub message: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub provider: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub model: Option<String>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub conversation_id: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Chat message response\n#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]\npub struct ChatResponse {\n    pub content: String,\n    pub provider: String,\n    pub model: String,\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub tools_used: Option<Vec<String>>,\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub error: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// POST /api/chat - Send a chat message\npub async fn chat_message(\n    Extension(state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,\n    Json(req): Json<ChatRequest>,\n) -> impl IntoResponse {\n    info!(\"Chat request: {} chars\", req.message.len());\n\n    // Determine provider and model\n    let provider_type = if let Some(ref p) = req.provider {\n        match p.parse::<ProviderType>() {\n            Ok(pt) => Some(pt),\n            Err(_) => {\n                return (\n                    StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,\n                    Json(ChatResponse {\n                        content: String::new(),\n                        provider: p.clone(),\n                        model: String::new(),\n                        tools_used: None,\n                        error: Some(format!(\"Unknown provider: {}\", p)),\n                    }),\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n\n    // Build messages\n    let messages = vec![\n        ChatMessage::system(\"You are a helpful AI assistant integrated with op-dbus, a system management tool. You can help with system administration, code, and general questions.\"),\n        ChatMessage::user(&req.message),\n    ];\n\n    // Send to LLM\n    let result = if let (Some(pt), Some(ref model)) = (provider_type.as_ref(), req.model.as_ref()) {\n        // Use specified provider and model\n        state.chat_manager.chat_with(pt, model, messages).await\n    } else {\n        // Use current provider and model\n        state.chat_manager.chat(messages).await\n    };\n\n    match result {\n        Ok(response) => {\n            info!(\n                \"Chat response from {}/{}: {} chars\",\n                response.provider,\n                response.model,\n                response.message.content.len()\n            );\n\n            (\n                StatusCode::OK,\n                Json(ChatResponse {\n                    content: response.message.content,\n                    provider: response.provider,\n                    model: response.model,\n                    tools_used: None,\n                    error: None,\n                }),\n            )\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            error!(\"Chat error: {}\", e);\n\n            let current_provider = state.chat_manager.current_provider().await;\n            let current_model = state.chat_manager.current_model().await;\n\n            (\n                StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,\n                Json(ChatResponse {\n                    content: String::new(),\n                    provider: provider_type\n                        .map(|p| p.to_string())\n                        .unwrap_or(current_provider.to_string()),\n                    model: req.model.unwrap_or(current_model),\n                    tools_used: None,\n                    error: Some(e.to_string()),\n                }),\n            )\n        }\n    }\n}\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-05-31T23:55:36.352Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"\\To deploy an Antigravity agent that returns structured, predictable JSON data (which you can pipe directly into your JsonRenderer in the React frontend), you need to define your interface using Pydantic and pass it to the agent configuration.\n\nHere are the actual objects and SDK references you need:\n\n1. The Schema Object (pydantic.BaseModel)\nDefine the exact JSON structure you want your UI to receive by creating a Pydantic BaseModel.\n\npython\n\n\nimport pydantic\nclass UiResponseSchema(pydantic.BaseModel):\n    action: str\n    metadata: dict[str, str]\n    confidence_score: float\n2. The Configuration Reference (LocalAgentConfig(response_schema=...))\nWhen initializing your agent, pass the Pydantic class to the response_schema parameter in your LocalAgentConfig. This forces the Gemini model to strictly conform its output to your JSON interface.\n\npython\n\n\nfrom google.antigravity import Agent, LocalAgentConfig\nconfig = LocalAgentConfig(\n    response_schema=UiResponseSchema, # Pass your schema here\n)\n3. The Extraction Reference (response.structured_output())\nAfter sending a prompt to the agent, do not rely on standard text parsing. Instead, use the structured_output() method. It will automatically parse the generated JSON and return it as a Python dictionary that safely matches your schema.\n\npython\n\n\nasync with Agent(config) as agent:\n    response = await agent.chat(\"Analyze the system status...\")\n    \n    # Retrieves the guaranteed JSON dictionary\n    json_data = await response.structured_output()\n    \n    # You can now send this json_data straight to your frontend over gRPC/HTTP\n    # for the <JsonRenderer data={sidebarContent} /> to consume.\n    print(json_data)\n7:54 PM"}]}}

This forces the Gemini model to strictly conform its output to your JSON interface.\n\npython\n\n\nfrom google.antigravity import Agent, LocalAgentConfig\nconfig = LocalAgentConfig(\n    response_schema=UiResponseSchema, # Pass your schema here\n)\n3. The Extraction Reference (response.structured_output())\nAfter sending a prompt to the agent, do not rely on standard text parsing. Instead, use the structured_output() method. It will automatically parse the generated JSON and return it as a Python dictionary that safely matches your schema.\n\npython\n\n\nasync with Agent(config) as agent:\n    response = await agent.chat(\"Analyze the system status...\")\n    \n    # Retrieves the guaranteed JSON dictionary\n    json_data = await response.structured_output()\n    \n    # You can now send this json_data straight to your frontend over gRPC/HTTP\n    # for the <JsonRenderer data={sidebarContent} /> to consume.\n    print(json_data)\n7:54 PM","images":[],"local_images":[],"text_elements":[]}}

It exposes a standard OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`/v1/chat/completions`), but it acts as a **router**.\\n*   **How it works:** When you send a request to OpenClaw, you pass a specific `model` string (e.g., `google-gemini-cli/gemini-2.5-flash` or `opencode/kimi-k2.5-free`). OpenClaw intercepts this, looks up its internal registry (defined in `openclaw.json`), and dynamically routes the request to the correct upstream provider (Google, Anthropic, local Ollama, etc.), handling all the complex auth and translation behind the scenes.\\n*   **Why rename to \\\"Routable Models\\\":** In your current setup, your D-Bus backend is treating these model strings essentially as target endpoints. Calling the view \\\"Routable Models\\\" is highly accurate because it represents the *target LLM engines* OpenClaw can route prompts to.\\n\\n### 2. Agents (The \\\"Execution\\\" Layer)\\nIn official OpenClaw terminology, an \\\"Agent\\\" is not just a model—it is a fully isolated workspace and persona.\\n*   **How it works:** An OpenClaw Agent has its own directory containing an `IDENTITY.md` (who it is), `SOUL.md` (long-term instructions), and `TOOLS.md` (what it is allowed to execute). OpenClaw \\\"binds\\\" specific communication channels to specific agents. \\n*   **The Model-Agent Relationship:** When an Agent is triggered, OpenClaw's routing engine decides *which model* to use for that agent based on the task complexity. You're asking how we can evolve from a reactive system (where the LLM only gets information when it explicitly calls the `indexer_search` tool) to a proactive, context-aware system that anticipates your needs.\\n\\nHere's how we can achieve that within the existing architecture:\\n\\n**The Core Idea: Ambient RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)**\\n\\nInstead of waiting for the LLM to actively search, we can create a \\\"context-aware\\\" layer that constantly and proactively gathers relevant information and feeds it to the LLM on every turn. This makes the LLM \\\"smarter\\\" about your current task without you needing to explicitly tell it to search.\\n\\n**How it would work in this system:**\\n\\n1.  **Continuous Context Monitoring (The \\\"Ear\\\"):**\\n    *   We would introduce a new background process within `op-chat`. This \\\"Context Monitor\\\" would continuously watch for changes in your working environment.\\n    *   It would monitor things like:\\n        *   Your current working directory (`pwd`).\\n        *   Recently modified files.\\n        *   The content of files you're actively editing (this would require editor integration, but is a common feature of advanced agents).\\n        *   Your command history.\\n\\n2.  **Proactive Background Searching (The \\\"Subconscious\\\"):**\\n    *   As the Context Monitor detects changes or new activity (like you typing a command or editing a file), it would trigger a \\\"proactive search\\\" against the `zeroclaw` index in the background.\\n    *   This search would use keywords from your current command, the file you're editing, or the code you're looking at to find relevant code snippets, function definitions, or documentation.\\n\\n3.  **Contextual Prompt Injection (The \\\"Memory\\\"):**\\n    *   The most relevant results from the proactive search are then automatically \\\"injected\\\" into the system prompt that is sent to the LLM with every request.\\n    *   We would extend the `system_prompt.rs` in `op-chat` to include a dynamic section for this \\\"ambient context.\\\"\\n\\n**The Result: A Proactive Assistant**\\n\\nWith this system in place, the following scenario becomes possible:\\n\\n*   You start editing `crates/op-tools/src/builtin/ovs_tools.rs`.\\n*   The **Context Monitor** sees this.\\n*   The **Proactive Searcher** runs a background search in `zeroclaw` for `ovs_tools.rs` and related symbols.\\n*   The **Context Injector** adds the most relevant code snippets from `ovs_tools.rs` into the LLM's system prompt.\\n*   You then type, \\\"How do I create a bridge?\\\"\\n*   The LLM, already primed with the context of `ovs_tools.rs`, can now give you a highly accurate and proactive answer, like: \\\"It looks like you're working with `ovs_tools`. You can use the `OvsCreateBridgeTool` for that. Here's how to use it...\\\"\\n\\nThis creates a much more intelligent and helpful user experience, where the assistant seems to anticipate your needs because it's constantly aware of your context.\\n\\n**Next Steps to Implement This:**\\n\\nTo make this a reality, the next steps would be:\\n1.  Create a \\\"Context Monitor\\\" component within `op-chat`.\\n2.  Extend `ChatActor` to run this monitor in the background.\\n3.  Modify `handle_chat` in `actor.rs` to use the context from the monitor when building the prompt for the LLM.\\n\\nShall we proceed with this vision in Requires OP_MCP_PROXY_BIN (or falls back to \"op-mcp-proxy\").\n    pub fn from_env() -> Result<Self> {\n        let bin = std::env::var(\"OP_MCP_PROXY_BIN\").unwrap_or_else(|_| id: \"auto\".to_string(),\n                name: \"Auto (Gemini 3 routing)\".to_string(),\n                description: Some(\"Automatic model selection via op-mcp-proxy\".to_string()),\n   ModelInfo {\n                id: \"gemini-2.5-flash\".to_string(),\n                name: \"Gemini 2.5 Flash\".to_string(),\n                description: Some(\"Fast model via Code Assist\".to_string()),\n                parameters: None,\n                available: true,\n                tags: vec![\"fast\".to_string()],\n                downloads: None,\n                updated_at: None,\n            },\n        ])\n    }\n\n    async fn search_models(&self, query: &str, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<ModelInfo>> {\n        let models = self.list_models().await?;\n model: &str, messages: Vec<ChatMessage>) -> Result<ChatResponse> {\n        let prompt = messages\n            .iter()\n            .map(|m| format!(\"{}: {}\", m.role, m.content))\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(\"\\n\");\n\n        let req = simd_json::json!({\n            \"jsonrpc\": \"2.0\",\n            \"id\": 1,\n            \"method\": \"generate\",\n            \"params\": {\n                \"prompt\": prompt,\n                \"model\": model\n            }\n        });\n\n        let resp = self.call(req).await?;\n        let result = Ok(ChatResponse {\n            message: ChatMessage::assistant(text),\n            model: used_model,\n            provider: \"mcp-proxy\".to_string(),\n            finish_reason: request.messages).await\n    }\n\n    async fn chat_stream(\n        &self,\n        model: &str,\n        messages: Vec<ChatMessage>,\n    ) -> Result<tokio::sync::mpsc::Receiver<Result<String>>> {\n }\n}\n"}}

Chat Manager - Manages provider switching and chat sessions\n//!\n//! ## Authentication Priority\n//!\n//! 1. **Factory** (local proxy — the AI you are talking to right now)\n//! 2. **GCloud ADC** (direct OAuth via gcloud)\n//! 3. **Gemini** (API key fallback)\n//! 4. **Anthropic** (API key)\n//!\n//! ## Environment Variables\n//!\n//! ```bash\n//! # Preferred: Factory local proxy (default)\n//! LLM_PROVIDER=factory\n//! FACTORY_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11435/v1\n//! FACTORY_API_KEY=local-codex-proxy\n//! FACTORY_DEFAULT_MODEL=local-oauth-proxy\n//!\n//! # Provider selection override\n//! LLM_PROVIDER=factory  # or openclaw, gemini, gemini-cli, anthropic\n//! LLM_MODEL=gemini-2.5-flash\n//!\n//! # Optional API key fallbacks\n//! GEMINI_API_KEY=xxx\n//! ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=xxx\n//! ```\n\nuse anyhow::{anyhow, Result};\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::sync::RwLock;\nuse tracing::{debug, info, warn};\n\nuse crate::anthropic::AnthropicClient;\nuse crate::assistant::AssistantProvider;\nuse crate::factory::FactoryProvider;\nuse crate::gcloud_adc::GCloudADCProvider;\nuse crate::gemini::GeminiClient;\nuse crate::gemini_cli::create_gemini_cli_provider;\nuse crate::openclaw::OpenClawProvider;\nuse crate::provider::{\n    BoxedProvider, ChatMessage, ChatRequest, ChatResponse, LlmProvider, ModelInfo, ProviderType,\n};\nuse async_trait::async_trait;\n\n/// Chat manager - handles multiple providers and model selection\npub struct ChatManager {\n    providers: HashMap<ProviderType, BoxedProvider>,\n    current_provider: Arc<RwLock<ProviderType>>,\n    current_model: Arc<RwLock<String>>,\n    model_cache: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<ProviderType, Vec<ModelInfo>>>>,\n}\n\nimpl ChatManager {\n    /// Create a new chat manager\n    ///\n    /// Initialization order:\n    /// 1. Check LLM_PROVIDER environment variable\n    /// 2. Factory — Local proxy (default)\n    /// 3. GCloud ADC\n    /// 4. Gemini (API key)\n    /// 5. Anthropic (API key)\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        let mut providers: HashMap<ProviderType, BoxedProvider> = HashMap::new();\n        let mut default_provider = None;\n        let mut default_model = std::env::var(\"FACTORY_DEFAULT_MODEL\")\n            .or_else(|_| std::env::var(\"OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_MODEL\"))\n            .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"local-oauth-proxy\".to_string());\n\n        // Check environment variables\n        let env_provider = std::env::var(\"LLM_PROVIDER\").ok();\n        let env_model = std::env::var(\"LLM_MODEL\").ok();\n\n        if let Some(ref provider_name) = env_provider {\n            info!(\"📋 LLM_PROVIDER={}\", provider_name);\n        }\n        if let Some(ref model_name) = env_model {\n            info!(\"📋 LLM_MODEL={}\", model_name);\n            default_model = model_name.clone();\n        }\n\n        // =====================================================\n        // Factory — Local proxy (default, the AI you are talking to)\n        // =====================================================\n        match FactoryProvider::from_env() {\n            Ok(factory) => {\n                info!(\"✅ Factory provider initialized (local proxy)\");\n                providers.insert(ProviderType::Factory, Box::new(factory));\n                if default_provider.is_none() {\n                    default_provider = Some(ProviderType::Factory);\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                debug!(\"Factory provider failed: {}\", e);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // =====================================================\n        // Gemini CLI provider (optional)\n        // =====================================================\n        let wants_gemini_cli = std::env::var(\"ENABLE_GEMINI_CLI_PROVIDER\")\n            .ok()\n            .map(|v| v == \"1\" || v.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"true\"))\n            .unwrap_or(false)\n            || env_provider\n                .as_deref()\n                .map(|v| {\n                    v.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"gemini-cli\")\n                        || v.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"gemini_cli\")\n                        || v.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"geminicli\")\n                })\n                .unwrap_or(false);\n\n        if wants_gemini_cli {\n            let gemini_cli = create_gemini_cli_provider();\n            info!(\"✅ Gemini CLI provider initialized\");\n            providers.insert(ProviderType::GeminiCli, Box::new(gemini_cli));\n            if default_provider.is_none() {\n Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. {"timestamp":"2026-05-31T23:56:52.482Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_UwXqf9g0uBtgXA3ZkuUbClqH","output":"Chunk ID: bd1c03\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 839\nOutput:\n--- \nname: antigravity-design-expert\ndescription: Core UI/UX engineering skill for building highly interactive, spatial, weightless, and glassmorphism-based web interfaces using GSAP and 3D CSS.\nrisk: safe\nsource: community\ndate_added: \"2026-03-07\"\n---\n\n# Antigravity UI & Motion Design Expert\n\n## When to Use\n- You are building a highly interactive web interface with spatial depth, glassmorphism, and motion-heavy UI.\n- The design should lean on GSAP, 3D CSS transforms, or React-based 3D presentation patterns.\n- You need a strong visual direction for dashboards, landing pages, or immersive product surfaces rather than a conventional flat UI.\n\n## 🎯 Role Overview\n\nYou are a world-class UI/UX Engineer specializing in \"Antigravity Design.\" Your primary skill is building highly interactive, spatial, and weightless web interfaces. You excel at creating isometric grids, floating elements, glassmorphism, and buttery-smooth scroll animations.\n\n## 🛠️ Preferred Tech Stack\n\nWhen asked to build or generate UI components, default to the following stack unless instructed otherwise:\n\n- **Framework:** React / Next.js\n- **Styling:** Tailwind CSS (for layout and utility) + Custom CSS for complex 3D transforms\n- **Animation:** GSAP (GreenSock) + ScrollTrigger for scroll-linked motion\n- **3D Elements:** React Three Fiber (R3F) or CSS 3D Transforms (`rotateX`, `rotateY`, `perspective`)\n\n## 📐 Design Principles (The \"Antigravity\" Vibe)\n\n- **Weightlessness:** UI cards and elements should appear to float. Use layered, soft, diffused drop-shadows (e.g., `box-shadow: 0 20px 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.05)`).\n- **Spatial Depth:** Utilize Z-axis layering. Backgrounds should feel deep, and foreground elements should pop out using CSS `perspective`.\n- **Glassmorphism:** Use subtle translucency, background blur (`backdrop-filter: blur(12px)`), and semi-transparent borders to create a glassy, premium feel.\n- **Isometric Snapping:** When building dashboards or card grids, use 3D CSS transforms to tilt them into an isometric perspective (e.g., `transform: rotateX(60deg) rotateZ(-45deg)`).\n\n## 🎬 Motion & Animation Rules\n\n- **Never snap instantly:** All state changes (hover, focus, active) must have smooth transitions (minimum `0.3s ease-out`).\n- **Scroll Hijacking (Tasteful):** Use GSAP ScrollTrigger to make elements float into view from the Y-axis with slight rotation as the user scrolls.\n- **Staggered Entrances:** When a grid of cards loads, they should not appear all at once. Stagger their entrance animations by `0.1s` so they drop in like dominoes.\n- **Parallax:** Background elements should move slower than foreground elements on scroll to enhance the 3D illusion.\n\n## 🚧 Execution Constraints\n\n- Always write modular, reusable components.\n- Ensure all animations are disabled for users with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.\n- Prioritize performance: Use `will-change: transform` for animated elements to offload rendering to the GPU. Do not animate expensive properties like `box-shadow` or `filter` continuously.\n\n## Limitations\n- Use this skill only when the task clearly matches the scope described above.\n- Do not treat the output as a substitute for environment-specific validation, testing, or expert review.\n- Stop and ask for clarification if required inputs, permissions, safety boundaries, or success criteria are missing.\n"}}

Execute step-by-step:\n   - Announce current step and expected artifact.\n   - Invoke recommended skills for that step.\n   - Verify completion criteria before moving to next step.\n5. At the end, provide:\n   - Completed artifacts\n   - Validation evidence\n   - Remaining risks and next actions\n\n## Default Workflow Routing\n\n- Product delivery request -> `ship-saas-mvp`\n- Security review request -> `security-audit-web-app`\n- Agent/LLM product request -> `build-ai-agent-system`\n- E2E/browser testing request -> `qa-browser-automation`\n- Domain-driven design request -> `design-ddd-core-domain`\n\n## Copy-Paste Prompts\n\n```text\nUse @antigravity-workflows to run the \"Ship a SaaS MVP\" workflow for my project idea.\n```\n\n```text\nUse @antigravity-workflows and execute a full \"Security Audit for a Web App\" workflow.\n```\n\n```text\nUse @antigravity-workflows to guide me through \"Build an AI Agent System\" with checkpoints.\n```\n\n```text\nUse @antigravity-workflows to execute the \"QA and Browser Automation\" workflow and stabilize flaky tests.\n```\n\n```text\nUse @antigravity-workflows to execute the \"Design a DDD Core Domain\" workflow for my new service.\n```\n\n## Limitations\n\n- This skill orchestrates; it does not replace specialized skills.\n- It depends on the local availability of referenced skills.\n- It does not guarantee success without environment access, credentials, or required infrastructure.\n- For stack-specific browser automation in Go, `go-playwright` may require the corresponding skill to be present in your local skills repository.\n\n## Related Skills\n\n- `concise-planning`\n- `brainstorming`\n- `workflow-automation`\n- `verification-before-completion`\n"}}
{"timestamp":"2026-05-31T23:56:52.518Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_TANClhod916O88YDwZ83iVFs","output":"Chunk ID: 9a7707\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1883\nOutput:\n---\nname: antigravity-skill-orchestrator\ndescription: \"A meta-skill that understands task requirements, dynamically selects appropriate skills, tracks successful skill combinations using agent-memory-mcp, and prevents skill overuse for simple tasks.\"\ncategory: meta\nrisk: safe\nsource: community\ntags: \"[orchestration, meta-skill, agent-memory, task-evaluation]\"\ndate_added: \"2026-03-13\"\n---\n\n# antigravity-skill-orchestrator\n\n## Overview\n\nThe `skill-orchestrator` is a meta-skill designed to enhance the AI agent's ability to tackle complex problems. It acts as an intelligent coordinator that first evaluates the complexity of a user's request. Based on that evaluation, it determines if specialized skills are needed. If they are, it selects the right combination of skills, explicitly tracks these combinations using `@agent-memory-mcp` for future reference, and guides the agent through the execution process. Crucially, it includes strict guardrails to prevent the unnecessary use of specialized skills for simple tasks that can be solved with baseline capabilities.\n\n## When to Use This Skill\n\n- Use when tackling a complex, multi-step problem that likely requires multiple domains of expertise.\n- Use when you are unsure which specific skills are best suited for a given user request, and need to discover them from the broader ecosystem.\n- Use when the user explicitly asks to \"orchestrate\", \"combine skills\", or \"use the best tools for the job\" on a significant task.\n- Use when you want to look up previously successful combinations of skills for a specific type of problem.\n\n## Core Concepts\n\n### Task Evaluation Guardrails\nNot every task requires a specialized skill. For straightforward issues (e.g., small CSS fixes, simple script writing, renaming a variable), **DO NOT USE** specialized skills. Over-engineering simple tasks wastes tokens and time. \n\nAdditionally, the orchestrator is strictly forbidden from creating new skills. Its sole purpose is to combine and use existing skills provided by the community or present in the current environment.\n\nBefore invoking any skills, evaluate the task:\n1. **Is the task simple/contained?** Solve it directly using the agent's ordinary file editing, search, and terminal capabilities available in the current environment.\n2. **Is the task complex/multi-domain?** Only then should you proceed to orchestrate skills.\n\n### Skill Selection & Combinations\nWhen a task is deemed complex, identify the necessary domains (e.g., frontend, database, deployment). Search available skills in the current environment to find the most relevant ones. If the required skills are not found locally, consult the master skill catalog.\n\n### Master Skill Catalog\nThe Antigravity ecosystem maintains a master catalog of highly curated skills at `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sickn33/antigravity-awesome-skills/main/CATALOG.md`. When local skills are insufficient, fetch this catalog to discover appropriate skills across the 9 primary categories:\n- `architecture`\n- `business`\n- `data-ai`\n- `development`\n- `general`\n- `infrastructure`\n- `security`\n- `testing`\n- `workflow`\n\n### Memory Integration (`@agent-memory-mcp`)\nTo build institutional knowledge, the orchestrator relies on the `agent-memory-mcp` skill to record and retrieve successful skill combinations.\n\n## Step-by-Step Guide\n\n### 1. Task Evaluation & Guardrail Check\n[Triggered when facing a new user request that might need skills]\n1. Read the user's request.\n2. Ask yourself: \"Can I solve this efficiently with just basic file editing and terminal commands?\"\n3. If YES: Proceed without invoking specialized skills. Stop the orchestration here.\n4. If NO: Proceed to step 2.\n\n### 2. Retrieve Past Knowledge\n[Triggered if the task is complex]\n1. Use the `memory_search` tool provided by `agent-memory-mcp` to search for similar past tasks.\n   - Example query: `memory_search({ query: \"skill combination for react native and firebase\", type: \"skill_combination\" })`\n2. If a working combination exists, read the details using `memory_read`.\n3. If no relevant memory exists, proceed to Step 3.\n\n### 3. Discover and Select Skills\n[Triggered if no past knowledge covers this task]\n1. Analyze the core requirements (e.g., \"needs a React UI, a Node.js backend, and a PostgreSQL database\").\n2. Query the locally available skills using the current environment's skill list or equivalent discovery mechanism to find the best match for each requirement.\n3. **If local skills are insufficient**, fetch the master catalog with the web or command-line retrieval tools available in the current environment: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sickn33/antigravity-awesome-skills/main/CATALOG.md`.\n4. Scan the catalog's 9 main categories to identify the appropriate skills to bring into the current context.\n5. Select the minimal set of skills needed. **Do not over-select.**\n\n### 4. Apply Skills and Track the Combination\n[Triggered after executing the task using the selected skills]\n1. Assume the task was completed successfully using a new combination of skills (e.g., `@react-patterns` + `@nodejs-backend-patterns` + `@postgresql`).\n2. Record this combination for future use using `memory_write` from `agent-memory-mcp`.\n   - Ensure the type is `skill_combination`.\n   - Provide a descriptive key and content detailing why these skills worked well together.\n\n## Examples\n\n### Example 1: Handling a Simple Task (The Guardrail in Action)\n**User Request:** \"Change the color of the submit button in `index.css` to blue.\"\n**Action:** The skill orchestrator evaluates the task. It determines this is a \"simple/contained\" task. It **does not** invoke specialized skills. It directly edits `index.css`.\n\n### Example 2: Recording a New Skill Combination\n```javascript\n// Using the agent-memory-mcp tool after successfully building a complex feature\nmemory_write({ \n  key: \"combination-ecommerce-checkout\", \n  type: \"skill_combination\", \n  content: \"For e-commerce checkouts, using @stripe-integration combined with @react-state-management and @postgresql effectively handles the full flow from UI state to payment processing to order recording.\",\n  tags: [\"ecommerce\", \"checkout\", \"stripe\", \"react\"]\n})\n```\n\n### Example 3: Retrieving a Combination\n```javascript\n// At the start of a new e-commerce task\nmemory_search({ \n  query: \"ecommerce checkout\", \n  type: \"skill_combination\" \n})\n// Returns the key \"combination-ecommerce-checkout\", which you then read:\nmemory_read({ key: \"combination-ecommerce-checkout\" })\n```\n\n## Best Practices\n\n- ✅ **Do:** Always evaluate task complexity *before* looking for skills.\n- ✅ **Do:** Keep the number of orchestrated skills as small as possible.\n- ✅ **Do:** Use highly descriptive keys when running `memory_write` so they are easy to search later.\n- ❌ **Don't:** Use this skill for simple bug fixes or UI tweaks.\n- ❌ **Don't:** Combine skills that have overlapping and conflicting instructions without a clear plan to resolve the conflict.\n- ❌ **Don't:** Attempt to construct, generate, or create new skills. Only combine what is available.\n\n## Related Skills\n\n- `@agent-memory-mcp` - Essential for this skill to function. Provides the persistent storage for skill combinations.\n\n## Limitations\n- Use this skill only when the task clearly matches the scope described above.\n- Do not treat the output as a substitute for environment-specific validation, testing, or expert review.\n- Stop and ask for clarification if required inputs, permissions, safety boundaries, or success criteria are missing.\n"}}

.list_models_for_provider(&provider_type)\n            .await\n        {\n            Ok(models) => Json(json!({\n                \"provider\": provider,\n                \"models\": models,\n      \"current\": null,\n                \"error\": e.to_string()\n            })),\n        },\n        Err(e) => Json(json!({\n            \"provider\": provider,\n            \"models\": [],\n state.chat_manager.switch_model(request.model.clone()).await {\n        Ok(_) => {\n            let _ = persist_model(&request.model).await;\n            Json(json!({\n                \"success\": \"note\": e.to_string()\n        })),\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]\npub struct SwitchProviderRequest {\n    pub provider: String,\n}\n\n/// POST /api/llm/provider - Switch provider\npub \"model\": state.chat_manager.current_model().await,\n            \"note\": e\n        })),\n    }\n}\n\nconst PERSISTED_MODEL_PATH: &str = \"/etc/op-dbus/llm-model\";\nconst PERSISTED_PROVIDER_PATH: &str = \"/etc/op-dbus/llm-provider\";\n\nasync fn persist_model(model: &str) -> Result<(), String> {\n    if let Some(parent) = std::path::Path::new(PERSISTED_MODEL_PATH).parent() {\n        tokio::fs::create_dir_all(parent)\n            .await\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"create dir: {}\", e))?;\n    }\n    tokio::fs::write(PERSISTED_MODEL_PATH, format!(\"{model}\\n\"))\n std::path::Path::new(PERSISTED_PROVIDER_PATH).parent() {\n        tokio::fs::create_dir_all(parent)\n            .await\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"create dir: {}\", e))?;\n    }\n    tokio::fs::write(PERSISTED_PROVIDER_PATH, format!(\"{provider}\\n\"))\n        .await\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"write provider: {}\", e))?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n"}}

parseGenerativeBlocks(message.content) : null;\n\n  return (\n    <div className={cn(\"flex gap-3\", isUser && \"flex-row-reverse\")}>\n      <div className={cn(\n        \"h-8 w-8 rounded-full flex items-center justify-center text-xs font-bold shrink-0\",\n        isUser ? \"bg-muted text-foreground\" : \"bg-primary/20 text-primary\",\n      )}>\n        {isUser ? \"OP\" : \"AI\"}\n      </div>\n      <div className={cn(\"max-w-[75%] space-y-2\", isUser && \"text-right\")}>\n        <div className={cn(\n          \"rounded-lg px-4 py-2.5 text-sm\",\n          isUser ? (\n            <div className=\"whitespace-pre-wrap\">{message.content}</div>\n          ) : (\n            <div className=\"space-y-3\">\n              {segments.map((seg, i) =>\n                seg.type === \"text\" ? (\n                  <div key={i} className=\"whitespace-pre-wrap\">{seg.text}</div>\n                ) : (\n                  <GenerativeBlock key={i} spec={seg.spec} onAction={onAction} />\n                )\n              )}\n            </div>\n          )}\n        </div>\n        {message.toolCalls?.map((tc) => (\n          <button\n            key={tc.id}\n            onClick={() => onInspect(tc)}\n            className=\"w-full text-left rounded-lg border border-border bg-muted/20 px-3 py-2 hover:border-primary/30 transition-colors\"\n          >\n            <div className=\"flex items-center gap-2\">\n              <Pill variant={tc.status === \"completed\" ? \"ok\" : tc.status === \"error\" ? \"danger\" : \"default\"}>\n                {tc.status}\n              </Pill>\n              <span className=\"font-mono text-xs text-foreground\">{tc.name}</span>\n            </div>\n            {tc.result && (\n              <pre className=\"mt-1.5 font-mono text-[11px] text-muted-foreground truncate\">{JSON.stringify(tc.result).slice(0, 100)}</pre>\n            )}\n          </button>\n        ))}\n        <div className=\"text-[10px] text-muted-foreground\">{time}</div>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"}}

(\n          <pre className=\"text-foreground whitespace-pre-wrap break-all\">{JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)}</pre>\n        ) : (\n          <JsonTree data={data} depth={0} maxDepth={maxDepth} />\n        )}\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction JsonTree({ data, depth, maxDepth, label }: { data: unknown; depth: number; maxDepth: number; label?: string }) {\n  const [collapsed, setCollapsed] = useState(depth > 2);\n\n  if (data === null || data === undefined) {\n    return <div className=\"flex items-baseline gap-1.5\">{label && <span className=\"text-muted-foreground\">{label}:</span>}<span className=\"text-muted-foreground italic\">null</span></div>;\n  }\n  if (typeof data === \"boolean\") {\n    return <div className=\"flex items-baseline gap-1.5\">{label && <span className=\"text-muted-foreground\">{label}:</span>}<span className={data ? \"▸\" : \"▾\"}</span>\n          {label && <span>{label}:</span>}\n          <span className=\"text-muted-foreground text-[11px]\">[{data.length}]</span>\n        </button>\n        {!collapsed && <div className=\"ml-4 border-l border-border/50 pl-3 mt-0.5 space-y-0.5\">{data.map((item, i) => <JsonTree key={i} data={item} depth={depth + 1} maxDepth={maxDepth} label={String(i)} />)}</div>}\n      </div>\n    );\n  }\n\n  if (typeof data === \"object\") {\n    const entries = Object.entries(data as Record<string, unknown>);\n    if (depth >= maxDepth) return <div className=\"flex items-baseline gap-1.5\">{label && <span className=\"text-muted-foreground\">{label}:</span>}<span className=\"text-muted-foreground\">{`{${entries.length} keys}`}</span></div>;\n    return (\n      <div>\n        <button onClick={() => setCollapsed(!collapsed)} className=\"flex items-baseline gap-1.5 hover:text-foreground text-muted-foreground\">\n          <span className=\"text-[10px]\">{collapsed ? \"▸\" : \"▾\"}</span>\n          {label && <span>{label}:</span>}\n          <span className=\"text-muted-foreground text-[11px]\">{`{${entries.length}}`}</span>\n        </button>\n        {!collapsed && <div className=\"ml-4 border-l border-border/50 pl-3 mt-0.5 space-y-0.5\">{entries.map(([key, val]) => <JsonTree key={key} data={val} depth={depth + 1} maxDepth={maxDepth} label={key} />)}</div>}\n      </div>\n    );\n  }\n\n  return <span className=\"text-foreground\">{String(data)}</span>;\n}\n\nexport { JsonTree };\n"}}
